cards.title: Canvas frontend redesign — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified Canvas frontend redesign as the next E6 Canvas slice. Build the modified hybrid surface: Workbench-style project/file viewer, hybrid code/split/graph editor, context-command model, UE5-style node/pin visual language, hover-only types, compact getter capsules, embedded simple variables, graphite styling, and detail toggles. Source remains the only semantic truth.
cards.plan:
# Plan: Canvas modified hybrid UI

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-CANVAS1 outcome E with owner modifications.
- Existing E6 Canvas architecture and protocol from #352; do not introduce a graph asset or GUI-owned semantics.

Scope:
- Source/Canvas/html.rs, Source/Canvas/js.rs, Source/Canvas/*.rs protocol helpers, tests/canvas.rs, tests/web_dev.rs, docs/design/frontends/canvas/NOTES.md if behavior notes drift.
- Keep /canvas and /__jet_canvas routes source-backed.

Implementation steps:
1. Replace the old palette-first left surface with a persistent Workbench-style project/file viewer backed by /canvas/project and source ids. It must show workspace/package/file/function graph navigation and source-control/provenance facts where available.
2. Keep hybrid editor modes: Code, Split, Graph. Ensure selection, source-span jump, graph picker, replay/debug overlay, inspector, and project viewer all point at the same source-backed graph state.
3. Move commands out of the palette. Add command entrypoints through right-click, Ctrl+K, and drag-from-pin release menus. Drag-release menus must filter to compatible pin/node actions and show denied actions with exact why/fix where an existing diagnostic applies.
4. Polish node language: consistent shape/color families for exec/control/data/effect/fallible/reference pins; pin label is only the variable/field name; type appears in hover/inspector detail, not default label text.
5. Render variable/const getters as compact pure capsule/bubble nodes. Allow simple variables to embed inside field/value sockets for clean graphs, with an expand action back to a normal node.
6. Add detail toggles for types, diagnostics, effects, debug values, and package metadata so the default graph is streamlined graphite/gray rather than crowded.
7. Preserve keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior, NO_COLOR/non-visual fallbacks where terminal output is involved, and existing source transaction audit payloads.

Acceptance:
- A real Jet program opened through jet dev --target=web shows the modified hybrid Canvas UI at /canvas.
- Project/file viewer is not a command palette; commands are available through context surfaces and Ctrl+K.
- Getter capsules, embeddable variables, hover-only types, and compatible drag-from-pin menus are visible in browser proof.
- Existing graph/edit/source-control/debug features still work; no stub controls.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test canvas
- nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev
- Browser proof against /canvas with console clean except known host warnings.
- Full nix develop -c cargo test before closing the card, unless the owner explicitly accepts scoped proof with unrelated blockers logged.

log.text: Completed #356 Canvas frontend redesign modified hybrid slice. Implemented Workbench project/file viewer, Code/Split/Graph lens switch, context-command/Ctrl+K path, drag-pin refused E0204 teaching action, graphite detail toggles, hover-only type labels, semantic pin shapes, getter capsules, embedded simple variables, and workspace panels preserved from #352. Fixed closeout blockers: JetOS runtime package refs prefer first-party source before nix fallback; REPL notebook turn controls compile under deny(warnings); retired C marker diagnostics avoid live retired spellings. Proof: cargo test --test web_dev 4/4; cargo test --test canvas 42/42; cargo test --test jetpack 93/93 and full verify later 95/95; Playwright browser proof at http://localhost:8081/canvas had modified_hybrid contract, Split lens, detail toggles, getter capsules, embedded variables, nonblank canvas pixels, and zero console/page errors; nix develop -c scripts/agent/verify-full.sh completed green.
Planning update: moved to E6 epoch workOrder 21; plan written; phase set to ready.

Owner ratified D-FE-CANVAS1 as modified hybrid: Workbench-like project/file viewer replaces command palette; commands move to right-click, Ctrl+K, and drag-from-pin compatible menus; nodes get UE5-style semantic pin colors/shapes, hover-only types, compact getter capsules, embeddable variables, and graphite streamlined styling.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: build-cache normalization model — complete action identity owned by #419
cards.body: Prior cache-key contract is insufficient for imported/generated inputs, dependencies, targets, toolchains, policy, and observable source. E4-JP2 replaces it.
cards.plan: docs/plans/epoch-4/cas-build-cache.md

log.text: 2026-07-09 truth audit: reclassified from shipped capability to historical substrate; world-class milestone owns live completion.

Independently re-verified with EXTRA scrutiny (orchestrator) given this card touches the core compile pipeline (I2/I3): nix develop -c cargo build --workspace clean. Targeted tests confirmed exactly: tests/build_cache_normalization.rs 10/10 (whitespace/comment/rename/reorder/profile/version-sensitive + 4 extra discrimination guards), tests/build_cache_race.rs 1/1 (8-concurrent-process integrity check), crates/jet-foundation lib CanonicalAST:: 3/3.

Went beyond targeted tests given the risk here — manual end-to-end smoke of the real jet binary, not just the test suite: (1) nix develop -c ./target/debug/jet run hello.jet twice — first run showed the front-end effects summary, SECOND run (cache hit) correctly skipped it and still printed "hello, world" — confirms the short-circuit works for real, not just in unit tests. (2) edited the source (changed the printed string) and re-ran — correctly re-ran the full pipeline (front-end summary reappeared) and printed the NEW string, confirming edit/rename-sensitivity holds in practice. (3) jet build produced a working binary. (4) manually reproduced the exact race scenario from the plan: 3 concurrent jet run processes, all named main.jet in different directories with different content, launched simultaneously via nix develop's shell — each process's stdout correctly matched its own source with zero cross-contamination, confirming the cache-poisoning race fix holds under a real concurrent run, not just the automated 8-process regression test.

Full nix develop -c cargo test --workspace run to completion, exit code 0, zero FAILED/error lines. The I2/I3 soundness argument (cache hit = replay of a previously-validated exact whole-program AST + toolchain version + manifest bytes + profile, never a validation bypass; embed_file/embed_bytes correctly declines caching rather than risk external-state staleness) was reviewed and holds — no gap found on the orchestrator's independent read either. This was the last card in the owner's stated jetpack sequence for this session (#99 -> #176 -> #90 -> #3 -> #13 -> #179 -> #85). Closing: phase -> done.

E4 prep: plan expanded, zero ballots. Located real cache-poisoning race (CmdCompile.rs build(): rustc -o onto shared build/<stem> before store_cached copy — concurrent same-stem processes cross-contaminate) + fix (per-process temp path, atomic rename). D-BUILDNORM1=A ratified but cache_key hashes post-codegen Rust today, defeating incremental point — plan moves key to pre-sema canonical AST bytes + toolchain salt. Hash naming interlocked with #3 envelope.

Interlock noted 2026-07-02: D-JPK-CACHE1=A freezes cache-envelope fields (output hash, platform key, signature slot, provenance link) into the hangar/lock schema — normalization contract must carry them.
D-BUILDNORM1=A recorded and implementation plan attached. Advanced to ready.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.
Carded from Ideas.md sweep (L125). Full design ballot attached — owner decides proceed/direction.
[epoch restructure 2026-06-26] - → e5. Owner restructure: E3 = every major feature; E4 = Jai metaprogramming; E5 = jetpack/jetos; E6 = CI & documentation (deferred until features are set).

Found and reproduced a real cache-poisoning race in the current build cache (Source/BuildCache.rs + Source/CmdCompile.rs build()): cache_key() correctly SHA256-hashes the generated rust_code+profile, but the binary is compiled to a SHARED non-unique path (bin_path(file), e.g. build/main, keyed by source stem only) BEFORE store_cached(key, &bin) copies it into the content-addressed slot. Two jet processes compiling different sources with the same stem concurrently (e.g. two run/test invocations both producing build/main) can race: process A computes hash_A from its own rust_code, but by the time it calls store_cached, process B has already overwritten build/main with its binary, so hash_A permanently maps to B's binary in the shared ~/.cache/jet/build/ cache. Repro: many concurrent/rapid jet run invocations during Epoch 3 syntax-wave work; tests/cli.rs simple_exec_runs_without_a_manifest started failing (build/main.rs correct, cached binary under the correct hash printed wrong output). Fix for this card: compile to a unique per-process temp path before the content-addressed copy, so store_cached never races on a shared path. Cleared ~/.cache/jet/build/ as an immediate workaround; the poisoning will recur without the root-cause fix.

Implemented both parts.

PART 1 (race fix, section 0): BuildCache::store_cached (Source/BuildCache.rs) is now atomic -- writes to dir/bin.tmp.<pid> then fs::rename into dir/bin. CmdCompile.rs::build() no longer compiles onto the shared build/<stem> path directly: it now allocates a private per-process working dir build/.work.<bin_name>.<pid>/ holding the generated .rs, the rustc output binary, AND (discovered while writing the regression test) rustc's own crate-name-derived intermediate .rcgu.o object files, which also collided across concurrent same-stem builds and are now isolated the same way (rustc invoked with an explicit --crate-name pinned to the file stem, since the private .rs filename is not a valid crate identifier). store_cached is called against the private binary (safe: only races other processes computing the identical content-addressed key), then the private binary is fs::rename'd onto the shared build/<stem> display path (last-writer-wins on that convenience path is fine; it was never a content identity). Regression test tests/build_cache_race.rs::concurrent_distinct_sources_sharing_a_stem_do_not_poison_the_cache spawns 8 concurrent jet-run processes on distinct main.jet sources (different literal output) sharing a cwd and a JET_CACHE_DIR, then re-runs each source from its own isolated cwd against the same cache and asserts each cache hit returns exactly that source's own binary. This reproduces and pins the exact scenario the plan described (previously broke tests/cli.rs::simple_exec_runs_without_a_manifest under concurrent Epoch 3 work) and fails without the fix (verified: reproduced the crate-name and .rcgu.o collisions live before fixing them).

PART 2 (normalization, sections 1-3, D-BUILDNORM1=A): new crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs -- canonical_bytes(bundle: &ProgramBundle) serializes the WHOLE pre-sema bundle (entry file plus every module the loader resolved via imports, not just the entry) using each module's Debug-derived rendering of (pub_file, web_target_ceiling, html_path, imports, items) with a custom strip_spans() pass that removes every 'Span { start: N, end: M }' substring while leaving string/char literal contents (including ones that text-mimic a Span rendering) untouched -- verified by a dedicated unit test. Confirmed via recon (subagent read of AST.rs) that NO AST node stores comments or doc-comments (parser drops them entirely), so whitespace/comment insensitivity falls out for free from parsing + span-stripping; confirmed no HashMap/HashSet appears anywhere in the serialized item/import subtree (only in bundle-level resolved-state fields deliberately excluded, e.g. used_core/import_targets/web_partitions/dep_roots), so Debug rendering is deterministic. ast_cache_key(bundle, profile_tag, jet_version) = SHA256(canonical_bytes + 0 + profile_tag + 0 + jet_version) -- SHA-256 via the existing SHA256::sha256_hex, matching Lock::LockEnvelope::output_hash's algorithm (D-JPK-CACHE1=A interlock: same mechanism, not wired together yet, deferred to Epoch 6 as the plan directs). CanonicalAST re-exported through the full seam chain (jet-foundation -> jet-lexer/jet-parser -> jet-sema -> jet-codegen -> jet-driver -> Source/lib.rs) so Source/CmdCompile.rs can call jet::CanonicalAST::ast_cache_key.

CmdCompile.rs: new native_cache_key(file, profile_tag, mode_tag) loads the program pre-sema via Loader::load_entry_with_overlay (confirmed via recon this runs lex+parse+import-resolution only, no Sema::check_bundle), returns None (never cache) if any module's source contains embed_file/embed_bytes (external-file-bytes-not-in-AST gap, closed conservatively rather than papered over) or if the file fails to parse; folds in a SHA-256 of the enclosing pkg.jet's raw bytes (manifest_fingerprint) plus Manifest::COMPILER_VERSION as the toolchain/policy salt, so an effect-budget (D-EFFBUDGET1) tightening in pkg.jet or a compiler version bump invalidates old entries rather than being masked by an unchanged AST. jet run (mode_tag=='run', no --emit-rust) now short-circuits the ENTIRE front end on a cache hit -- sema and codegen never run, only the pre-sema parse inside the key computation -- and directly execs the cached binary. jet build deliberately keeps running its full front end even on a cache hit (only rustc is skipped, as before) because tests/pkg.rs asserts the unconditional per-build 'effects:' stderr summary and the capability summary on jet build stdout; confirmed via recon no jet-run test snapshots that stderr line, so the deeper run-side short-circuit is test-safe. jet test/doctest/bench/dev/debug builds keep their existing cache behavior (test gets its own mode_tag-scoped AST key so a test-harness binary can never be served for jet run; dev/doctest/bench/debug pass cache_key=None -- interactive/one-shot, still race-safe via build()'s private workdir). The old BuildCache::cache_key(source, profile_tag) signature is untouched and still used by BuildCache.rs's own unit tests; nothing else referenced it (checked via grep) so no call site needed updating.

SOUNDNESS ARGUMENT (I2/I3), verified end to end: a cache hit means (a) this exact whole-program AST -- entry plus every imported module, span/comment-stripped, identifier/order-sensitive -- (b) under this exact toolchain version and (c) this exact pkg.jet manifest bytes and (d) this exact build profile, was already parsed, type-checked, codegen'd, rustc-compiled to success, and (for jet run) executed at least once before. Skipping sema+codegen on a hit therefore replays a previously-validated result; it can never let unchecked code through, because storage only happens after a full successful pipeline run, and any input that could change sema's outcome for byte-identical AST bytes (imports -- closed by whole-bundle hashing; toolchain/codegen version -- closed by the version salt; manifest-driven policy like effect budgets -- closed by the manifest-fingerprint salt; embedded external file bytes -- closed by unconditionally declining to cache embed_file/embed_bytes programs) is either folded into the AST, folded into the salt, or excluded from caching outright. No gap found that required stopping; the one real external-state hazard (embed_file/embed_bytes) is handled by declining to cache rather than by hashing file bytes into the key, since Sema's own comptime_inputs tracking is only available post-sema and re-deriving it pre-sema was unnecessary when simple exclusion is sound and cheap.

TESTS: crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests (3: strip_spans_removes_span_renderings, strip_spans_keeps_span_lookalike_inside_string_literal, strip_spans_keeps_char_literal_with_quote); tests/build_cache_normalization.rs (10: whitespace_insensitive, comment_insensitive, rename_sensitive, reorder_sensitive, profile_sensitive, version_sensitive, operator_sensitive, literal_sensitive, string_literal_content_sensitive, stable_across_reloads -- covers all six named properties plus extra discrimination guards); tests/build_cache_race.rs (1: concurrent_distinct_sources_sharing_a_stem_do_not_poison_the_cache, 8 concurrent processes). All new tests green; smoke-verified manually outside the suite too (jet run cache-miss then cache-hit shows front-end skip via -v; jet build cache-hit still prints its effects/capabilities summary).

FULL SUITE: nix develop -c cargo test --no-fail-fast run twice independently, exit 0 both times, 70/70 test binaries 'test result: ok', 0 FAILED, 1058 individual tests passed total (a one-off engine_dispatch::json_flag_forwarded_verbatim_to_engine failure on an earlier concurrent run reproduced as a PATH/binary-copy flake under full-suite parallelism -- passed alone and on both full clean reruns, unrelated to this card's files).

EXIT CRITERIA: all checked -- race fixed (store_cached atomic + build() private workdir + rename-publish); key is pre-sema canonical AST, not post-codegen Rust, with sema/codegen skipped entirely on a jet-run hit; toolchain-version salt folded in; all six normalization properties tested and passing; naming/algorithm (SHA-256, output_hash-shaped) consistent with D-JPK-CACHE1's Lock::LockEnvelope::output_hash; full suite green including the new concurrent-process regression test.

Decision: D-JPK-GC1=B plus owner amendment is ratified. Verb is jet clean, not jet gc. Default stale_after is 30 days. Auto-GC is opportunistic and no-daemon. jet clean does GC plus optimize/dedup. Lockfile and generation reachable objects are never collected. No owner decision needed.

1. Add reachability scan in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Store.rs from .jet/lock package/toolchain entries and future jetos generation roots. Treat unknown legacy records as live until proven stale.

3. Replace current blunt Store::clean, which removes every entry. New clean computes live/stale/build-tmp classes, removes only unreferenced objects older than 30 days, sweeps orphan scratch, and keeps reachable roots.
4. Add optimize pass in jet clean: dedup or hardlink identical files inside Jet-owned hangar objects only; never mutate /nix/store outputs. Report GC bytes and optimize bytes separately.
5. Route build scratch under hangar tmp in Provider.rs / Recipe.rs / Store.rs. Clean on success and failure; U27 shell-on-fail is the later explicit preserve exception.
6. Add bounded opportunistic auto-GC after successful hangar-touching jetpack commands. No daemon, no root.
7. CLI/docs cleanup: keep jetpack clean and top-level jet clean dispatch; remove stale jet gc user text. Fix E2604 fix text in docs/spec/diagnostics.md and Source/Publish/Advisory.rs from jet gc --force to jet clean.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: platform intent/constant CI — real tier-1 execution owned by #398/#426/#433
cards.body: Historical platform model and narrow CI test do not prove native package-manager behavior or sandboxing on macOS/Windows.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-PLATFORM1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add one canonical platform model for jetpack targets: linux, macos, windows plus arch keys used by the hangar envelope. Keep jetos Linux-only and keep Nix bridge Linux/macOS-only.
2. Thread platform keys through realization, lock/envelope records, provider selection, adapter recipes, service supervision, secrets activation, trust prompts, and diagnostics so platform-specific behavior is explicit.
3. Audit path and process handling: executable suffixes, shebang avoidance, PATH separators, case sensitivity, symlink/hardlink fallback, file permissions, shell startup, service child-process cleanup, and config/cache directories.
4. Stand up CI matrix in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Keep the Nix-dependent bridge tests excluded or platform-gated on Windows; all native jetpack tests must run there.
5. Add portability fixtures for env modules, services, secrets, trust grants, adapters, hangar locks, and engine dispatch. Make every platform skip explicit and tied to D-JPK-PLATFORM1, not ad hoc.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Envelope,Store,Provider,Recipe,RefSpec,Services,Secrets,Trust,Shell,CLI}.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- platform fixtures under `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`; tests in `tests/{jetpack,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,pkg}.rs`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E12xx diagnostics for unsupported platform package, platform-specific bridge requirement, and non-portable adapter asset pattern if not already covered by U23.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, `docs/spec/roadmap.md`, and epoch-4 docs only where behavior changes.
- Add CI assertions that every new diagnostic has coverage and every platform lane runs the native jetpack suite.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test platform key parse/render and lock/envelope round trip.
2. Process tests for `jet env`, `jet dev`, `jet services`, `jet secrets`, and adapter realization using temp HOME/JET dirs on each OS.
3. Windows-specific tests: `.exe` command lookup, no shebang dependence, CRLF-safe scripts, backslash paths, config dir under user profile.
4. macOS tests: service cleanup, file-lock behavior, symlink/hardlink fallback.
5. Linux tests: existing Nix bridge lane plus native lane.

Gates:
- No Windows dependency on Nix bridge.
- No root or daemon assumption; aligns with U28.
- No `/tmp` scratch assumption; aligns with U22.
- Done only when all three CI lanes pass or a missing hosted runner is tracked as infrastructure with equivalent local proof logged.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: no-daemon policy/status — enforced sandbox owned by #398
cards.body: Historical runtime policy detects availability and warns; it never enters an OS jail. No strong-sandbox claim remains.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-NODAEMON1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add a jetpack runtime policy module that names the invariant in code: no resident daemon, no root requirement, file-lock coordination, and sandbox downgrade policy. Keep jetos activation as the only future sudo exception.
2. Audit all jetpack verbs for daemon/root assumptions: env/dev/services/secrets/image/push/run/add/update/clean/search/info/logs/explain. Replace any implicit global state with user-owned dirs and cross-process file locks.
3. Implement or centralize hangar file locks around realization, clean/optimize, service state, secrets store writes, and discovery index writes. Tests must prove concurrent invocations serialize without corrupting lock or hangar state.
4. Add sandbox capability detection: Linux unprivileged user namespaces when present; macOS/Windows best native isolation currently available; explicit warning when downgraded. Add `jet config sandbox require` path that turns fallback into a hard error.
5. Add CI assertions for no daemon and no root: no long-lived jetpack process after verbs exit, no sudo/system service install in jetpack paths, no setuid helper, no write outside user-owned roots.
6. Thread warning/error copy through normal diagnostics and JSON output so CI can detect sandbox fallback.

Likely touched files/modules:
- New `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/RuntimePolicy.rs`, `Sandbox.rs`, or `Locking.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Store,Services,Secrets,Trust,Shell,CLI,Provider,Recipe,WorkspaceLock}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Tests in `tests/{jetpack,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,pkg}.rs`; platform CI in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add L02xx warning for sandbox unavailable and E12xx for sandbox-required failure.
- Add E12xx for root-required invariant violation only if a runtime path can hit it; otherwise keep as CI assertion.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, CLI help for `jet config sandbox require`, and epoch-4 docs.
- Ensure `--json` carries sandbox status without ANSI or prose scraping.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test policy classification: jetpack verbs never require root; jetos switch is future allowlist only.
2. File-lock tests: spawn two realizes/clean/index writes against one temp hangar; assert one waits and final state parses.
3. Service tests: `jet services up/down/logs` leaves no resident jetpack supervisor after parent command exits; child services are project-local and down stops them.
4. Sandbox tests: fake capability detector for available/unavailable/require modes; assert warning vs hard error copy.
5. Path ownership tests: temp HOME/JET dirs; no writes to `/nix`, `/etc`, `/var`, global sockets, or `/tmp` except platform APIs outside jetpack control.
6. CI grep/assertion: no `sudo`, setuid helper, daemon socket, launchd/systemd install path in jetpack code or fixtures, excluding documented jetos activation code.

Gates:
- Any future design needing a daemon or privileged helper must raise a new owner decision before implementation.
- Fallback sandbox warning is loud and test-pinned; silent downgrade fails gate.
- Cross-platform behavior matches U25.
- Offline and hangar guarantees from U22/U29 remain intact under concurrent runs.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: fixture offline sweep — syscall/closure proof owned by #395/#433
cards.body: Historical offline fixture reuses fabricated provider output; it does not prove verified closure substitution or OS-level network denial.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-OFFLINE1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add one `NetworkMode` or `OfflineMode` value threaded through jetpack CLI dispatch, resolver, providers, adapters, cache substitution, script deps, service startup, and build runner. `--offline` must be parsed once and passed explicitly.
2. Classify verbs in code: realize-class (`env`, `dev`, `run`, `build`, `test`, `services`, package realization) versus network-class (`add`, `update`, `outdated` when refreshing, `publish`, cache push, registry sync). Network-class verbs refuse under `--offline` before doing work.
3. Teach providers and cache code to prove lock-satisfied realization from local hangar/lock only. If any object is missing and offline is set, emit one loud diagnostic naming the object/ref and the command that can fetch it later.
4. Add network-deny test harness: a fake provider/cache client that fails on network attempts plus, where practical, an env var or test hook that makes all network calls error. Prefer deterministic in-process denial over slow real network timeouts.
5. Sweep every current realize-class verb with a lock-satisfied fixture and network denied: env shell, dev with services, run package/tool, build, test, services up/health/logs, secrets activation, adapters/prebuilt/copy, images if present, discovery search/info.
6. Update docs/diagnostics and CLI help. Make `--offline` visible in completions/man output and stable JSON errors.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{CLI,Provider,RefSpec,Store,Recipe,ScriptDeps,ScriptLock,Services,Secrets,Trust,Image,Discovery}.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Fetch,Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,CLISpec,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Tests in `tests/{jetpack,pkg,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,cli}.rs`; fixtures under `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E1258 or next free E12xx for offline-forbids-network and reuse it for fetch misses and network-class refusal, with specific What/Why/Fix per context.
- Add diagnostics.md entry and process snapshot coverage; update `jet explain` coverage through existing test.
- Document verb classification in epoch-4 docs and user CLI help.
- Ensure no ANSI, spinner, or timeout text in offline errors.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test verb classification and `--offline` flag parsing through engine dispatch.
2. Lock-satisfied fixture: realize once online with fake local provider, then rerun all realize-class verbs with network denied and assert success.
3. Missing-object fixture: delete one hangar object, rerun `jet env --offline`, assert E12xx names object/ref and fix.
4. Network-class tests: `jet update --offline`, `jet add --offline`, publish/cache push under offline all refuse immediately with E12xx.
5. Adapter/build tests: locked prebuilt/copy/build recipe uses only local source and tool deps; locked `fetch(url, sha256:)` miss fails loudly under offline.
6. Service/secrets tests: offline `jet dev` starts from local hangar and decrypts local secret store without metadata refresh.
7. Discovery tests from #205: `jet search` and `jet info` read local index offline.

Gates:
- No network from realize-class verbs when lock is satisfied.
- No lazy metadata refresh, telemetry, update check, or cache probe in realize path under offline.
- Cache substitution miss falls back to local build only when not offline; under offline it errors without a fetch.
- U22 reachable-retention must keep current lock objects or this card cannot be marked done.
- Done requires golden sweep over every shipped realize-class verb, not a narrow provider unit test.

cards.title: Ship bootable jetos VM installer and install/reboot proof
cards.body: Owner acceptance: run a VM, install jetos, reboot into installed jetos, and prove it works as a real OS. Implement real QEMU boot media/disk image flow, installer environment, disk partition/format/install, bootloader or equivalent boot path, first boot into installed generation, guest-side verification, and reproducible harness. Done means a command produces media, QEMU boots it, installs to a virtual disk, reboots from that disk, then verifies packages, services, networking, generations, rollback, and proof artifacts inside the guest. The current jetos-installer-<host>.img proof text is not sufficient.

cards.title: Build functional jetos Studio prototype
cards.body: Owner acceptance: jetos Studio must be a usable source-backed GUI, not only a plan. Implement the ratified `jetos studio` surface as a first prototype over canonical Jet modules: load a project, select host, render guided control panels plus source/diff/provenance, edit real settings through source transactions, show plan/proof/rollback status, and refuse hidden GUI-owned semantic state. Done means a user can edit a jetos config in Studio, preview the exact Jet diff, save, reproject, and run the corresponding jetos check/build/proof flow.

cards.title: Canvas full-language and Core parity truth gate
cards.body: Audit verdict: Canvas is source-backed for shipped graph/edit operations, but it does not fully edit every language feature, does not browse all Core methods, and the Run path is a debug-overlay simulation. This card owns decisions needed to turn Canvas from strong prototype into truthful full-surface editor.
cards.plan:
# Plan: Canvas full-language/Core parity gate

Ratified inputs:
- D-CANVAS-PARITY1=C AST-derived semantic ratchet plus manual UX matrix.
- D-CANVAS-CORECATALOG1=C typed Core action catalog from sema-known Core facts.
- D-CANVAS-ACTIONAUTH1=C intent cards with expert authority drawers.
- D-CANVAS-CODELENS1=C explicit Edit Source mode using source transactions.
- D-CANVAS-PROOFLENS1=C proof/debug rail with stale-proof reasons.

Implementation slices:
1. Generate Canvas parity rows from AST item/stmt/expr/type forms and current Syntax decisions; fail if a new form lacks projection/edit/support status.
2. Replace generic expr collapse where feasible with specific nodes for current core language forms; unsupported forms get explicit Canvas diagnostic/action-disabled reasons.
3. Build Core catalog endpoint from sema/Core registry: functions, methods, docs, imports, effects, fallibility, receiver type, examples, authority.
4. Wire compatible action search from pins and graph context; insertion writes ordinary Jet source and rechecks/reprojects.
5. Replace simulated Run path with real checked command/action authority for run/check/build; mutation commands require confirmation and audit payload.
6. Add explicit Edit Source mode to Code lens: edit buffer, preview diff, format/check, write/reproject, conflict detection.
7. Add proof/debug rail tied to source revision, check/build/run/proof status and stale reasons.
8. Reconcile docs/spec/spec.md, docs/reference/canvas-protocol.md, and parity matrix.

Acceptance:
- Every shipped AST language form has Canvas parity status and tests or unsupported diagnostic.
- Core method browser exposes all current Core modules/methods with typed compatible insertion.
- Split/Edit Source changes text, formats/checks, reprojects graph, and can run real output.
- Canvas Run/Build authority is real, not a toast/simulation.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test canvas
- nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev
- Browser smoke: edit source and graph, insert Core method, run, stale proof rail updates.
- nix develop -c scripts/agent/verify-full.sh before done.

questions.text: What are the tradeoffs of option B instead of c? What is lost by going with b over c?
questions.answer: B vs C for refinements: B gives construction-checked refined values, literal checks, and flow narrowing. It does not prove arbitrary arithmetic or quantified facts. C can prove `a + b` remains PositiveInt, prove indexing is in bounds, eliminate runtime checks, and verify function postconditions over all inputs. What is lost with B: proof-preserving arithmetic, universal proofs, cross-function theorem reasoning, and check elision based on proofs. What B keeps: the most common product value, one constructor path, no solver dependency, deterministic compile times, and beginner-friendly diagnostics. Best sequencing: ship B as the surface and invariant discipline; let future C reuse those predicates if a solver/prover tier is owner-approved.

cards.title: jetos Studio frontend redesign — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified jetos Studio frontend redesign as an E7 Studio slice. Build a normal clean dashboard plus sidebar app over the existing source-backed Studio projection/edit service. Dashboard is opsboard-style; settings are sidebar categories; Changeset is a first-class sidebar page; page/category registration is extensible; projectional document is not the primary UI.
cards.plan:
# Plan: jetos Studio dashboard/sidebar UI

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-STUDIO1 outcome E with owner modifications.
- D-JOS-STUDIO-HOST1: local projection/edit service plus browser fallback; no Canvas coupling.
- #264 shipped source-backed Studio prototype; this card redesigns the actual Studio UI, not semantics.

Scope:
- crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/studio_projection.rs for installed app projection.
- crates/jetpack/src/CLI/bridge_os_studio.rs, crates/jetpack/src/CLI/studio_server.rs, crates/jetpack/src/CLI/studio_transactions.rs for served/edit flows if route data needs expansion.
- tests/jetpack.rs and focused Studio tests/fixtures.

Implementation steps:
1. Replace projectional-document-first layout with a normal app shell: top status/dashboard header, left sidebar, main page, persistent staged changes footer/tray.
2. Build dashboard landing page from real data.json/source/proof facts: hosts, selected host, generation ribbon, service health, alerts, monitoring summary, proof/rollback status, and last run status. Keep copy plain and operational.
3. Build sidebar categories: Dashboard, Settings, Monitoring, Services, Packages, Secrets, Generations, Changeset, Proof/Provenance. Back categories with an internal page registry so future Studio pages register title/id/source/data needs without redesign.
4. Move settings into category pages with ordinary controls. Each setting edit must stage a source transaction and show exact Jet diff before apply.
5. Make Changeset a first-class page: unified diff, impact ledger, generation delta, proof requirements, per-hunk include where supported, Build only, Build and switch, Discard.
6. Keep one apply path. Edits from settings, dashboard alerts, rollback actions, and changeset review all stage into the same changeset/apply gate.
7. Preserve source-backed guarantees: no hidden GUI semantic state, exact config.jet diff, provenance/proof visibility, browser/headless fallback, and deterministic review output.

Acceptance:
- jetos studio --serve opens the redesigned dashboard/sidebar UI.
- Dashboard is understandable at a glance; settings are in sidebar categories; Changeset is a sidebar page.
- A settings edit previews exact Jet diff, stages in Changeset, saves through the existing transaction service, reprojects, and can run check/plan/build/proof.
- Existing #264 tests still pass and new tests cover page registry, Changeset page, dashboard data rendering, and source transaction path.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack <focused Studio tests>
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack
- nix develop -c cargo build --bin jetos
- Browser/headless proof for served Studio page.
- Full nix develop -c cargo test before done unless unrelated blockers are logged and owner accepts scoped proof.

cards.title: JetOS replacement truth gate — import real NixOS and prove installed guest
cards.body: Owner asked whether JetOS can replace an entire NixOS flake/flake-parts/Home Manager config tomorrow. Audit verdict: no. Current JetOS has substantial generation/installer/VM proof plumbing, but no full semantic NixOS/HM importer and no real installed-guest acceptance proof for the owner config. This card owns the decisions and implementation gates to make that claim true.
cards.plan:
# Plan: JetOS real NixOS replacement gate

Ratified inputs:
- D-JOS-NIXIMPORT1=C semantic NixOS/flake-parts/Home Manager importer with audited facts-only fallback.
- D-JOS-REALGUEST1=C real installed-guest proof required for replacement claims; fake QEMU only tests plumbing.
- D-JOS-DESKTOPPROOF1=C live desktop/session/app/user-home proof, not file presence.
- D-JOS-IMAGEPROOF1=C image variants are built only when bootable and smoke-proved; placeholders are staged.
- D-JOS-FIRSTBOOT1=D Studio first-boot control center with Canvas deep-link.

Implementation slices:
1. Add NixOS import IR and CLI: jet os import <flake-or-dir> --host <name> [--user <name>] [--write] [--facts-only]. Parse/evaluate available Nix facts through structured JSON, not text scraping. Generate JetOS modules for system, users, packages, services, files, secrets, overlays, specialisations, Home Manager; emit exact omissions.
2. Add fixture coverage for flake.nix, flake-parts, nixosModules, home-manager.users, overlays, mkDefault/mkForce, disabledModules, specialisations, secrets, system packages, user packages.
3. Harden jet os lift: either route to import/facts-only or downgrade wording so it cannot look like replacement import.
4. Add real-QEMU proof tier distinct from fake-tool unit tests. Fake QEMU tests remain plumbing; real acceptance rejects fake tool paths and requires guest-bound serial/display/user/app/service artifacts.
5. Upgrade desktop proof from file/script presence to live guest assertions for display manager/session, terminal fallback, Studio app, user home, browser fallback, package/service/network facts.
6. Upgrade image variants: no sparse marker says built; raw/sd/qcow only built after real artifact + smoke proof.
7. First boot: generated system launches Studio control center and proves source/proof/rollback/update health path; Canvas opens from source spans only.
8. Update docs/spec/roadmap and tests so replacement claims require import+real guest tier.

Acceptance:
- Owner-style NixOS flake/flake-parts/Home Manager fixture imports to JetOS source with zero silent omissions.
- Generated JetOS config builds offline where fixtures provide packages, and omissions are explicit otherwise.
- Real VM tier command installs, reboots, logs in, opens Studio, proves desktop/services/packages/network/home/rollback from installed disk.
- Fake-QEMU tests cannot close #363 acceptance.

cards.body:
Plan: docs/plans/agent-durability.md W1. CI currently runs 6 of ~90 test targets; golden/fuzz self-skip when rustc is missing, so a green run can be vacuous; one step still calls the retired tools/Tower path.

Scope: corpus-wide lossless check — parse(fmt(src)) token-stream-equal parse(src) for every example and every tests/ui fixture. One test closes the class; new syntax is covered automatically with no per-feature test to remember.

Focused corpus test failed on examples/features/basics/string_view.jet at ordered token 80: before Ident("Bench"), after LParen. cards.title: durability: tower enforcement gates (W5)
cards.body:
Plan: docs/plans/agent-durability.md W5. Today any phase jump is legal (store.mjs:224-243, triage-to-done included), decision add validates only the title, ratify outcome is unchecked against option keys, agents can write frozen/owner-lane cards, card delete cascades away ratified decisions, verdicts get mis-filed as log notes.

Scope (strictness per D-TWRGUARD1): card.checklist[] + done-gate; card.gates field required before leaving planning (BALLOT FIRST becomes structural); ballot-ready validation on decision add with --draft escape; tower verdict command minting an owner verdict as a ratified decision + card flip; ratify outcome must match an option key; owner-attribution rules for ratify/activate; non-assignee write guard; frozen/owner-lane write guard; no cascade-delete of ratified decisions; blockedBy accepts decision ids; release of a building card requires --handoff; ratify hook auto-appends syntax-decision chores (Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions.md log, jet devtools grammars, re-bless) to the card checklist.

Exit: each guard has a Tower test proving refusal/acceptance; existing board data migrates clean; skills docs updated to match.
cards.plan:
D-TWRGUARD1=C ratified — agent-hard, owner-soft. Criteria/checklist data model + done-gate + acceptance ballots are OWNED BY #463 (D-TWR-CRIT1=C); this card builds the rest of the guard family on top. All gates apply only when --by ≠ owner; owner writes bypass everything; every bypassing owner-quote is event-logged. Steps:
1. store.mjs guard layer (single chokepoint in mutate path): (a) ballot-ready validation on decision add — gist/story/inWild/options[].code/rec required, --draft flag exempts and keeps it out of the owner queue; (b) ratify/activate rejected for agents unless --quote "owner's words" given (recorded in event log); (c) no agent writes to frozen or owner-lane cards; (d) release of a building card requires --handoff note; (e) card delete refuses to cascade away ratified decisions (they retire to history instead once #461 lands; until then delete is refused outright); (f) ratify outcome must match an option key; (g) blockedBy accepts decision ids.
2. tower verdict '#N' --outcome "..." --by owner — mints an owner verdict as a ratified decision on the card and flips the card, so verdicts stop landing in logs (owner rule).
3. Ratify hook: ratifying a syntax-group decision auto-appends the standard chores (Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions.md log, jet devtools grammars, re-bless) to the card's criteria (#463 model).
4. Errors: E_GATE_* family, each with an actionable message naming the missing thing.
5. Tests: one refusal + one acceptance test per gate; owner-bypass test per gate; migration clean on live-shaped fixture.
6. Docs: Tower/AGENTS.md gate table; tower + tower-ballot skills.
Exit: every gate has paired refusal/acceptance tests; live board migrates clean; skills updated; suite green.

cards.title: Tower: archive finished board history
cards.body: tower.json is 4.2MB; 68% is closed history (496 ratified decisions = 1.7MB, 305 done cards = 1.1MB). Every write rewrites + backs up the full file (backups/ 82MB), streams it to the phone, and lands it in git (356 versions). Ballot D-TWR-ARCHIVE1 decides where finished history lives. Messages data (103KB) already removed with the messaging feature.
cards.plan:
D-TWR-ARCHIVE1=B ratified (auto-retire split live/history) MODIFIED by owner comment: keep a walk-back buffer before anything retires, and done must be strictly tested (that half lands via #463/#458). Steps:
1. store.mjs — .tower/history.json append-only ledger {decisions[], cards[], events[], each with retiredAt}. Written under the same cross-process lock; committed to git.
2. Retire policy WITH BUFFER (owner comment): on every write, retire (a) decisions status=ratified whose ratifiedAt is older than config retireAfterDays (default 3) — inside the window they stay in tower.json, show in the UI 'recently decided' strip, and tower decision reopen works one-step; (b) cards phase=done older than the same buffer AND passing the #463 done-gate rules; their questions ride along; (c) events beyond the newest 500.
3. Walk-back UX: Now view gets a collapsed 'Recently decided (N) — reversible for X days' strip listing buffered ratifications with one-tap Reopen. Reopen pulls it back to open and reverts the card advance.
4. Merged reads: findCard/decision show/card show fall through to history transparently; tower archive restore <id> moves an item back to live (reopen for ratified decisions). Board Done counts read a per-epoch summary; full done lists lazy-load via GET /api/history?epoch=.
5. CLI: tower archive status|show <id>|restore <id>. First write after upgrade migrates the existing 496 ratified decisions + 305 done cards (all outside any buffer) → tower.json ~0.5MB.
6. Tests: buffer respected (nothing retires early), reopen-from-buffer, retire-after-buffer, merged reads, restore, migration on a live-shaped fixture, backups shrink.
7. Docs: Tower README/AGENTS.md + tower-setup skill (retireAfterDays).
Exit: tower.json ≤ ~0.6MB after migration; every retired item still reachable by id; a ratification can be walked back within the buffer from phone UI; suite green.

log.text: verified by orchestrator: suite 79/79 (independent rerun); migration smoke on live-board copy: 4.2M -> 1.8M live + 2.4M history; archive status/show/restore + archived-read fallback + recentlyDecided strip working. Live retire fires on this write. Closing.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.process — subprocess parity with Python subprocess/Go os/exec
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Python subprocess flexibility, Go os/exec explicitness, duct-style pipelines. Current: run([cmd]) capturing everything + exit(code) only.

Gaps: streaming stdin write and incremental stdout/stderr read while the child runs; env control (set, remove, clear-then-set); working-directory control; timeout with kill; send signals (terminate/kill/interrupt); detached spawn; exit status detail (signal vs code); pipelines (child stdout → child stdin) without a shell; safe argv-only execution documented (no shell interpolation footgun — safe by default); output size limits; inherit-vs-capture per stream.

Done means: a build-tool-shaped example (spawn, stream logs live, timeout, propagate exit) ships with golden output. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan:
Acceptance: core.process must cover real build-tool and agent-operation workflows without shell strings: safe argv-only execution by default, streaming logs, exact exit status, env/cwd control, timeouts, signals, detached children, output limits, and shell-free pipelines.

Current facts found during plan pass:
- docs/reference/core-library.md documents only process.exit(code) and process.run([String]) -> ProcessResult ? IOError.
- ProcessResult currently has code/output/errors only.
- Sema/codegen know core.process exit/run only; effects classify core.process as Exec.
- Existing taint tests treat process.run as an Exec sink; any expanded surface must keep that policy coverage.

Gate queued:
- D-PROCESS1: exact process spawning/pipeline surface.

Implementation plan after gate clears:
1. Baseline tests: pin current process.run/exit behavior and taint Exec-sink coverage before expanding.
2. Data model: add ProcessSpec, Child, ExitStatus, StreamMode, ProcessPipe/Pipeline types per ratified surface. Keep argv lists canonical; no shell-string helper unless separately ratified.
3. Sema/effects: register all new calls in CheckerCoreLib known-items, mark Exec effects, preserve taint sink checks on every execution path, and type-check stream/stdin/stdout modes.
4. Runtime/codegen: implement through TIR/prelude only; no codegen checks. Use std::process Command internally; map OS errors into IOError and child outcomes into ExitStatus without exposing Rust/stdout internals.
5. Safety defaults: bounded capture default or explicit output_limit, no inherited env mutation, timeout kill semantics documented, process handles RAII-clean where possible, and interrupt/terminate/kill behavior platform-pinned.
6. Examples/goldens: build_runner.jet streams stdout, sets cwd/env, times out a child, pipelines two argv commands, propagates exit. Keep fixture commands cross-platform or test-gated.
7. Docs: update docs/reference/core-library.md, docs/spec/spec.md effects table, syntax-decisions D-PROCESS1 entry, and stdlib ledger (#310 if present).
8. Verification: targeted process/taint/golden tests, cargo build, hello smoke, process example smoke, final nix develop -c cargo test before close.

Devil-pass hardening:
- No shell string default; argv-only is the safe path.
- No silent output buffering footgun; streaming and capture limits are explicit.
- No second process model; process.run lowers to ProcessSpec.run.
- No raw OS status leaks; ExitStatus is typed and portable.

cards.plan:
# Plan: jet dev server pinned dashboard + overlay

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-DEVSRV1 outcome D with owner modification: keep a nicely formatted pinned terminal dashboard header.

Scope:
- Source/CmdDevWeb.rs for dev web server output and injected browser overlay/status strip.
- tests/web_dev.rs and any dev-server CLI transcript tests.

Implementation steps:
1. Add terminal dashboard header for TTY: status, URL/port, watched target, client count, last build time, current build/error state. Header remains pinned while logs scroll below.
2. Keep one shared poll/status source for browser strip and terminal header so ready/building/error/offline/client count cannot drift.
3. Browser corner strip mirrors status; on error it expands to full overlay with verbatim diagnostic frame over last-good build.
4. Terminal verbose mode/request log prints under the same header. Errors erase/settle any live region before printing diagnostics.
5. Non-TTY output degrades to append-only deterministic status lines. NO_COLOR uses words instead of color-only state.
6. Preserve current dev server routes, last-good-build behavior, Canvas route, and reload/poll protocol.

Acceptance:
- jet dev <file> --target=web shows pinned dashboard header in TTY.
- Browser strip and terminal header report identical state and client count.
- Compile error shows full browser overlay and terminal diagnostic; clean rebuild clears both.
- Request/rebuild logs appear below the header.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev
- Add/update focused tests for status payload, overlay injection, terminal formatting fallback, and non-TTY output.
- Browser smoke: launch jet dev, load app and /canvas if relevant, trigger compile error, verify overlay clears after fix.

cards.title: jet CLI: shrink top-level verb surface — namespace the long tail
cards.body: jet's own top-level verb count (excluding the ~14 verbs that pure-forward to the jetpack engine via EngineDispatch) is ~45: help, doctor, completions, devtools, man, version, upgrade, explain, fmt, fetch, update, toolchain, init, lock, gc, publish, keygen, key backup, yank, vendor, schema, semindex, dossier, impact, graph/query/explain-build, codemod, expand, audit, sbom, bind, repl, dev, serve, debug, store verify/rollback/generations, eval, run, build, test, check, fix, new, emit, bench, lint, add, remove. Registry/signing ops (publish, keygen, key, yank, vendor — Source/CmdSupply.rs) and introspection ops (semindex, dossier, impact, graph, query, codemod, expand, audit, sbom) live directly in the Source/ root crate, not crates/jetpack — a verb-ownership question #367/D-PRODUCT-SPLIT1 (binary/crate ownership) did not address. jet ? (D-FE-HELP1, card #360) solves DISCOVERY of this surface with a palette; it does not address whether the surface itself should be narrower/grouped, matching the git porcelain/plumbing lesson (git ships ~30+ subcommands but only ~17 are used daily) and the uv/bun-era trend toward one lean unified CLI. This is a distinct owner-facing IA decision, separate from #360's UI archetype and #367's binary-ownership split.

Data.Text(e.addr) — any core-call argument reading a FIELD of a bare/read binding — passes sema but the generated Rust moves out of a shared reference and rustc rejects with E0507 (exit 101 ICE banner). Reproduces with a plain fn f(e: Email) { Data.Text(e.addr) }, independent of serde. Root: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/arg_expect.rs expect_core_arg_impl flags borrowed IDENTS for implicit-clone/E0209 but not field-path reads. Correct fix per D-MEM1/S2 (no silent clone): extend the borrowed-place detection to field paths so sema demands copy, with ui snapshot; workaround today is user-written copy e.field. Sema-accepted → rustc-rejected = I2 P0.

log.text: Parent integrated verification: hostile UI 1/1, explicit-copy and owned-slice real compile/run 1/1, ICE/rustc agreement 8/8 green. Independent Sol accepted f25f0a4b; criteria 1-4 verified. Closed P0 I2 field/index ownership gap.

[review] ACCEPT through f25f0a4b. Borrowed root rejection total and renderer-independent; exact/generic diagnostics truthful; Slice excluded; explicit-copy and I2 proofs green (UI 1, corelib 1, bare UI 1, ICE 8).

P0 architecture fix f25f0a4b makes rejection total after borrowed ownership-root classification. Renderer success keeps exact path; renderer failure now emits truthful generic E0209 over full consumed-expression span with non-lying copy-prefix guidance. Hostile if-valued index snapshot and explicit-copy real compile/run green.

Diagnostic-truth fix b6e3f556 removes root-name fallback and renders valid computed Int index forms including calls, methods, unary, parentheses, binary, fields, and nested indexes. Hostile pick() and -(-i) snapshots pin exact full paths/copy fixes; explicit-copy real compile/run green.

Final semantic review fix at 6861c386: Index ownership root detection is independent of computed-index rendering; i + 1 path gets exact E0209/full span/copy fix. Slice excluded because TIR creates an owned inclusive-copy value. UI and real compile/run prove computed explicit copy plus consuming owned List<Data> slice without false E0209.

P1 review fix landed at 5223b2eb: ownership-place walker now traverses Index and Slice bases while rejecting call/method temporaries; indexed hostile UI pins exact e.items[0].text span and copy fix; explicit indexed copy real compile/run green. Re-review required.

Builder complete at 1dbb9448. Failing-first repro was no errors; sema-only root-aware field-place E0209 fix landed. Targeted UI, bare-ident regression, explicit-copy real compile/run, and rustc agreement green. Independent review required; no full suite run.
Selected as final genuine low-hanging sidequest after epoch sweeps. Narrow P0 I2 sema ownership fix; existing E0209, no new syntax/diagnostic.

cards.title: Sema soundness audit: adversarial review + fuzz corpus expansion
cards.body:
jet-sema (~40k lines) owns all checking (I3); a soundness hole means unsound generated Rust reaches users silently — the worst bug class in the project (I1/I2). #185 (done) swept reachable ICEs and rustc leaks; this card hunts the other two classes: accepts-invalid (sema approves a program it must reject) and miscompiles (approved program computes the wrong thing).

Audit surface, in priority order:
1. Ownership/move/borrow proofs, including the tier-2 view/ref rules (E2-M5) and RAII cleanup (S63).
2. Sendability proofs for tasks/channels (E2-M1) — data-race freedom claims.
3. #Unsafe gate containment (D-LL1): generated `unsafe` appears only inside user-written gates; safe Jet emits none (tests/golden.rs enforces — extend it).
4. Generics + trait resolution: associated types, error conversion for `?`, trait delegation (S62), argument labels/defaults (S61).
5. Comptime/@Pure evaluation boundary (M9.5, E2-M16) — comptime results must agree with runtime semantics.
6. Newer surface: fan-out `f.[…]` (S75), fixed-size lists `[T#N]` (S76), refinements (D-REFINE1 when landed).

Method: adversarial review pass per area → each suspected hole becomes a tests/ui fixture or golden test BEFORE the fix; extend tests/fuzz_sema.rs with generative/mutation strategies over the ratified grammar; use the interpreter-vs-compiled differential battery (I2, jet dev parity) as a miscompile oracle — divergence is always a bug in one side.

Done means: audit notes committed under docs/ (findings, per-area verdict, corpus description); every confirmed hole has a failing test then a fix, all suite green; fuzz corpus + runner wired so #211 CI can execute it in budget; no invariant bent. No owner gates expected — if a finding requires a semantics change visible to users, ballot it before fixing.
cards.plan: Order: (1) read docs/spec/architecture.md R1–R12 + spec.md sections per area; (2) per audit area, spawn adversarial review (opus-tier reasoning) over the relevant sema modules — CheckerCore.rs, CheckerInfer/, CheckerCoreLib.rs, Bundle.rs; (3) write attack programs as tests/ui fixtures — expect reject; write miscompile candidates as differential fixtures — expect byte-identical interpreter/compiled output; (4) extend tests/fuzz_sema.rs: grammar-directed generation from crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs so the fuzzer only speaks ratified syntax; (5) fix confirmed holes smallest-first, full suite between fixes; (6) audit notes + corpus docs; full nix develop -c cargo test green at close.

cards.title: jetpack/jetos CLI output redesign — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified hybrid jetpack/jetos CLI output as an E4 output substrate slice. Keep colored + - ~ plan symbols, support both -y and --yes, and add nh-style dependency chain/progress visualization for long downloads/builds/realization where appropriate. Jetos uses the same output substrate later.
cards.plan:
# Plan: jetpack/jetos hybrid CLI output

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-CLI1 outcome D with owner modifications: keep colored + - ~; both -y and --yes; add nh-style dependency chain/graph visualization for long builds/downloads.

Scope:
- crates/jetpack/src/Output.rs, crates/jetpack/src/CLI/*.rs command call sites, crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/commands.rs and generation/proof call sites that already share Theme/Output.
- tests/jetpack.rs, CLI usage tests, fixture stderr/stdout snapshots where output is pinned.

Implementation steps:
1. Extend the shared Theme/Output layer with consequence-scaled rendering: quiet ledger, pinned live region for long work, plan gate for mutations, deterministic plain fallback.
2. Preserve colored +, -, ~ for plan diffs; NO_COLOR replaces color with stable text markers while keeping symbols readable.
3. Normalize confirmation bypass so -y and --yes are accepted everywhere the mutation confirmation gate appears. Non-TTY mutation without yes prints plan and exits without applying.
4. Add dependency-chain progress model for long realization/build phases: downloads, builds, cached/reused nodes, current edge, counts, size/elapsed where known. Render as a pinned graph/chain in TTY; append ledger lines in non-TTY.
5. Wire jetpack add/build/env/gc and jetos plan/build/switch/proof through the same output primitives where they already share command execution paths.
6. Erase live regions before diagnostics; diagnostics remain verbatim.
7. Keep JSON output schemas untouched unless a separate schema version decision is raised.

Acceptance:
- Trivial commands stay quiet.
- Long build/download commands show useful dependency-chain progress in TTY.
- Mutations show a plan with + - ~ and require confirmation unless -y/--yes.
- Non-TTY output is deterministic and non-interactive.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack <focused CLI output tests>
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack
- Add transcript/snapshot coverage for + - ~, -y, --yes, non-TTY no-hang, NO_COLOR, and dependency-chain fallback.
- Full nix develop -c cargo test before done.

cards.title: durability: JIT lowering doc pass + TIR exhaustive dispatch (W4)
cards.body:
Plan: docs/plans/agent-durability.md W4. jet-jit lower_ctx.rs has 22 comment lines per 1866 (hairiest logic, pure reverse-engineering); the TIR quadruple (subset gate / emit / lower / interpreter) is memory-coupled — a missed arm is a runtime ICE, and wildcard _ arms hide gaps.

Scope: doc-comment pass mapping each lowering region to its TIR variant and the R12 parity contract; restructure the four TIR consumers to exhaustive match on the TIR enum so a new variant breaks the build in every consumer; distinguish honest named-unsupported fallthroughs from lazy wildcards.

Exit: no bare _ arms over TIR variants in the four consumers (pinned by grep test or enum exhaustiveness); adding a dummy variant breaks all four compilations (demonstrated, then reverted).

log.text: Closed after corrected independent review and parent integrated proof: runtime boundary 1/1 exact E3410; TIR exhaustiveness 7/7. First vacuous skip fix was rejected and replaced with real Cranelift execution without AOT masking.

Lean closure lane started in approved worktree. Root cause reproduced: 15ca83b5 removed io/stdin_filter from expected E3410 boundary while JIT still intentionally rejects ambient Tier-2 stdin; restoring truthful boundary and focused regression, not faking execution.

REOPENED by independent exact rerun: nix develop -c cargo test --test dev dev_default_matches_compiled_binary -- --exact --nocapture fails current HEAD after 51.48s. Actual boundary set includes io/stdin_filter E3410; expected set omits it. Not cache poisoning. Prior 43/43 close claim is not reproducible. Fix JIT support or restore exact expected boundary, then independent rerun before done.

Fallout fixed by parent: jit_gaps if-let message (#455), dev boundary list stdin_filter now runs under dev==AOT (#291 parity win), formatter \u-escape corruption exposed by #436 fixture, capability digest re-pin.

cards.plan:
# Plan: jet env hybrid prompt

Ratified inputs:

- tests/jetpack.rs, tests/env_dev_trust.rs, and focused shell rc tests.

Implementation steps:
1. Make default prompt include environment label and compact current path in bash, zsh, and fish. Keep current dev-shell branding unmistakable.
2. Add adaptive receipt/status behavior where feasible in shell rc: transient command receipt, running marker for Jet-owned commands, failure next-action line without restating diagnostics.
3. Implement ^G glance for build/test/env status if supported by the generated shell rc; unsupported shells get a documented no-op fallback rather than broken control sequences.
4. Implement optional always-on strip exactly as the ratified D-FE-PROMPT-STRIP1 config says.
5. Respect NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR and non-TTY shell startup. No powerline-only glyph dependency; words carry the state.
6. Keep env source truth in env.jet/module eval; no hidden prompt database.

Acceptance:
- Entering jet env in bash/zsh/fish shows env name and partial path by default.
- NO_COLOR renders readable words without ANSI reliance.
- Optional strip can be enabled by the ratified config and shows the same status words as ^G.
- Existing trust/env behavior and foreign flake fallback remain unchanged.

questions.text: I want to use add but we need to have two methods available. One that adds and overwrites on collision and one that does not overwrite on collision. Propose updated methods so experts can control whether they want to have values be updated by default if key already exists or if they want to add unique, only if the key is new
questions.answer: Ballot updated to your direction. Option A (rec) is now: one verb family — add(key, value) -> T? upserts and returns the displaced old value (None = the key was fresh), so the default path already gives experts collision visibility for free; add_new(key, value) -> Bool stores only if the key is absent and returns false with the existing value untouched — the race-safe claim in one call. Element containers: add(value) -> Bool. insert and put both die; scores[name] = v index-write stays the literal upsert. Precedents: Rust insert returning Option<old>, .NET indexer + TryAdd.

cards.title: dev suite parallel flake: core.perf fidelity signal is a process-global static
cards.body: Under full parallel cargo test --test dev, core.perf fidelity signal races across JIT-resident test threads: cranelift_three_way_differential_battery diverges on tooling/fidelity and 3+ sibling tests sharing dev_diff_lock cascade with PoisonError. Green standalone/single-threaded. Architectural: the signal needs per-instance or thread-scoped state (or the battery needs an isolation harness). Observed across waves on card 521 (2026-07-12/13).

log.text: Fidelity signal statics converted to thread_local (c06b735f): jit runtime_host + comptime Methods; AOT static untouched (per-process naturally). dev target 57/57 at default parallelism twice + serialized once; golden/effects clean. 3/3 criteria met+verified (jet-verify-close3).

Root cause: core.perf fidelity signal was process-global (static AtomicU32) in both in-process tiers -- jet-jit resident JIT (runtime_host.rs JIT_PERF_FIDELITY) and jet-comptime interpreter/REPL (Methods.rs PERF_FIDELITY) -- shared by every cargo-test thread in the one test binary process. AOT tier's own static (jet-codegen Prelude/Core.rs) is correctly untouched: each AOT run is a separate OS process already. Fix: both in-process statics -> thread_local Cell<u32> (not per-JitRuntime-instance: resident_jit_fidelity_matches_runtime_contract's ?-early-return design needs fidelity to survive a full try_compile_bundle teardown+fresh_runtime restart on the SAME thread, ruling out scoping to JitRuntime/Interp). thread_local isolates concurrent test threads (fixes the race + PoisonError cascade via dev_diff_lock) while preserving same-thread persistence across restarts/hot-swaps/REPL turns. Evidence: cargo test --test dev default-parallel 3 consecutive clean runs (55/55, excluding 2 pre-existing tests that fail identically on unmodified master, parallel or solo: jit_coverage_audit/jit_try_compile_manifest_matches, a JIT-gap-manifest drift unrelated to this bug); --test-threads=1 55/55; cranelift_three_way_differential_battery + resident_jit_fidelity_matches_runtime_contract + interpreter_matches_compiled_binary + dev_default_matches_compiled_binary all green standalone; golden 3/3, effects 48/48; jet run smoke ok. cards.title: JIT tier-1a: Cranelift JIT (dev-loop hot-reload) — c139
cards.body: Ideas.md: add Cranelift JIT, later own bytecode/native JIT. Was Tower c139 (ready); c140/c141 (own bytecode VM / own native JIT) are separate frozen v2 cards. Jet is AOT-compiled; the Cranelift JIT is the optional hot-reload dev accelerator (tier-1 over interpreter tier-0), not how the language runs. Accepted work. Bundle-risk: Cranelift JIT vs later custom tiers differ. Owner requirement (2026-06-30): JIT and `jet run` must be functionally identical on every program the AOT path covers; native stays the performance tier. `jit_covers` must converge on `tir_covers`, not fall back to the E2201 interpreter for tasks/channels/Core.
cards.plan: JIT/AOT parity by construction. Canonical plan: docs/plans/epoch-3/jit-aot-parity.md. Orchestration: implementation agent must first read .agents/prompts/OrchestrationPrompt.md and run as that orchestrator. Owner direction 2026-07-06: Jet wins two fronts. AOT targets C/C++/Rust/Go/Zig/Odin territory with optimized native binaries and expert control; JIT/dev targets JS/TS/Python/data-analysis/web-dev loops with rapid design/test/refine. Every AOT-runnable program must run under jet dev in some backend path with identical stdout/stderr/exit/diagnostics/panics/side effects. Native JIT lowering is preferred for speed; transparent shared-runtime/platform/AOT-subprocess fallback is valid when resident JIT hosting is unsafe or incomplete. User never owns backend gaps. No parity ballots remain. Exit: dev_default_matches_compiled_binary covers stdout+stderr+exit for every example, gap manifest contains only transparent internal fallback reasons, no jit_covers whitelist remains, R12 documents two consumers/one IR, full suite + jet-verify green.

cards.title: Derive output mechanism (emit source fragments re-entering lexer/parser/sema) — D-METADERIVE1
cards.body: Ideas.md: user derives emit source fragments that re-enter lexer/parser/sema. Open decision D-METADERIVE1 under c155; D-CTCODEGEN1 already ratifies the architecture rule.
cards.plan: D-METADERIVE1=A: implement user derive output as source fragments. Steps: (1) parser for `derive Trait for T { ... }`; (2) sema registers derive providers and enforces local-only orphan rule (trait or type local); (3) derive body runs at comptime with `T.reflect()` and `$name` splices; (4) emitted Jet text re-enters lexer/parser/sema per R11/D-CTCODEGEN1, never injects pre-parsed AST; (5) diagnostics for generated-fragment failure pin at the user `#[Trait]` trigger with optional generated context; (6) examples and goldens for a custom derive; (7) follow-up card for emit-template quoting, not a blocker.

questions.text: Give me the tradeoffs, limitations, and benefits that we would get from having both A & B as the selected option
questions.answer: Having both A ($ splice source fragments) and B (typed AST builder API) simultaneously: BENEFITS — (1) $ splice covers quick, copy-modify derives (easy to read, errors in Jet source terms); (2) AST builder covers programmatic generation without string concatenation or escaping; (3) users can pick the right tool for their derive's complexity. LIMITATIONS — (1) I8 violation: two mechanisms for the same semantic job (emitting derive output). Real codebases will use both; code review becomes harder. (2) Stabilization cost: every new language construct must be handled in BOTH the string parser path (A) and the AST builder (B), forever. Miss one and the two systems diverge. (3) The AST builder is effectively a complete typed representation of every Jet syntax node — it's a large, complex API that must version-lock to the compiler's internal representation. (4) Error quality differs: $ splice errors point at generated Jet code (readable by derive users); AST builder errors point at builder call sites in Rust (opaque). VERDICT: the costs outweigh the benefits. Teams will converge on one; having both means maintaining two. Option A ($ splice) handles all cases — complex programmatic generation is just string building, which is what Rust proc macros do. The AST builder's type-safety advantage is real but doesn't justify doubling the API surface. Recommend ratifying A and documenting patterns for complex derives (template helpers, string builders).

# Plan: hybrid REPL with notebook controls

Ratified inputs:

- Interactive REPL shows addressable turns with notebook controls.

cards.title: Concurrency runtime push: Go-scale M:N tasks + structured combinators
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 concurrency push. Merges #36 (Verse-style race/all/any/select combinators) and #103 (try-both / keep-the-winner) into the Go-scale M:N runtime card. Prior foundations already shipped: #102 taskgroup scope, #101 task-handle coroutine-grade controls, #112 deadline propagation. This card now owns the remaining runtime-quality push: native OS parking, structured combinator completion, select integration, cancellation correctness, observability, and scale/perf proof. No @async/await or function coloring; ordinary Jet code parks at wait/IO points under the task/channel/taskgroup model.
cards.plan:
Canonical concurrency implementation plan (D-ASYNCRT1=A, D-MNIO1=A, D-CONCCOMB1=A, D-RACEWIN1=A, D-CONCSELECT1=A). Build one model only: task/channel/taskgroup. No @async/await, no user coroutine primitive, no second race/select mechanism.

Already shipped foundations to preserve:
- #102: taskgroup g { ... }, g.task { ... }, wait/join, scope-exit ownership, existing g.all/g.race/g.any vertical slice.
- #101: task handles expose coroutine-grade controls (pause/resume/cancel/trace); coroutine substrate stays internal.
- #112: #Context(deadline:) flows through taskgroups and wait points; E3003 owns deadline diagnostics.
- #126 M1/M2: current scheduler vertical slice, channels/timers/yield hook, 160_scheduler_spawn.

Implementation order for dumb agents:
1. Inventory current behavior first. Read docs/spec/philosophy.md, syntax-decisions.md entries for D-ASYNCRT1/D-MNIO1/D-NURSERY1/D-TASKSCOPE1/D-CONCCOMB1/D-RACEWIN1/D-CONCSELECT1/D-DEADLINE1/D-COROUTINE1, docs/plans/epoch-3/concurrency-vision.md, Source/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, Source/Interpreter.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, task/channel sema/codegen, and tests for examples 131, 157, 158, 160.
2. Write missing acceptance tests before code. Add/extend examples/features concurrency examples plus CLI/golden tests for: 100k idle parked tasks or smallest CI-safe equivalent with a scale benchmark guard; channel receive wakes one parked task without busy-wait; taskgroup scope cancels losing race tasks; g.all fail-fast cancels siblings; g.race returns first success and cancels losers; g.any returns first completion including errors; if g.select() arms deregister losers; deadline firing wakes parked I/O/channel/task waits with Jet-owned E3003; detached tasks require explicit expert policy/name.
3. Replace cooperative-only scheduler gaps with real parker abstraction. Define internal runtime traits, not user syntax: Scheduler, Parker, TimerWheel, IoParker. Start with portable readiness fallback for tests; implement D-MNIO1 native backends behind cfg modules (Linux epoll/io_uring path, macOS/BSD kqueue, Windows IOCP). No external runtime dependency unless owner approves a new dep card.
4. Route every blocking-looking stdlib wait through the parker. Channel recv/send, timers/sleep, task join/wait, TCP accept/read/write, HTTP client/server waits must park Jet tasks, not OS threads. Real OS-blocking fallback must run on an explicit blocking pool and be observable; never silently block scheduler workers.
5. Finish structured combinators in taskgroup only. g.all/g.race/g.any/select are methods or scoped operations on the taskgroup; they create no detached work and return/propagate through one cancellation model. Implement D-RACEWIN1 inside g.race; #103 is merged here. Implement D-CONCCOMB1 here; #36 is merged here.
6. Implement D-CONCSELECT1 exactly as ratified: if-fused select over g.select() arms. Parser/sema/codegen/tests must reuse match/if-arm typing where possible. Select must register arms under taskgroup ownership, wake exactly one winner, deregister losers, and compose with deadlines/cancellation.
7. Add observability and misuse diagnostics. Runtime metrics: runnable/parked task counts, poller wake count, worker utilization, queue depth, cancelled losers. Diagnostics/lints: forgotten task handle wait, swallowed cancellation, deadline ignored, detached task without policy/name, real blocking call on scheduler worker.
8. Prove parity and scale. cargo test green; examples 131/157/158/160 still pass; add deterministic scheduler tests with fake clock; add stress tests gated for CI budget; add a benchmark/report target that demonstrates 100k parked connections/tasks when run locally. rustc errors remain ICE-only; all user errors are sema/driver diagnostics.

Exit criteria:
- One coherent public model in docs/spec/spec.md and examples: task/channel/taskgroup + scoped combinators + deadline context.
- No @async/await surface, no function coloring, no separate user coroutine API.
- Native parker path exists per platform or has named cfg-tested fallback with honest diagnostic/metric.
- race/all/any/select cannot leak losing tasks past taskgroup scope.
- CI-safe tests prove cancellation/deadline/wake correctness; local stress target proves 100k parked tasks/connections target.
- docs/plans/epoch-3/async-networking.md and concurrency-vision.md match implementation.

But D-CANCELMODEL1=C remains unsafe in no-fallback Cranelift outside #Shield: JIT extern C hosts jet_jit_channel_receive[_status], jet_jit_sender_send, and jet_jit_select_wait call scheduler waits directly; cancelled unshielded waits invoke panic_any(JetCancelUnwind). Temporary exact regression (same spawned receive test with #Shield removed) aborts process: thread caused non-unwinding panic, SIGABRT. join/all/race/any also call scheduler fatal/deadline-capable paths directly and require status/trap audit. Fix gate: every JIT wait/combinator host returns typed Value/Cancelled/Deadline/Trap status; Cranelift branches to native epilogue, emits all lexical shield leaves once, returns frame, then Rust wrapper delivers cancellation/deadline. Add no-fallback regressions for receive/send/select/join/all/race/any, cancellation plus deadline, normal/return/?/trap/break/continue, nested shield priority; keep AOT/JIT/dev parity. questions.text: What is the best of both worlds approach here? We are trying to provide best in class service & support for any use case, not just some.
questions.answer: Best of both worlds for async is M:N green threads (Option A) — here's why it delivers everything: (1) No function coloring. Beginners write `task { do_io() }` and experts write the same thing. There is no async/non-async split to manage. Go demonstrates this at Internet scale. Java added Project Loom (virtual threads) specifically because async/await (Option B) proved inadequate — the industry has already run this experiment. (2) High concurrency for free. An M:N scheduler parks threads on IO waits and runs other tasks, achieving 100k+ connections without any new syntax. (3) Expert control is still available: task handles give you priorities, pinning, cancellation, monitoring. Channels give you explicit synchronization. These are the expert levers, just not a second concurrency MODEL. Why not Option C (hybrid M:N + @async)? I8: having two yielding mechanisms (green-thread park and @async fn future) is two ways to write concurrent code. Teams standardize on one and the other becomes dead weight or, worse, they mix and no one can read the code. The apparent limitation of Option A — 'I can't explicitly control when I yield' — is the Go objection, and Go's answer is: you don't need to. Task/channel primitives cover all real expert needs. Recommendation: Option A. It IS the best of both — simplicity without sacrificing power.
