questions.text: For all/most of the “marker/attributes”, or at least the ones for which this is appropriate like memory, why not have the ability to mark individual scopes/blocks, functions, modules, AND packages. This way the user can define in one place based on where they want the given “marker” to be relevant insteead of tons of repetition. This also keeps consistency throughout various echelons. Please update this ballot accordingly and open another ballot/card to allow that type of scoping everywhere as appropriate
questions.answer:
Yes. Adopt one scoping ladder for eligible markers: block, function, module, and package. One declaration applies below that point; the innermost declaration of the same marker key wins, while unrelated inherited keys remain. `jet explain` should show the effective value and every contributing or overridden declaration.

Memory facts are eligible: `#Policy(no_alloc)`, `zero_rc`, and `arena_bounded(N)`. Effect bounds and prohibitions can inherit where their semantics remain sound. `#Unsafe` needs split treatment: block and function forms may authorize audited unsafe operations, while module and package forms may only tighten policy, such as forbidding unsafe code or requiring audit evidence. A wide `#Unsafe` authorization would violate the user-written audited-region requirement.

Keep per-site claims narrow when the proof depends on the exact site. `#Grant` creates a lexical authority handle that must not escape. `#Tainted` marks a specific value origin. `#Sanitizer` vouches for one function. Serde field attributes change one field's wire shape. Those cannot safely become implicit package-wide claims.

questions.text: This seems excessive if it is the default requirement. We want to treat experts like adults, not baby them. If we need to enforce stricter rules, then that should be enforceable and auditable for enterprises/teams, but should not be forced for EVERY user unless they opt in and need the safety. We need to allow ignoring/bypassing things like unsafe as opt in at package level. That way if a new user (who is an expert) wants to do some unsafe work, they can just use a single flag or add a single line to the package file to suppress/ignore/ skip need for unsafe markings
questions.answer:
You're right about the additional typed obligation layer. I reworked option A so normal packages keep the current D-LL1/D-UNSAFE2 behavior: the `#Unsafe` gate alone. Teams opt into `policy: { unsafe: .Obligations }`; audit output records the effective policy and each operation's obligations. Experts can write `policy: { unsafe: .Relaxed }` once, which makes the reason optional and removes L3101, but still requires a `#Unsafe` region or function for low-level operations.

Boundary: under current I1 and D-UNSAFE2, no package setting may permit raw operations outside `#Unsafe`. Memory and type safety remain enforced outside every gate.

Your request to “skip need for unsafe markings” could instead mean removing `#Unsafe` itself. That conflicts with current I1 and D-UNSAFE2 and requires an explicit invariant-amendment ballot. I added that as separate option D: `policy: { unsafe: .Unchecked }` permits package-wide ungated unsafe and records that choice. I recommend A: adult default, optional enterprise obligations, one-line reduced ceremony, and the ratified boundary intact.

questions.text: My idea for opt in GC is that it could be supported as a package level setting or potentially smaller scope depending on user config. This way for things like go-project replacements in jet or typescript or python project replacements, the user could just opt into using the GC once and not worry about it. We should allow finer control and open up the GC to be usable on a lower mechanical level for embedding into modules/functions/etc, but should be magic by default. Also I want it to have a logging capability which could serve as a way to track/tool/debug where memory isn’t properly traced so that we have a clear way for the user to remove the GC and be fully borrow checker based. Update this card accordingly and make a new set of cards/ballots as needed to meet this goal
questions.answer:
Yes. The updated ballot proposes GC opt-in on the four-echelon ladder being opened by D-MARK-SCOPE1 from #644. One `package.jet` line can cover a whole Go, TypeScript, or Python replacement. The same setting can narrow to a module, function, or block.

Under the recommended option, GC is magic inside an opted scope. Heap values gain traced identity with no `Gc<T>` ceremony. Bare storage creates a traced edge; `&` still gates writes, `^` transfers a root, and `~` stays a deep copy. Outside the scope, D-MEM1 remains unchanged.

GC observability is also a required migration path. Trace mode records every allocation the ownership checker could not prove, its source site, and the reason. `jet gc report` groups those sites and gives concrete fixes, such as owned restructuring or `Pool<T>`/`Id<T>`. The target end state is an empty report, after which the scope opt-in can be removed.

D-DEP-GC1=A already chose the std-only native collector, so this does not reopen I6. Any later external collector or runtime bridge needs its own I6 ballot. Two implementation cards cover scope semantics and trace/report tooling.

cards.title: GC scope opt-in: package, module, function, block
cards.body: Implement D-OPTGC1's `gc` key in the existing `#Policy(…)` family across package, module, function, and block scope through D-MARK-SCOPE1's shared applicability matrix. Do not build GC-specific inheritance. A package opt-in gives Go, TypeScript, and Python replacement projects automatic traced storage without `Gc<T>` ceremony. Narrower scopes support embedded GC subsystems. D-MEM1 read, `&` write, `^` take, and second-class-borrow safety remain enforced. Outside opted scopes, ownership stays the default. This card owns GC semantics, sema, TIR, AOT, dev parity, diagnostics, docs, and examples. GC trace/report behavior is tracked separately.

cards.title: core.auth base64url decoder accepts non-canonical encodings (JWS signature malleability)
cards.body: Found via full-suite flake (core_auth_verify_jwt_bad_signature_is_error fails ~25-50% of runs): jet_auth_b64url_decode (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Auth.rs) ignores nonzero trailing padding bits, so a signature whose final base64url char is altered within the padding band decodes to the same 32 bytes and verifies. RFC 7515 requires rejecting non-canonical base64url exactly to prevent this malleability. Fix fail-closed: decoder rejects nonzero leftover bits; verify_jwt maps signature-part decode failure to InvalidSignature. Related same-day flake to diagnose: tests/pkg.rs key_rotation_warns_not_errors intermittently reds with E1246 (signature doesn't match recorded public key) — determine whether it shares the canonicality bug or is a distinct signing-path nondeterminism; card separately if distinct. Prelude is include_str-embedded: rebuild jet before smoke tests.
cards.plan: Fix canonicality once in shared `jet_auth_b64url_decode`: reject impossible residual lengths and any nonzero unused trailing bits before returning bytes, while preserving the accepted URL alphabet and unpadded canonical form. Audit every decoder caller so stricter rejection is intentional. In JWT verification, map signature-segment decode/canonicality failure to InvalidSignature without changing header or payload error contracts. Add exhaustive last-character alias regressions for both padding-bit widths, canonical RFC vectors, malformed alphabet/length cases, and an end-to-end token whose altered signature text formerly verified. Rebuild the include_str-embedded prelude before smoke tests. Reproduce the key_rotation flake independently; if it survives this fix, raise a separate root-cause card rather than folding unrelated signing nondeterminism into this patch.

cards.title: First-party typed Event and Hook system
cards.body: Design and finish Jet’s first-party typed Event and Hook system on the existing runtime, ownership, effects, debugger, and Canvas facts. Scope: typed Event<T>, DecisionHook<T,E>, subscription and EventScope lifetimes, deterministic ordering/once/priority/reentrancy, bounded async dispatch and backpressure, structured cancellation/deadlines/close, typed failure policy, HookDecision continuation, diagnostics, debugger traces, and Canvas projection. D-EVENT1=D, D-EVENT2=A, and D-EVENT-CONTINUE1=C are binding; no new signal/reactive mechanism or stale external plan document is authoritative. Acceptance follows the card checklist and current refs.
cards.plan: Finish the first-party typed Event<T>/Hook<T,R> system on existing runtime/ownership/effect machinery. Apply D-EVENT1=D, D-EVENT2=A, and D-EVENT-CONTINUE1=C exactly: subscription handles own lifetime, ordering/once/priority/reentrancy are deterministic, cancellation integrates structured concurrency, async dispatch has explicit backpressure, and fallible handlers use the ratified continuation policy. Add trace/debug and Canvas projection as views over the same source/runtime facts. No second signal/reactive mechanism.

cards.title: Allow user definition of operators for classes/structs - even python does this
cards.body: Allow user definition of operators for classes/structs - even python does this. We should have excellent, convenient, and intuitive default behavior but allow full access to “internal” apis, like operator definitions for structs/types. Need to design and choose a consistent syntax. Python uses double underscore prefix (and postfix?) to indicate some of these.
cards.plan: Implement D-OPDEF1 through the existing capability mechanism, not Python-style dunder names or a second operator registry. Reuse closed capability bundles such as @Numeric/@Comparable: parse and register the ratified declaration form, resolve exactly one operator method per type, type-check same-type/result laws in sema, lower approved calls through TIR, and keep codegen inference-free. Preserve E0105 no-overload and built-in lane/linalg closure. Ship Money/Vec-style examples plus ambiguity, missing capability, wrong operand/result, orphan, and recursion diagnostics.

cards.title: Terminal + CLI visual system: designed color/polish on EVERY user-facing surface
cards.body:
Owner mandate (repeated, 2026-07-14 and earlier #360 bounce): sparse/NO_COLOR-looking TTYs are unacceptable on real terminals. Every user-facing surface must look intentionally designed in color mode — not one cyan row and plain chrome.

Surfaces in scope (non-exhaustive, add as found):
- jet ? help palette (interactive + query + F1)
- jet REPL hybrid UI
- jet diagnostics / explain
- jetpack + jetos CLI Theme/Output (nh-class)
- jet env shell prompt receipts/spinners
- tower CLI status/brief human output
- any new interactive TTY app

Law:
- One shared Theme vocabulary (accent, dim, success, warn, error, invert selection, borders) — I8, no per-surface inventing unrelated palettes.
- Color on when TTY && !NO_COLOR (and --color=always|never honored). NO_COLOR keeps a readable monochrome design, not an afterthought.
- Borders, headers, categories, hints, selections, match emphasis all styled in color mode.
- Do not close a frontend/CLI card that ships a new interactive surface without this bar.

First vertical: jet ? Help/Render rich color. Then share Theme into REPL/diagnostics/jetpack.
cards.plan: Use one shared Theme vocabulary and renderer primitives across every TTY surface. Audit help, REPL, diagnostics/explain, jetpack/jetos, env receipts, Tower, and new interactive commands; migrate each without per-surface palettes. TTY auto-color honors NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR/--color; monochrome retains hierarchy, focus, contrast, and keyboard behavior. Prove real terminal matrices, redirected bytes, narrow/wide viewports, ANSI safety, accessibility contrast, snapshots, and no semantic output drift.

cards.title: Choose how an output links to callable code
cards.body: Decide the one relationship between a package output and the ordinary Jet function it starts.
cards.plan: Implement D-SHAPE-OUTPUT-CALLABLE1 across parser, sema, TIR lowering, dev/JIT, formatter, package model, CLI selection, semantic index, Canvas, docs, and diagnostics. Runnable typed Outputs hold one checked Jet function reference; sema resolves it before codegen, enforces the Output kind's exact parameter/return/effect/authority contract, rejects ambiguity or mismatch with Jet-owned snapshots, and carries a resolved callable identity into dumb codegen. Preserve ceremony-free standalone `fn run`; inside a Package, D-ECO-OUTPUT-DEFAULT1's deterministic selection is the sole selection path. No string symbol lookup, generated Rust name, runtime reflection, second callable wrapper, or rustc diagnostic. Prove free functions, qualified functions, moved/renamed source, stale locks, each runnable Output kind, formatter/grammar stability, inspect/Canvas reconstruction, and AOT/dev parity.

cards.title: Implement common marker scoping and provenance
cards.body: Implement D-MARK-SCOPE1 after ratification. Define one compiler-owned applicability matrix for marker placement at block, function, module, and package levels. Preserve I1: package or module declarations may tighten unsafe policy but never authorize unsafe operations outside a user-written #Unsafe block or function. Keep site-specific value, authority, function-proof, and field-wire markers at their exact legal sites. Effective marker facts must carry source provenance through sema, diagnostics, tooling, AOT, and dev execution.
cards.plan: After #534 completes D-SHAPE2's single `@Rule` marker migration, implement only D-MARK-SCOPE1=A's common scope/applicability/provenance ladder. Package settings enter through the ratified `package.jet` `policy:` field; source rules use the post-migration `@Rule` form at module, function, or block scope. One compiler-owned registry matrix defines each rule's legal echelons, inheritance, same-key override or merge, tightening law, conflicts, and effective-source provenance. Authority, unsafe, taint, sanitizer, and wire rules cannot widen beyond their sound sites. Parser, formatter, sema, semantic index, diagnostics, and `jet explain` consume the same matrix. This card does not implement memory facts, GC promotion, a collector, or GC reports.

cards.title: Test isolation: key_rotation_warns_not_errors flakes on HOME/helper race
cards.body: Full-suite flake (verify-full 2026-07-15, ~intermittent): tests/pkg.rs:3782 key_rotation_warns_not_errors reds with E1246 signature-verification-failed. NOT the base64url canonicality bug (#663) — canonical generated signatures don't explain genuine-signature mismatch. Worker diagnosis (isolated 10x green): process-global HOME race. Tests overwrite a cache-selected crypto helper while mutating HOME at tests/pkg.rs:73, but KEYS_LOCK (tests/pkg.rs:3423) guards only JET_KEYS_DIR; concurrent sign/verify select different real/fake helpers under parallel gate load. Fix: widen the test lock to cover HOME/helper selection, or make helper selection not read process-global HOME. Test-only; signing path fail-closed behavior untouched.
cards.plan: Fix the test race in `tests/pkg.rs` with one existing lock: remove the separate `KEYS_LOCK` and make `with_keys` take `STORE_LOCK`, which already surrounds all three `install_closed_status_crypto_helper` callers while they temporarily change process-global `HOME` and write the HOME-selected cached helper. Audit every `with_keys` and helper-installer call for nesting before the change. Keep `cached_crypto_helper_path`, signing, verification, E1246, and key-rotation product behavior unchanged. Prove the fix by repeatedly running the rotation test alongside the three entropy/helper tests under the normal parallel harness, then targeted pkg tests and full verification; do not hide the race with global single-thread execution.

cards.title: Choose one identifier casing law
cards.body: Owner wants one enforced casing law across the whole language; the surface today is a documented mix (effect keywords Pascal vs lowercase keywords, module split, constant spelling drift, unenforced S54 convention). Ballot D-SHAPE-CASE1 presents PascalCase-everywhere vs snake_case-everywhere vs strict machine-enforced two-tier. Interacts with D-SHAPE3b (Val/None/Ok/Err), D-CASING1 (markers), S54. Outcome drives a migration slice + lint E-code; sequence BEFORE the mass example-touching law cards so snapshots re-bless once.
cards.plan: D-SHAPE-CASE1 is the sole current gate. After ratification, encode the chosen law as one compiler-owned category table and migrate the complete surface without compatibility aliases: A makes every identifier PascalCase; B makes every identifier snake_case and amends conflicting prior casing laws; C enforces PascalCase type-like names and snake_case value-like names. For C, immediately raise the ballot's three named follow-up decisions for effect-keyword, generic-module-template, and constant spelling before touching those ambiguous categories; unambiguous categories proceed from the ratified table. Implement lexer/parser/sema name-category checks, formatter-preserving behavior, one coded diagnostic with precise category/fix, LSP/rename support, docs/examples/snapshots/grammars, package/API migration checks, and AOT/dev-neutral behavior.

questions.text: I need a much more thorough analysis. Give me a bunch more languages showing casing for multiple code excerpts and explain real world tradeoffs extensively, including the implications of prescribing style -> where enterprises may have internal style guides that conflict -> how often does this happen? Is this an issue elsewhere?
questions.answer:
Survey. Nearly every language designed after 2010 prescribes a casing convention. They converge on the same two-tier shape: types are PascalCase, values are snake_case or camelCase. They differ mainly in how the rule is enforced. The ballot's comparisons section now carries 15 languages with code; summary below.

Enforcement varies by level. Grammar-enforced languages make casing part of parsing, so violation is a syntax error: Haskell, Elm, Erlang, Prolog, and partly Ruby. Rust warns through default compiler lints. Dart, Kotlin, and Go enforce through shipped tools. Python, Java, C#, Swift, and TypeScript rely on convention and optional linters. C++ sets no shared default at all.

Enterprise style-guide conflicts. These happen almost only in languages that never enforced a law from the start. Where casing is grammar-enforced, conflict is impossible and nobody forks: no Haskell, Elm, or Erlang shop runs a lowercase-type house style. Go overloads casing with visibility, and it is universally accepted; Google's and Uber's guides build on it rather than against it.

Rust shops keep the non_snake_case warnings; the #[allow] escape exists mainly for FFI, not house style. The conflicts cluster where no law shipped. Python's PEP 8 is unenforced, so legacy camelCase survives for decades in unittest, logging, and Twisted. C++ and JavaScript set no default, so Google, LLVM, Qt, and Unreal each wrote a different guide, and reading across codebases suffers.

The empirical pattern is consistent. A language born with an enforced law sees internal guides adopt it, not fight it. A language that shipped without one grows many competing house styles that never reconcile.

Implications of prescribing style. A single enforced law speeds onboarding and reading, because a reader infers a name's category from its shape without opening its definition. It also makes tooling predictable: derives, LSP rename, and doc generation can rely on category-from-name. Codegen output stays stable because names map one way.

One cost is real. Foreign names must keep their original casing, so any prescribed law needs a narrow, sanctioned escape for interop. Rust uses #[allow(non_snake_case)] on extern items; Dart suppresses the lint on FFI and JS interop. Jet will need the same narrow escape for FFI bindings. That belongs in a follow-up decision, not invented here.

Where this shows up elsewhere. Formatters are the precedent. gofmt, black, and prettier proved that teams accept a prescribed style when it is universal and tool-enforced from day one. The resentment cases are retrofits, where a rule arrives after a large codebase already chose differently. Enforcing casing from the start avoids that retrofit.

On this evidence C is the right law. It is the only option that keeps the type-versus-value signal every post-2010 language preserves, while still being machine-enforced so no file can drift.

questions.text: I don’t understand what this means, dumb it down to plain language
questions.answer:
Plain version. Today your build script can look at one type at a time (to derive things). This ballot asks: may the build script also READ the finished, fully-checked program — every package, type, and function — and report its own errors?

Concrete use: your team rule is "every public function that touches the network must take a timeout". Today that rule lives on a wiki or an external linter that half-parses Jet and drifts. With B, your build entry can loop over all functions and emit a real Jet diagnostic — same format as compiler errors, and the API forces you to fill in code + what/why/fix, so quality stays I4-grade.

Hard limits that keep it safe: READ ONLY (build code cannot change your program, ever — that is rung C, still frozen); runs only from YOUR chosen build entry, never when merely importing a library (a dependency cannot run rules or code inside your build); and if you don't write one, nothing changes.

B = "the compiler will show your program to your build script and let it complain, nothing more."

cards.title: Polyglot Phase 1: systems floor — inline tier, inline asm, C++ binder
cards.body: From docs/proposals/polyglot.md. Adds the missing fourth D-FFI-UNIFY1 tier (#Foreign(<lang>) inline bodies with the Jet signature as checked contract), the assembly floor (#Foreign(asm) inside #Unsafe, typed operands), and the cpp.* binder (clang bindgen, opaque class handles, exceptions -> T ? CppError, on-demand template instantiation). One ballot per decision: D-FFI-INLINE1, D-FFI-ASM1, D-FFI-CPP1. Gates every later phase: inline tier shape is reused by all languages.
cards.plan: Implement the ratified systems floor on D-FFI-UNIFY1's checked boundary. cards.title: Parser correctness policy: contracts, adversarial corpus, and dependency gates
cards.body: Audit every hand-rolled protocol/config parser: LSP JSON, manifest TOML subset, SemVer/ranges, C prototypes, and registry/advisory formats. For each, publish its accepted grammar, reject unsupported cases deliberately, add hostile-input coverage, and fix correctness holes. Jet owns every diagnostic. If a protocol cannot be made correct within I6, stop that slice and raise a separate dependency-exception ballot before adding any crate.
cards.plan: Inventory parser entrypoints and current documented promises. Build a parser-by-parser contract table. Add adversarial tests for escapes, Unicode, nesting, malformed input, recovery, overflow, and ambiguous versions/prototypes. Tighten contracts or implementations until behavior and docs agree. Any external parser remains owner-gated under I6.

cards.title: Plan affine quantity point semantics
cards.body: Prepare point, difference, declaration, conversion, and diagnostic ballot only after dimensional algebra ownership is ratified.
cards.plan: All quantity choices are ratified. Implement D-SHAPE-QUANTITY1=A compiler-owned zero-cost dimensions, D-QUANTITY-DECL1=A exact scale/offset declarations, D-QUANTITY-TYPE1=A generic Dimension/Kind bounds, D-QUANTITY-POINT1=A Point/Delta algebra, and D-QUANTITY-CONVERT1=B exact same-dimension implicit conversion in mixed arithmetic, arguments, and bindings. The finer operand unit wins mixed arithmetic; equal scales keep the left unit. Point conversion applies scale plus offset and Delta conversion applies scale only. Sema never rounds silently: inexact or overflowing boundaries reject with the destination-owned from_* or from_*_rounded fix. package.jet explicit_units and narrower #Policy(explicit_units) require written conversions through the normal policy ladder. Finish declaration, sema, API/Codable/semver, diagnostics, inspect, examples, grammar, and AOT/dev parity without a second conversion path.

questions.text: Remember one of the goals is not to baby experts. There can be value in having explicit conversions but in practice I would expect people doing pragmatic work to want implicit conversions which would be defined in advance anyway by the unit family. Maybe have some kind of marker/policy that can disable implicit conversions? For example, in my case if I was doing cad measurements, I would probably name something like inner_diameter_mm and length_m. It would be annoying to have to do mathematical operations with tons of dot methods just to manually convert everything. Implicit should be default with an explicit opt in
questions.answer: Agreed, and the ballot now recommends exactly that. Reworked option B: same-dimension units convert on their own wherever the family ratio makes the conversion exact — mixed arithmetic (lands on the finer unit so whole numbers stay exact), argument passing, and binding all just work, so length + inner_diameter is one plus sign, no dot-method chain. The guardrail kept: the compiler never rounds silently — a non-exact conversion (1500m into whole km) is a compile error naming the from_meter_rounded fix, so implicit never loses precision. The opt-in you asked for rides the policy ladder you just ratified: policy: .{ explicit_units: true } in package.jet, or #Policy(explicit_units) at module/function/block, restores explicit-only in that scope. Ballot updated and ready to ratify (rec B).

cards.title: Subjectless multi-arm if for ordered condition dispatch
cards.body: Reduce repeated `else if` chains with a subjectless `if { condition -> body }` form. Preserve `if` as Jet's only branching keyword and reuse existing arm bodies, first-match ordering, pattern-test bindings, fallback rules, formatter shape, and checked TIR lowering. This card is gated on D-IFGUARD1; no syntax or implementation lands before owner ratification.
cards.plan: After D-IFGUARD1 is ratified, implement only the selected surface. For a subjectless form, parse `if {` as ordered Boolean arms and reuse the existing dispatch pipeline through a compiler-private Bool subject; this is lowering only, not a source-level comparison. Do not add another keyword, AST mechanism, or codegen path. Sema checks every head as Bool. A pattern binding reaches the body only from a leading pattern test joined through `&&`; bindings under `||` never enter body scope. Evaluate heads once from top to bottom, run only the first matching body, and apply the ratified fallback law. Update Syntax.rs decision adjacency, parser and formatter, sema, diagnostics and UI snapshots, grammar/editor support, examples and goldens, formal/spec prose, Canvas projection/editing, and dev/AOT parity. Use targeted verification and fresh Sol review.

The running compiled program cant link the compiler, so serve() shells out to jet build --target=web for every rebuild (subprocess, not a library call) -- new Prelude/DevServer.rs, std-only. If no fn dev() exists, falls straight through to todays default (jet dev --target=web / #Target(Web) inference), unchanged -- verified via the pre-existing test suite untouched.

Verified for real this time by checking the process tree for the actual compiled child binary + confirming a live jet build subprocess-driven rebuild-on-save, not just that a server responded on the port.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.text — Unicode completeness (case folding, segmentation, width)
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Swift String honesty + ICU floor. Cards #66 (graphemes, normalization) and the unicode slice of #117 are done — verify shipped surface first.

Audit list: NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD normalization (verify); full Unicode case mapping and case folding for upper/lower/caseless-compare (not ASCII-only); grapheme iteration (verify) plus word and sentence segmentation (UAX #29); display width (east-asian width) for terminal alignment; char classification (alphabetic, numeric, whitespace per Unicode); efficient String builder for heavy concatenation; general str utility audit vs Rust str + Python str (splitn/rsplit, trim variants, pad/center, starts/ends combinators, char_indices equivalents). Collation/locale sort: record policy (probably an i18n non-goal for now — state it).

Done means: audit table in docs, gaps shipped with examples + golden tests or recorded as declined non-goals. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).

Verify/complete NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD, full case mapping/folding, grapheme/word/sentence segmentation, D-TEXTWIDTH1=B display width, classification, scalar/UTF-8 helpers, and efficient builder/util parity. cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: libsodium/age misuse-resistance — high-level envelopes a beginner cannot hold wrong, primitives behind them for experts. Card #64 (crypto push) is done — but the prelude currently exposes only sha256, hmac, and random_bytes; verify what actually shipped (FFI bridge included), then close the gaps.

Scope: authenticated encryption seal/open envelope with one canonical cipher (XChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-GCM — owner ballot), nonce handling internal (never user-supplied by default); Ed25519 sign/verify; X25519 key exchange; Argon2id password hash + verify with safe defaults; HKDF; SHA-512 and BLAKE3; constant-time comparison; key/secret types that refuse Display (no keys in logs — safe by default); simple key encoding (raw/hex/PEM as needed); file-encryption envelope (age-class). PQ hybrid agility already tracked (#71).

I6: implementations in-house or behind the FFI bridge crate — each new bridge dep is an owner ballot. Done means: each primitive ships with test vectors from the reference specs (RFC/NIST/libsodium vectors) as golden tests. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).

cards.title: Sigil sweep: # for attributes/instructions/properties, @ for locations/addresses/sources
cards.body: Owner decree 2026-07-23: revert the rule/marker plane from @ back to #. Conceptual split: # marks attributes, instructions, properties; @ marks locations, addresses, sources. Reverses D-SHAPE2/D-MARKERMOVE1's @ plane; restores D-ATTR1's # plane. Highest priority: lands before any parallel in-flight syntax work to avoid rework.
cards.plan:
SCOPE (all gates ratified: D-VERDICT-732-1, D-ATTR4=A, D-LOOPLABEL3=A)
- Flip @ -> # for the whole applied-rule plane: RULE_PREFIX in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/markers.rs plus every APPLIED_RULES spelling (@Unsafe, @Test, @Pure, @Cli, @Task, @Every, @Target, @Pre/@Post/@Persist, @Inline/@InlineAlways, bundles, serde markers, @DebugOnly, @Meta, @[allow(...)], @[a,b] lists, pub-file/no-prelude/static/inline/SIMD-reduce rules).
- effects_surface.rs already holds ATTR_PREFIX="#" and FOREIGN_AT_ATTR="@" from D-ATTR1; those become authoritative again. Teaching-error direction reverses: @Marker in rule position -> 'attributes use #'.
- D-ATTR4=A: interpolation debug spec flips to {value#Debug}.
- D-LOOPLABEL3=A: loop labels leave @ entirely. New: outer :: loop naming (compile-time label kind in the ordinary namespace), outer.break()/outer.next() dot exits, bare break/next keywords keep working for the innermost loop. outer@ suffix + break outer@ retire with a teaching error; E0988 matrix updated; outer := loop rejected; label-in-value-position is a teaching error. expr ?? outer.break() composes per D-ORRETURN-CANON1.
- STAYS @ pending #733/D-JPK-REF1: provider@target source refs (U6), path@host OS selector (D-JPK-OSHOST1=C). Do NOT touch ref grammar in this card.
- STAYS #: [T#N] fixed-size separator (S76), #Caller(), textkit#1.2.0 version pins (VERSION-#).

FOOTPRINT (measured 2026-07-23): ~182 files with @-marker spellings across examples/docs/crates; docs/spec/diagnostics.md ~104 hits, syntax-decisions.md ~84, spec.md ~54, examples/canon.jet 18; examples/features/basics/labeled_loops.jet for D-LOOPLABEL3.

SLICES (each verified with targeted tests; full suite once at closeout)
1. Syntax registry: flip RULE_PREFIX to #, reconcile effects_surface constants, register :: loop-label form, update decision-ID comments.
2. Lexer/parser: # dispatch in rule position (decl/expr/scope); outer :: loop + dot-exit parsing; wrong-plane fall-throughs (#Wasm/#Js/#Suppress/#Uninit/#Ref retirements) keep behavior under the new prefix.
3. Teaching errors: @Marker -> use-# error; outer@/break outer@ -> use ::/dot-exit error; label-as-value error; each with UI snapshot (I4).
4. Formatter: emit # and :: labels; fmt STABILITY round-trip tests (idempotence alone misses dropped tokens).
5. Sema/LSP/highlights + editors/tree-sitter grammar (zed grammar-repo is generated, do not commit).
6. Sweep examples/**.jet + golden outputs (I5), canon.jet + labeled_loops.jet first; rm -rf ~/.cache/jet/build before smoke.
7. Docs sweep: syntax-decisions.md, spec.md, diagnostics.md, philosophy refs; UI snapshots re-blessed.
8. Closeout: fresh-binary smoke, one full-suite run, Sol review.

COORDINATION
- No other card may introduce @-plane or outer@-label spellings until this lands; in-flight branches rebase on the flip commit.
- Land slices 1-4 as one atomic sweep so no split-brain surface ships.
- Ref grammar (#733, D-JPK-REF1) is owner-gated and explicitly out of scope here.

cards.title: Silent no-op: list element field writes are dropped
cards.body:
Ship-blocker from the 2026-07-23 persona audit (Klaus, systems dev).

Repro (/tmp/persona-klaus/mut.jet): `ps[0].x = 11` and `ps[0].x += 1` compile clean, mutate a temporary, and the old values print. Plain `ns[1] += 5` IS rejected with a teaching error — so the accepted spelling is the broken one.

This kills array-of-structs code (games, sims) with silent wrong physics. It breaks the spirit of I3: sema passes what codegen drops. Fix first, before any polish work.

log.text: Review finding — crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:41 and crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/statements.rs:822: indexed compound field assignment does not preserve Jet operator-hook semantics. Sema accepts hs[0].value += rhs when value implements Jet Add because compound_field_type cannot resolve Expr::Index; the new emitter then writes native Rust +=. Jet generates user_Add, not std::ops::AddAssign, so rustc rejects a sema-approved program, violating criterion 1 and I2. Repro check with a [Holder] whose Vec2 field implements Add reports no Jet problems. Fix by resolving and rewriting the indexed field hook through the existing Add method spine, or emit E0362 before TIR; add a regression for this indexed user-operator case. Numeric Int = and += paths pass targeted TIR, golden, strict interpreter/JIT/AOT three-way, fresh build/smoke, Pool parity, and columnar runtime/UI checks. Broad jit_coverage_audit still has known unrelated manifest drift; the new collections/struct_list_mutation entry is observed covered and IndexFieldAssign reports 2 covered, 0 gaps.
Master integration agent: do not stage, commit, or merge sidequests-implementation while these cards are active. Wait for explicit closeout handoff; sidequest workers own this worktree.

Investigation: parser and sema accept a mutable list-element field place, but TIR lowers the index through clone-returning jet_index_vec. AOT and default dev print old values. Forced interpreter gives E2201. Planned fix: use a bounds-checked mutable list place in shared TIR lowering; keep the interpreter teaching boundary.
Integration notice: implementation uses branch sidequests-implementation in .agent-worktrees/sidequests-implementation. Leave branch for the master integration agent after closeout.
Started root-cause trace for list element field writes. No code changes yet.

cards.title: Semantic-core TIR: structured facts, no Rust text inside the IR
cards.body:
Owner directive 2026-07-24: one compiler core; every engine is a lens on it; a feature is written once and works in jet run and jet build the same day.

Why this card exists: TIR is the shared program form, but it carries pre-rendered Rust text (ty_clause strings, Rust place strings like (*user_x), field_rust names, literal text such as vec![1i64, 2i64]). Only the AOT Rust emitter can consume that text. The Cranelift JIT needs structured data, so every feature needs a second hand-written JIT lowering, and 262 example programs sit in tests/jit_gaps.txt today. This card removes the Rust text from TIR so one lowering serves every engine.

This is the root card of the one-core rework. Cards for the canonical interpreter, tiered jet run, and the desugaring wave build on it. Decision D-ONECORE1 on this card picks the overall structure.

1. Inventory every TIR field that holds rendered Rust text (kw, ty_clause, place, field_rust, tmp names, literal strings). Post the checked list to this card's log.
2. Replace them variant by variant with structured facts: typed places, typed literals, type references, symbol ids. Move all Rust text rendering into the emit layer of jet-codegen.
3. Hold byte parity while doing it: golden/snapshot suites and tests/dev.rs::dev_default_matches_compiled_binary stay green after each variant lands.
4. Update the Cranelift lowering to read only structured facts; delete every string-parsing workaround in crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs.
5. Write the core TIR contract into docs/spec/architecture.md (R12 restated per D-ONECORE1) and hand the frozen-contract work to e9 card #668.

cards.title: Tiered jet run: Cranelift per function, interpreter deopt, retire E2211
cards.body:
Today a Cranelift coverage gap in jet run is a hard stop: error E2211 tells the user to go run jet build instead (D-LENS-RUN1, card #728). 262 example programs hit that wall. Once the canonical interpreter (#777) defines runtime behavior, a gap no longer needs to be a wall: the JIT can compile the functions it covers and hand the rest to the interpreter, the way the JVM and V8 tier their execution.

This card makes jet run tiered: tier 1 is native Cranelift, tier 0 is the interpreter, chosen per function, same observable behavior either way. E2211 retires as a user-facing error. tests/jit_gaps.txt stays, but as a performance ratchet, not a feature gate.

Decision D-LENS-RUN2 on this card picks what the user sees at a deopt. It amends ratified D-LENS-RUN1, which forbade any fallback while the only fallback was a different engine with different coverage. The interpreter changes that premise: the fallback IS the reference engine.
cards.plan:
1. Add per-function tier selection to the JIT backend: lower each function through Cranelift; on a named unsupported reason, bind that function to the interpreter instead of failing the program.
2. Make cross-tier calls work both directions (native calling interpreted and back) over the existing host-shim boundary in crates/jet-jit.
3. Retire E2211 per the D-LENS-RUN2 outcome; keep the named gap reasons as internal traces. Add the expert visibility surface the outcome names (for example jet run --trace-tiers).
4. Convert tests/jit_gaps.txt into a performance ratchet: gaps may only shrink; a new gap needs a named reason in the same diff; CI fails on silent growth.
5. Extend the #727/#730 differential gate: every corpus program must produce identical stdout, stderr, and exit code under pure-interpreter, mixed-tier, and AOT runs.

Acceptance: no runnable checked program fails jet run for coverage reasons; the differential gate is green across tier mixes; hot-swap and resident dev still work.
Owned paths: crates/jet-jit/**, Source/Interpreter.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs (run routing), tests/jit_gaps.txt, tests/dev.rs, docs/spec/diagnostics.md (E2211 retirement).

cards.title: Core-shrink wave: surface features desugar in lowering, engines stay untouched
cards.body:
The reason backends fall behind is that TIR is wide: it carries one construct per surface feature (for-in forms, map literals, string interpolation, destructuring, fan-out), and every engine must handle every construct. This card narrows TIR to a small core by desugaring surface features into existing core constructs during lowering, after #776 gives the core clean structured form.

End state: adding a surface feature is a parser + sema + lowering change only. The interpreter, the Cranelift tier, and the Rust emitter see constructs they already support, so both jet run and jet build work the day the lowering lands. That is the structural guarantee behind the owner's one-core directive.
cards.plan:
1. Rank TIR constructs by backend cost: for each executable variant, count the emit arm, the Cranelift arm, and the interpreter arm it forces. Post the ranking to the card log.
2. Desugar the expensive wide constructs into core ones at lowering, one per slice: for-in over literals and collections, map/set literals, string interpolation, tuple/struct/list destructuring, fan-out.
3. Each slice deletes the matching special-case arm from every engine in the same diff. Parity gates stay green per slice.
4. Prove the guarantee on a real feature: implement one small ratified surface feature end to end and show the diff touches no engine files.
5. Record the final core construct list in the TIR contract doc for the e9 freeze card (#668).

Acceptance: measured drop in per-engine match arms; one demonstration feature ships with zero engine-file changes; no new entries in tests/jit_gaps.txt during the wave.
Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/** (lowering), matching arm deletions in crates/jet-jit/** and the emit layer and the evaluator, touched tests.

cards.title: Universal typed-literal head: Type.{ body } for every type
cards.body: Generalize S29/D-DOTCTOR1/2: any type may head a .{ } literal body — scalars U8.{250}, lists [U8].{42,0,0}, maps [String: Int].{}, fixed arrays [U8#3].{255,128,0}, and one-expression assertion bodies Int.{ fetch_rows() }. Body elaborates against the head exactly like an expected-type position; it never converts. Amends D-EMPTY: [T].{} is the explicit empty; bare [] stays contextual.
cards.plan:
blockedBy: none

Authority: D-DOTCTOR3=A (ratified). Amends S29 / D-DOTCTOR1 / D-DOTCTOR2 and D-EMPTY.

Goal: Any type may head a .{ } literal body. The body elaborates against the head like an expected-type position. It never converts.

## 1. Syntax authority
- Add the D-DOTCTOR3 entry in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs.
- Append the syntax-decisions.md log: universal Type.{ body }; [T].{} is the explicit empty; bare [] stays contextual; Int.{ expr } is a one-expression assertion.
- Run jet devtools grammars and bless grammar outputs.

## 2. Parser
Owned: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/postfix.rs and struct-lit helpers; AST for headed bodies that are not only named fields.
- Keep record field lists: Point.{ x: 1, y: 2 }.
- Accept element / entry lists for [T], [T#N], [K: V].
- Accept a single expression body for scalars and assertions.
- Accept empty {} for empty collections (and existing empty/unit cases).
- Nested list bodies may be bare .{ … } or plain [ … ]; both elaborate against the element type.
- Keep E0320 for retired dotless Type { }.
- Formatter prints headed forms; it does not rewrite them into typed bindings.

## 3. Sema
Owned: crates/jet-sema StructLit path (CheckerItems::check_struct_lit and/or a shared typed-literal elaborator), CheckerInfer/expr.rs StructLit arm.
- Resolve the head type (named, list, fixed array, map, scalar, generic apps).
- Set expected_type from the head; elaborate the body; never insert from_* conversions.
- Scalar literal bodies use comptime range checks in the E0135 family (D-RANGETYPE1).
- A mismatched non-literal body is the ordinary type error; teach from_* when the author wanted a conversion.
- Amend D-EMPTY: [T].{} is explicit empty; bare [] keeps contextual inference.

## 4. Lowering / TIR / codegen
- Lower headed literals to the same TIR shapes as today’s expected-type literals and struct construction.
- No new runtime. Codegen stays dumb (I3).
- Prove jet run and JIT parity on the new examples.

## 5. Examples (I5)
- Add examples/features/types/typed_literal_head.jet (or extend dot_construction.jet) covering: U8.{ 250 }, [U8].{ 42, 0, 0 }, [U8#3].{ 255, 128, 0 }, [String: Int].{}, Int.{ fetch_rows() }-style assertion, nested [[U8]].{ .{ 1, 0 }, [0, 1] }.
- Update examples that still put the type only on the binding when a head is the right spelling.
- Bless examples/features/expected/**/*.out.

## 6. Diagnostics / UI snapshots (I4)
- Prefer ordinary mismatch diagnostics; add a new code only if a body shape needs its own what/why/fix.
- Range overflow stays in the E0135 family with UI snapshots.
- No snapshot means no new diagnostic (I4).

## 7. Acceptance tests
- Parser/golden coverage for each head kind.
- Sema: match OK; mismatch fails; no silent convert; [T].{} vs contextual [].
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test (scoped) + jet run on the new example; UI snapshot tests green.
- Meet and verify criteria 1–4 plus the added implementation criteria below.

Land this card before #781 and #782. Those cards rewrite bindings onto these heads.

cards.plan:
blockedBy: none

Authority: D-UNINIT-SENTINEL2=A (ratified). Amends D-UNINIT-SENTINEL1. Prerequisites: #780 Type.{ } heads and #781 bare bindings.

Goal: Move the uninit trigger only. New spelling: bytes := [U8#128].{ uninit }. Flow proof E0420 / E0423 / E0424 and the use core.mem gate stay the same.

## 1. Syntax authority
- Add/amend Syntax.rs for D-UNINIT-SENTINEL2.
- Append syntax-decisions.md: uninit is legal only as the whole body of a Type.{ } head; retire name: Type := uninit.

## 2. Parser
Owned: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/bindings.rs and headed-literal parsing from #780.
- Remove the D-UNINIT-SENTINEL1 trigger (annotated := uninit).
- Accept Type.{ uninit } when uninit is the entire body.

## 3. Sema
Owned: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/bindings.rs (check_uninit_binding) and read-before-write tracking in CheckerInfer/expr.rs.

- Scalars and fixed arrays both allowed per ballot: n := Int.{ uninit }.

## 4. Lowering / TIR / codegen
Owned: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/statements.rs MaybeUninit path.

- Binding.uninit (or the equivalent flag derived from the headed body) still drives codegen.

## 5. Examples / UI snapshots

- Update tests/ui/uninit_*.jet and .stderr. Replace uninit_no_type.jet (annotation-forced) with illegal-position / non-whole-body cases.
- Bless goldens under memory/uninit*.

## 6. Acceptance tests
- Old name: Type := uninit is a parse error once #781 has landed.
- New spelling is green with the same flow diagnostics.

questions.text: We must ensure full expert control & auditability. We want magic out of the box for beginners but experts need to be able to see the inner workings & control as needed. Reconsider this ballot with devils advocate, make it best in the world, ensure ergonomics, magic, and full control are all considered. Tell my why your new option set is best, why you recommend your new recommendation, and how it compares to other languages
questions.answer: Updated D-WASM1. New rec: C, not pure inference. Default is inferred from effects and browser API use, but experts can pin `#Wasm`, `#Js`, and `#WasmExport`, then inspect `jet build --target web --explain-partition`. Devil’s advocate: overrides can create unsound crossings. Patch: sema checks all boundary types/effects, rejects browser handles in WASM, emits a bridge manifest, and snapshots boundary diagnostics. Compared to Next/SvelteKit: similar magic boundary inference, stronger typed bridge/audit story. Compared to Rust wasm-bindgen: less manual glue, more front-end-owned diagnostics.

questions.text: Why A not B? Is there a reason not to use B? it seems like it may be helpful to sometimes have the module level declaration
questions.answer: Reason for A over pure B: required module declarations make every beginner learn partitioning before rendering a page. But the module-level control is useful, so I folded it into A: default partitioning comes from `Browser` effect inference, and experts can add `#Target(Wasm)` / `#Target(Js)` at module level with sema validation. D-WASM1 now reflects that hybrid.

cards.title: Typed embedded and freestanding target profiles
cards.body:
Ratified decision: D-WD11 = B (Typed target profiles (recommended)).
Source ballot: docs/ballots/world-domination-review-2026-07-06.md.

How Jet scales down to microcontrollers, kernels, and no-OS targets.

Chosen direction: Board/target profiles make hidden defaults explicit only when embedded/kernels are selected. Expert controls memory, linker, allocator, panic, volatile, and audit output. Weakness fixed: normal Jet never sees target jargon.

Guardrails:
- Preserve magic defaults plus full expert control from the ballot.
- Before adding any new user-typeable syntax, manifest field, command spelling, marker, provider prefix, or diagnostic code, raise a follow-up Tower ballot.
- No implementation card may ship a stub: docs, examples, diagnostics, tests, and verification must land with behavior.
cards.plan: Implement typed target profiles only when freestanding/embedded/kernel targets are selected; normal Jet stays ceremony-free. Carry target, memory, linker, allocator, panic, volatile, ABI, startup, and audit facts through manifest/package model, sema, TIR, codegen, and build. Preserve I1/#Unsafe gates and transitive memory facts. Prove real Linux freestanding/QEMU plus representative MCU artifacts, linker scripts/maps, no-host-runtime rejection, deterministic cross-builds, size/budget reports, and AOT-only honesty where dev/JIT cannot run.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.encoding — format breadth (XML, binary interchange, streaming)
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Go encoding/* breadth with serde-quality fidelity (existing JSON/TOML/YAML/CSV adapters are already full-fidelity — keep that bar).

Gaps: XML parse/serialize (full, namespace-aware); one canonical binary interchange format (MessagePack or CBOR — pick one, I8; owner ballot); JSON Lines streaming read/write; streaming/incremental (pull) parsing for large JSON/CSV inputs with bounded memory; canonical/stable-key-order JSON output for hashing and diffing; base32; URL-safe base64 variant (verify what encoding.base64 already covers). All through the same Data tree + @[Codable] derive so decode<T> works uniformly.

Done means: each new format is a full adapter (not a lossy subset) with examples + golden tests, or a recorded non-goal. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).

cards.title: corelib audit: core.http — client/server parity with Go net/http + requests ergonomics
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Go net/http server completeness with Python requests/httpx client ergonomics. Client HTTPS-by-default (D-TLS1) and server TLS (D-TLSSERVE1) shipped — audit the rest.

Client gaps to audit: connection pooling/keep-alive; redirect policy control; cookie jar; multipart upload and form encoding; streaming request and response bodies (bounded memory); per-phase timeouts (connect/read/total); proxy support (env-standard); transparent gzip decompression; HTTP/2; typed URL input (consumes the core.url card).

Server gaps to audit: router with path params and wildcards; middleware chain; streaming responses and server-sent events; graceful shutdown; request size/time limits (safe defaults — I1); static file serving with range requests; access logging via core.log.

WebSocket client + server: likely its own module name (owner ballot). Done means: audit table plus shipped gaps with example servers/clients under golden tests; a realistic REST service example needs no third-party anything. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan: Finish D-HTTPDEPTH1/A on typed core.url/core.mime/core.net: Client/Server/Router/middleware, pooling/keepalive, redirects, cookies, forms/multipart, bounded streaming, phase timeouts, proxy, compression, TLS, SSE, limits, static ranges, logging, and graceful shutdown. Apply HTTP-CORE2/CLIENT2/SERVER2 and D-DEP-HTTP2=B exactly. HTTP/2 is a transport upgrade; WebSocket lives only in core.ws per D-WS1=B. Prove hostile protocol framing, smuggling/limits/disconnects, real client/server/browser interop, AOT/dev parity, examples/docs, and no facade.

cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 4. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.
cards.plan: After D-ENCXML-PROJECTION1 is ratified, implement only the selected public surface. If A wins, add xml.decode<T>, xml.decode_bytes<T>, root(document), expanded_name(node) returning the typed name view, attribute(element, name) returning the normalized String value, and content(element) returning ordered DataTree nodes, with the ballot signatures and namespace rules. If B wins, add the same decode entry points and tree-native helpers that return the exact XMLName and attribute DataTree nodes. If C wins, add the same decode entry points and Clark-string name and normalized-value attribute helpers. For every verdict, wire parser -> DataTree projection -> Codable through foundation, comptime, sema, and codegen; preserve source locations for parse errors; report projection failures as XMLError.Shape without a source location and with the deepest projected path; select attributes by local or Clark name, never prefix; cover scalar $text and struct @, child, $text, and $content mappings; add executable examples, goldens, targeted tests, and an independent review. Then resume the ungated XML conformance slices: official XML/Namespaces parser corpora, licensed C14N 1.1 and Exclusive 1.0 vectors, dual-limit and allocator matrices, byte identity, token editing, and fold/unfold hostile cases. Do not edit dirty sema, diagnostic, core_calls, docs-reference, or crypto paths until ownership clears.

It must inject one-byte reads, short writes, Interrupted retries, failure after N bytes, and close/drop observation into the exact codec engines. Run the same matrix over JSON, JSONL, CSV, and CBOR, then retain existing real-file and /dev/full probes. Prove terminal clones, accepted-prefix bytes, no duplicate writes, no background work, allocator ceilings, and whole hostile corpora. cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 9. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Review starts only after every producer closes. #710 first resolves its open XML projection ballot and finishes XML. #711 hostile-stream and #712 edition-surface work can proceed in parallel. #713 then proves whole/stream and execution-tier parity on those final engines. #714 pins all official and hostile corpora, examples, goldens, docs, and diagnostics against the shipped behavior. #715 reviews the clean integrated range after #710 through #714 close; it does not repair producer code or certify partial work. Preserve earlier accepted checkpoints as scoped history, not final proof. Reviewer procedure: 1. Record authority, base and tip, producer identities, reviewer identity/model/effort, target facts, and clean status. cards.title: JIT: reject gaps honestly without AOT fallback
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #688 criterion 2. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #688 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Authority is D-VERDICT-687-1. Default jet run uses JIT. jet build and jet run --release use AOT. A JIT gap is a compiler defect, not a fallback. Current dispatch violates that law. Default jet run enters run_compile_cmd and builds native Rust. Default jet dev constructs CraneliftBackend over AotFallbackBackend over InterpreterBackend. Hot swap and restart use the same ladder. CraneliftBackend delegates on a missing program or any JIT compile error. AotFallbackBackend compiles and runs AOT, then uses the interpreter when AOT is unavailable. Interpreter.rs also reruns an E0953 JIT result through AOT. That retry can duplicate effects. Explicit jet dev --interpret correctly uses InterpreterBackend and E2201. No E2211 source, registry row, snapshot, explain entry, or CLI test exists. Use this exact diagnostic copy. What: Jet JIT has a compiler gap for this checked program. Why: jet run uses the JIT lens and does not hide a JIT compiler gap by running AOT. Fix: run jet build <file> and the binary for now, then report E2211 with the detail below. Detail: JIT gap in {function}: {reason}. Attach the entry function span when available. Keep raw Rust and rustc text hidden. Return exit 101 because the exit table defines compiler defects as ICE. A watching dev session prints E2211, keeps the last good state, and continues. One-shot dev and default run exit 101. --try-anyway applies only to interpreter E2201 and never bypasses E2211. Implement in one order. First change api_debug try_resident, hot_swap, and restart from Option to Result and preserve unsupported host, lowering, safety, compilation, and panic reasons. Then make CraneliftBackend strict and remove its fallback generic. Delete AotFallbackBackend and its native subprocess runner after all product callers move. Keep InterpreterBackend only for explicit --interpret. Remove the E0953 AOT retry. Route default run to the same strict Cranelift backend. Keep build and run --release on CmdCompile AOT. Update watch, restart, and swap so a failed edit retains the last good runtime. Register E2211 under the JIT diagnostics area. Add the exact what, why, and fix row. Update the stale dev-loop prose. Add a rendered tests/dev/jit_gap.txt snapshot and generated error reference. Test supported JIT run, each gap class, unsupported host, no duplicate effects, watch recovery, one-shot exit 101, JSON, color, NO_COLOR, explain, default run, build, release run, and explicit interpreter. Re-run the #727 strict corpus gate. Do not add a daemon, alternate runner, new cache, or runtime AOT fallback.

cards.title: Script-speed run loop: cached re-run, jet dev signpost, start budget
cards.body:
Persona audit 2026-07-23: every `jet run` costs 12-14s, even when the file did not change. `jet dev` runs the same file in 4.7s, but `jet run` never mentions it. Python starts at once. The focused agent audit also measured an unchanged process example at 36.38s through the required development environment. This gap decides the script persona and blocks Jet from replacing Bash, Python, and Node for short agent tasks.

Work:
- An unchanged file re-runs from cache with no recompile.
- `jet run` prints one tip line when a compile is slow: point at `jet dev`.
- Measure and enforce cold/warm script budgets against matched Bash, Python, and Node tasks.

Rides #687/#688 (jet run = JIT lens) and #439 (watch engine). The self-host era work (#666/#669) is the long game; this card owns the Epoch 3 daily-driver feel.
cards.plan:
Amended 2026-07-24: two facts change this card. First, the 2026-07-24 environment fix (batch-pass rewrite of scripts/agent/clean-nix-tmp.sh) removed a multi-minute shellHook stall; the recorded no-op baseline (jet-env true 57.826 s, cold 13.905 s, warm 12.088 s) is invalid — re-measure all spans before enforcing any budget. Second, D-ONECORE1=A / D-LENS-RUN2=A (#776-#778) make default jet run tiered; the interpreter tier needs no Cranelift compile, which changes the cold-start calculus.
Resume when #778 lands the tiered run path and #439 exposes the shared invalidation service. Put warm artifact reuse at the tier boundary: cache compiled tier-1 modules keyed by exact source, dependency, compiler-build identity, target, capability, and configuration facts; a hit skips load, parse, check, lowering, and code generation with trace proof. Do not extend the AOT BuildCache path or add another runner, cache, watcher, or daemon. Measure spans separately: environment entry; compiler startup; load; parse; check; TIR lowering; tier-1 compile; artifact load; program time. Add the slow-run signpost only in the common run coordinator (once, stderr, TTY-aware, NO_COLOR/JSON suppressed). Benchmark matched no-op, file/JSON, and subprocess fixtures against Bash, Python, and Node; record machine facts, cold and warm medians, and tail latency; enforce the ratified budget only after the method and value exist.

cards.title: Anonymous union types: decide before the stdlib bakes casts in
cards.body:
Promotes the union half of idea b4eclxq. The any half is ALREADY DECIDED: D-ANY-JAI1 (syntax-decisions.md:169-172) ratified trait-bounded heterogeneous varargs and rejected a general Any top type. That rejection is law and is not reopened here.

The open question: does Jet ever get anonymous union types (Int | String), or do named enums stay the only union? Why now (lessons-learned, Go generics): the encoding/data/web wave (#296/#307/#706-#709) is baking APIs that need the answer, and a missing type capability fossilizes casts into a stdlib.

Ballot D-UNIONTYPE1 on this card picks. Implementation follows ratification.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-UNIONTYPE1=A as structural enum sugar, not a second sum mechanism. Add Type::Union with one canonicalizer that recursively flattens members, removes exact duplicates, and sorts by canonical source spelling; define parser precedence so T ? E1 | E2 places the union on the error side. Extend formatting, type traversal, equality/display, API snapshots, semantic index, and LSP to use that canonical form. In sema, allow only concrete closed member types, add implicit member-to-union widening at binding, argument, return, field, and error-propagation boundaries, and preserve exact union identity elsewhere. Extend union match heads to resolve an exact member type and feed the existing enum exhaustiveness and binding checks. Lower each canonical union to one deterministic compiler-generated enum emitted once per resolved union, with injection and match operations carried explicitly in TIR so codegen remains mechanical and native/web/dev agree. Extend Codable synthesis so each member encodes normally and decode selects a unique compatible wire shape; reject ambiguous or unsupported shapes in sema with registered UI diagnostics. Keep named-enum crossings explicit through ordinary match-based conversion functions and add no Any or cast escape. Update the syntax decision log and examples, regenerate grammar/tooling artifacts, bless snapshots, and run focused parser/formatter/sema/serde/golden plus AOT/dev/web parity checks.

cards.title: Browser debugging: source maps for the web target
cards.body:
Field audit TypeScript row: the browser is the runtime and feedback is live. Jet ships a web/canvas target, but devtools cannot step Jet lines.

Work: emit source maps for the JS/Wasm output so browser devtools show and step Jet source. The compiler already maps Jet lines to generated Rust for diagnostics (Source/Compiler.rs SourceMap) — extend that chain to the browser. Rides the web wave (#123, #701-#705).

Flip test: set a breakpoint on a Jet line in browser devtools and step.
cards.plan: 1. Reuse `TStmt::LineMarker` for web output. Do not add a second source-location model. 2. Add a std-only Source Map v3 encoder with stable source order. Use UTF-16 columns for JavaScript. 3. Record generated JavaScript positions before each emitted TIR statement. Emit `app.js.map` and its relative `sourceMappingURL`. 4. Compile Wasm with line data. Read rustc's Wasm line table after compilation. Join generated Rust lines to Jet lines through existing markers. 5. Emit Wasm byte-offset mappings in `app.wasm.map`. Put the relative map URL in the Wasm `sourceMappingURL` custom section. 6. Default, debug, and CI web builds include exact Jet bytes in `sourcesContent`. Release builds emit no maps or map references. 7. Use project-relative source names with `/` separators. Never emit absolute host paths. 8. Add both map files to build output, atomic dev swaps, static serving, and last-good rebuild behavior. 9. Reuse the current Chromium CDP harness. Prove Jet breakpoints and stepping in JavaScript and Wasm. 10. Run focused web tests and fresh review. If Wasm decoding needs a new tool or crate, stop and raise a dependency ballot.

cards.title: Toolchain telemetry and trust policy
cards.body:
Lessons-learned gap 2 (2026-07-23): Go's telemetry episode and Audacity show that even well-intentioned opt-out telemetry burns trust permanently. Nothing on the board mentions telemetry — deciding it implicitly by code later is the expensive path.

Ballot D-TELEMETRY1 on this card decides: opt-in only vs none at all, and exactly what jet/jetpack may send over the network (registry queries included).
cards.plan:
Implement ratified D-TELEMETRY1=A and D-REPORT-SEND1=A only. No new owner choices.

1. Inventory every jet/jetpack network path. Prove builds and ordinary commands never open telemetry, crash, or usage endpoints.
2. Keep registry/package traffic limited to what the user-requested operation needs (name, version constraint, protocol necessities).
3. Ship or harden `jet report` as a local inspectable bundle writer that prints the path. Do not ship `jet report --send` (D-REPORT-SEND1 amends the illustrative telemetry example).
4. Document the permanent zero-telemetry promise in owner-facing tooling docs.
5. Add regression tests that fail if a background usage/crash sender appears, and CLI tests for local report bundle creation without network send.

Proof: focused CLI/tooling tests + greps/audit of network call sites. No full suite required for this card alone.

cards.title: Bare bindings: retire the typed binding forms
cards.body: Binding grammar collapses to name :: value, name := value, name = value. The forms name: Type :: expr and name: Type := expr are removed as an immediate clean break — ordinary parse error, no teaching/retirement window. Types ride the value (Type.{ } heads, .new/.from_* calls); names carry types only in signatures and fields. Corpus migration: ~206 typed bindings rewrite mechanically.
cards.plan:
blockedBy: none

Authority: D-BIND-BARE1=A (ratified). Amends S1 / D-BIND4. Prerequisite feature: #780 universal Type.{ } heads (D-DOTCTOR3 shipped).

Goal: A binding is always bare. Keep only name :: value, name := value, and reassignment name = value. Delete name: Type :: expr and name: Type := expr. Immediate clean break — ordinary parse error, no teaching window.

## 1. Syntax authority
- Add the D-BIND-BARE1 entry in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs.
- Append the syntax-decisions.md log: bindings never carry types; types ride values or live on signatures and fields.
- Run jet devtools grammars.
- Update Source/LSP/Completion.rs snippets that still teach typed bindings.

## 2. Parser
Owned: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/bindings.rs (and formatter Statements.rs).
- Remove the typed :: and := binding productions.
- Keep name: Type on signatures, struct fields, and other non-binding positions.
- Old typed bindings become an ordinary parse error — no special retirement diagnostic.
- Formatter never emits typed binding forms.
- Editor grammars match the parser.

## 3. Sema
- Local bindings stop carrying a required annotation for emptiness, sized numbers, and similar cases; the value head from #780 supplies the type.
- Signatures and fields keep name: Type.
- Sweep binding helpers that assume Binding.ty is present for ordinary locals.

## 4. Corpus migration (~206)
- Mechanical rewrite: drop a redundant annotation when the value already self-types; otherwise lift the annotation’s type onto the value as a Type.{ } head or assertion.
- Touch examples/, tests/, and Jet sources under std as needed.
- Update docs/spec/spec.md binding bullets that still list typed forms.

## 5. Lowering / TIR
- No new runtime for bare bindings already supported.
- Confirm destructuring and other binding variants still parse after the grammar cut.

## 6. Diagnostics / UI snapshots (I4)
- Snapshot the ordinary parse error for retired typed forms.
- Re-bless any UI snapshots whose fix text still shows name: Type :: / :=.
- Hand uninit trigger changes to #782; do not leave a typed-binding-only uninit path.

## 7. Acceptance tests
- Corpus grep: zero live name: Type :: / name: Type := forms in .jet sources (comments that teach the retirement are fine).
- Example goldens and formatter round-trips green.
- scripts/agent/jet-env scoped tests + jet run on touched examples.

cards.plan:
## Outcome

Ship **Native debugger: DAP framing and state-machine core** as a complete slice. Every behavior in the title, body, and ratified decisions is required.

## Work

1. Apply these ratified decisions: D-DBG-DAP1=A, D-DBG-NATIVE1=A, D-DBG-AUTH1=B, D-DBG-EDITOR1=A, D-DBG-DIAG1=A.
2. Start with crates/jet-debug/src/Dap.rs, crates/jet-debug/src/Native.rs, crates/jet-debug/src/Inferior.rs, crates/jet-debug/src/LineMap.rs, crates/jet-debug/src/lib.rs, tests/debug.rs, editors/vscode/extension.js, editors/vscode/package.json, editors/vscode/README.md, editors/zed/wasm-src/src/lib.rs, editors/zed/languages/jet/config.toml, editors/zed/README.md, docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md, docs/spec/diagnostics.md. Own only these paths and direct callers or tests found by the trace.
3. Trace the public entry point through the production model to the observable result.
4. Map each named behavior to implementation and proof before writing.
5. Integrate the debugger with Jet source, semantic types, runtime state, and supported native backends without exposing generated Rust internals.
6. Stale binaries, optimized-away values, process exit, attach denial, signal or exception storms, and disconnect terminate cleanly with an honest state.
7. Update affected docs, examples, diagnostics, goldens, and audit output.

## Proof

Run focused unit, integration, and example checks for this slice. Exercise the real production path and its main failure case. A stub, canned result, mock-only path, or skipped check does not count. Full-suite proof belongs to Epoch 10 closeout.

## Scope

Do not absorb sibling cards or create a second mechanism. Record any newly found owner choice as a Tower ballot before code.

Codegen: TStmt::LineMarker + emit_bundle_dbg/compile_for_debug emit `// jet:line N` markers gated by cx.debug_linemap (off by default — zero effect on normal builds, golden tests, or the JIT tier; confirmed via full test suite + `cargo test --workspace` diffing). New Source/Debug/{LineMap,Inferior,Native,Dap}.rs. `jet debug` auto-dispatches interpreter vs native via the SAME E2203 boundary scan (needs_native) — one command, one meaning (I8); `--dap` forces native for editor launch; `--raw-frames` (D-DBG2) shows raw Rust file:line. Reuses the exact ratified (jet) vocabulary (D-DBG3) over both backends. Live-lldb verification surfaced and fixed THREE real bugs a docs-only implementation would have shipped broken: (1) lldb never re-prints a bare prompt over a pipe (echoes command instead) — naive prompt-wait hangs forever, fixed with a sentinel-command read loop; (2) a resume command's own stop banner is asynchronous and can lose a race to the NEXT command's reply — fixed by always deriving position from a synchronous follow-up `bt`, never the resume's own text; (3) the debuggee inherits lldb's stdout by default, so a Jet `print()` can tear a control-channel sentinel in half — fixed by redirecting debuggee stdout/stderr to temp files via `settings set target.output/error-path` and draining them into the transcript. Also loads rustc's own Rust pretty-printer (lldb_lookup.py + lldb_commands, same two files rust-lldb loads) so String/&str locals render as `"text"` instead of raw allocator internals. Tests: 12 new unit tests (LineMap/Inferior, no lldb needed) + tests/debug_native.rs (5 tests, gated on lldb presence like tests/observe.rs gates on rustc — skips clean without it). questions.text: What is the interplay with out idea for switft style unified protocol for both server & client to prevent drift?
questions.answer: The Swift insight is the `Responder` (or `Handler`) protocol pattern used by Vapor/Hummingbird/NIO: a single trait `trait Handler { fn handle(req: Request) -> Response }` becomes the composition unit for both the server's routing stack and the client's interceptor stack. Because both sides speak the same `Request`/`Response` types, they can never drift — any middleware that works on the server (auth, logging, retry) is structurally identical to a client-side interceptor. The plan for c164 already captures this: D-HTTPLIB2=B (split client/server modules) shares core types, and D-HTTPLIB1=A (function-first mux) is the routing side. The missing piece to make it Swift-unified is an explicit `Handler` trait in `core.http` that both the client and server implement. Concretely: the client IS a handler (wraps the network connection); the mux IS a handler (dispatches to route handlers); middleware wraps one handler with another. Testing then becomes free — inject a `MockHandler` anywhere in the chain. This should be a first-class design constraint in the c164 plan, not a separate decision. Agents writing the HTTP library plan should define `core.http.Handler` as the primary abstraction before splitting into client vs. server API docs.

cards.plan:
Complete only this slice; do not absorb sibling scope. Preserve these parent constraints where they apply:
Use D-FFI-UNIFY1=A as one foreign-namespace architecture: generated typed stubs and binders feed a common checked FFI boundary, while each language adapter owns transport details. Finish canonical descriptor, ownership/error/layout conversion, safe-vs-#Unsafe boundary, build/cache/provenance, package provider integration, and per-language capability reporting. Reconcile Python A, external provider A, existing C/Rust/npm/JS/Swift law, and active polyglot phase cards. video-mine evidence (2026-08-12): C FFI probe on the script tier — the binder emits clean typed #Bindgen modules (jet inspect bind works), but jet run fails E0956 with self-contradictory fix text and jet run --release fails E3201 because the sibling .c is not compiled. Diagnostic copy fixes are #1900; interpreter-tier ExternCall per I9 stays this card's architecture.

Evidence target from the Bun Zig-to-Rust port (mined 2026-08-10, youtu.be/iu_ALBDtoHo): Bun's Rust codebase carries about 4,000 permanent unsafe blocks, because every C and C++ call crosses FFI with unsafe and hand-written binding code. Ghostty's author cites C interoperability as the reason he kept Zig over Rust.

D-FFI-UNIFY1 already says generated bindings are safe wrappers by construction, and only calls outside a binding need #Unsafe. That law is right; this note records the outcome to hold it to. A C-heavy Jet program must need no user-written #Unsafe per foreign call, and the unsafe count must not scale with the number of foreign calls.

Backend-cleanup evidence for the shared binder architecture. crates/jet-pkg-model declares BindError 17 times, once per language binder: Ada, Cobol, Com, Cpp, Dart, DotNet, Fortran, Go, Java, Lua, Pascal, Perl, Php, PowerShell, R, Ruby and Tcl. Fourteen are the same four variants (Source, ToolMissing, ToolFailed, IO) spelled by hand; ComBind adds UnsupportedHost. The unified descriptor should own one BindError so a binder failure reads the same whichever language raised it. Recorded here rather than as a new card, per the no-duplicate rule.
