cards.title: Bootstrap readiness gate: dogfood portfolio + memory-model soundness campaign
cards.body:
OWNER AUTHORIZATION (latest direct instruction): begin the staged Jet-authored compiler port after Pip fixes known critical bootstrap/compiler issues. Keep Rust emission and rustc/LLVM/Cranelift. Create a clear source checkpoint at the transition. The Rust-hosted compiler remains production/reference until cutover. This card now gates production cutover and broader readiness, not the start of all port development. No readiness criterion is waived or marked met by authorization. Critical checkpoint/start work is homed on #3575.

Readiness evidence remains: (1) real dogfood portfolio and cold-read reviews; (2) memory-model v5 soundness campaign; (3) ratified-surface consistency; (4) owner readiness sign-off before production cutover.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Settle what the bootstrap readiness gate means now that the owner direction of 2026-09-28 makes the self-hosted compiler (Compiler/) the primary implementation and archives the Rust compiler. Then prove whatever evidence streams remain.

## Current state
- Earlier owner authorization started the staged Jet compiler port and kept Rust emission and rustc/LLVM/Cranelift. It made this card the gate for production cutover and broader readiness, not for the start of porting. #3575 (checkpoint and port start) is done.
- There are four evidence streams: (1) the dogfood portfolio with cold-read reviews; (2) the memory-model v5 soundness campaign with zero reachable UB from safe Jet; (3) a ratified-surface sweep; (4) owner sign-off.
- Criterion 3 still names `Syntax.rs` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs`). `node Tools/agent/lexical-ledger.mjs --check` also renders from `Syntax.rs` into `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`. The Jet lexer and parser tables live in `Compiler/JetLexer/Source/Lexer/Tokens.jet` and `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/*.jet`.
- The soundness oracle work is on #3645 (deciding, P0). The dogfood campaign is #2386 (ready).

## Owner question (open)
Does the 2026-09-28 direction count as the readiness sign-off? The options:
- (A) Yes. Record criterion 4 as met by that direction, retarget criterion 3 to the Compiler/ syntax tables, and keep criteria 1 and 2 as post-cutover quality gates.
- (B) No. A separate readiness ballot is still required.
- (C) Close #217 and move criteria 1 and 2 onto #3645 and #2386.

The recommendation is A, and this plan is written for A.

## Changes (option A)
1. Record the 2026-09-28 direction in the card log as the criterion-4 outcome, quoting it.
2. Retarget criterion 3 so that every user-typeable surface in `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md` matches the Jet lexer and parser (`Compiler/JetLexer`, `Compiler/JetParser`) at the gate revision. Point `Tools/agent/lexical-ledger.mjs` at the Jet token table as its source. That port belongs to the front-end batch; if it grows, file it as a separate card. Extend `tests/syntax_reconciliation.rs` so it fails on drift. The new spellings (`T?`, `-> T E!`, `(A | B)!`, `&x.push()`, `^x.seal()`, `prep`, `<: … :>`) are all in scope.
3. Criterion 2 is proven by #3645's soundness campaign artifacts, linked here. Criterion 1 is proven by #2386's reviewed portfolio (reviewer and date per verdict). This card only links and verifies them.

## Proof
- `node Tools/agent/lexical-ledger.mjs --check` exits 0 with the Jet token table as its source.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test syntax_reconciliation`: passes with an empty drift list.
- The card log links #3645's committed soundness artifacts and #2386's review records.

## Batch
batch-measure: this is a gate that collects evidence. The only code touched (the ledger source switch) is small and can go with batch-jetc-front if needed.

## Dependencies
- #3645 (soundness campaign; criterion 2).
- #2386 (dogfood portfolio; criterion 1).
- The owner answer to the question above.

cards.title: Self-hosting: functional Jet compiler
cards.body: Owner-directed full functional Rust-to-Jet compiler port. Jet owns loading, lexing, parsing, checking, compile-time evaluation, IR transformations, emission and compiler orchestration. Keep Rust alongside as bootstrap/reference until Jet is proven; approved native backend and OS adapters may remain, but Rust compiler semantic callbacks do not satisfy self-hosting. Substantial disjoint port batches precede wider parity and self-compilation suites; current-language validity is required during the port. Criterion 8 supersedes the historical inventory-only scope and completion exception. Historical inventory evidence and linked ratified decisions remain preserved.
cards.plan:
## Goal
A functional self-hosted Jet compiler. Jet owns loading, lexing, parsing, checking, compile-time evaluation, IR transformations, emission and orchestration. It compiles Jet programs and its own sources through the intended path, with no Rust compiler semantic callback after stage zero. Rust remains bootstrap and reference, and keeps only the retained host boundary (runtime, jet-rt, JIT/Cranelift adapters, MIR validation, rustc emission, CLI host, LSP, process/filesystem).

## Current state
- Trees exist for every phase: `Compiler/{JetLexer,JetParser,JetAst,JetSema,JetCodegen,JetEval,JetOptimizer,JetFoundation,JetDriver}`. `Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list` (236 lines) is the single assembly order. `assemble.mjs` builds one unit under `~/.cache/jet-luna/compiler-bootstrap/project`, and `check.sh` runs `jet check` on it with a 120 s timeout.
- No route executes the Jet compiler yet (log 2026-09-28). The lexer slice fails type-check (#3581: 42 problems). The full front-slice `jet check` was OOM-killed at 8 GB after 39 minutes. `Compiler/Bootstrap/Host` had 43 compile errors (Native.rs, NativeAdapter.rs, Runner.rs).
- Syntax cutover D-TYPE-SUFFIX1, D-PREP-BRANCH1/FN1 and D-FENCE2 was applied across 839 files (2026-09-28). All new Jet code uses the new spelling.
- Criteria 1-7 are met (the inventory slice). Criteria 8-12 are open: functional, layout, parity, performance, source quality.

## Changes (owner sequencing, explicit)
1. Build-out: finish every missing Jet implementation body (loading, lexing, parsing, checking, comptime evaluation including `fn build(b: BuildContext) -> BuildPlan` in `Compiler/JetDriver` and `BodyComptime.jet`, IR transforms, emission, orchestration). Find the missing bodies from current code, not inventories. No native integration, cleanup, bug fixing or optimization in this phase.
2. Integrate: make the assembled unit pass `jet check` inside the memory scope (the check's cost is its own defect if it exceeds it). Fix `Compiler/Bootstrap/Host`. Wire `Pipeline.jet` (load, parse, sema, MIR, emit, with failed-stage reporting) and `CompilerQueries.jet` behind the Rust CLI host. Then run current-language validity checks, focused functional, tier, self-compilation and differential checks against the Rust reference, with root fixes.
3. Merged slice requirements that stay in force. Lexer parity (#671): tokens, payloads including float bits, spans, synthetic terminators, ordered diagnostics, and a fixed-seed fuzz with zero divergence; no second keyword table (I7). Parser/AST (#809), sema/TIR (#810, #811), foundation registry and source primitives (#808), comptime/build (#812, with E3501/E3521, contained panics and no Rust-evaluator fallback), driver/CLI (#813: remove each crates/jet-driver path once its JetDriver replacement passes), stage0-to-stage1 receipt via `Compiler/Bootstrap/BuildIdentity.rs` (#814).
4. Optimize, then apply the strict Jet/Rust performance gate (criterion 11: normalized cost below 1.00 per required cell).
5. Layout (criterion 9): responsibility-named modules. Remove backups and duplicates with no compatibility wrappers.

## Proof
- The added criterion.
- `cargo test --test selfhost_parser`, `cargo test --test selfhost_terminators` and `cargo test --test selfhost_host_boundary` pass.
- A differential run over the valid/invalid corpora shows zero mismatches.
- Self-compilation of `Compiler/` through the generated Runner succeeds and fails when the Jet entry is bypassed.
- Heavy runs use one foreground scope: MemoryHigh=8G, MemoryMax=12G, MemorySwapMax=0, TasksMax=64, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1, RUST_TEST_THREADS=1, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-driver`: this is the self-host harness and orchestration umbrella.

## Dependencies
None open (#3575 is done). Main owns the serial stream: one bounded worker at a time, all commands through jet-env, no worker proof loops.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.files and Path — file I/O parity with pathlib/Go os/Rust fs
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Python pathlib ergonomics, Go os robustness, Rust std::fs safety. Card #58 (path objects, atomic write, dir-walk) is done — first verify what actually shipped vs docs/reference/core-library.md (the doc shows no walk/glob/metadata), then close the residual gaps so core.files is a strict superset of the bar.

Gaps to audit and close: file metadata (size, mtime, created, permissions, file type) as a typed Stat value; create_dir_all / remove_dir / remove_all; glob patterns and recursive walk with entry filtering; symlink create/read/detect and hardlinks; temp files and temp dirs with RAII cleanup; atomic write (verify #58); advisory file locking; canonicalize/absolute; copy_dir tree; seek/offset reads and byte-stream (non-line) buffered readers/writers; fsync/flush-to-disk; filesystem watch (notify events) — watch may deserve its own module name (ballot).

Done means: every gap either ships with example + golden test, or is recorded as an owner-declined non-goal in the stdlib map. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan: Current source already ships D-FSOPS1, D-FSWATCH1, and the owners D-WATCH-SCOPE1 comment: core.watcher owns file, process, and port handles; core.event scopes own callbacks; core.files/core.path own filesystem operations. Do not rebuild or rename this surface. Remaining closure is proof and truth reconciliation. First run the existing files_depth and watcher goldens plus corelib, parity, and path_durability tests against the production prelude. Verify the watcher example exercises recursive file changes, process exit, port readiness, WatchSet composition, scoped callbacks, cancellation/drop, and documented std-only polling fidelity without shell polling or silent platform claims. Obtain native Windows evidence for lexical path normalization and write_atomic replacement/durability already met on Linux; preserve collision-safe temp cleanup and permission behavior. Audit docs/reference/core-library.md and syntax-decisions against the actual core.watcher names and Event callback law. If any behavior is missing, repair the single existing implementation in FsIoEnvOsTesting.rs and ReactiveEventWatch.rs; add no alias, module, dependency, or new ballot. A different reviewer validates native evidence and every remaining criterion before closure.

log.text: Closed from integrated criteria evidence: lexical Path and atomic write proofs verified; unified watcher file/process/port example and focused tests verified; D-CORE-TREE1 reconciliation recorded core.files plus prelude Path methods, with no stale core.path target.

Timeline audit 2026-08-10: cross-epoch conflict with two ratified e3 rulings, flagged not rescoped, because this card is in build. The plan says "core.files/core.path own filesystem operations. Do not rebuild or rename this surface", and sizes the work at 52 gaps in core.files and 6 in core.path. Two later rulings move that surface. D-CORE-PATH1=A (card #1577, ratified 2026-08-06) makes Path a prelude type with methods and states that "the core.path free functions are deleted because the methods replace them". D-CORE-TREE1=A (card #1574) re-homes the Core namespaces. Every free function added here under the old shape is deleted by #1577. Before adding a new core.path free function, read D-CORE-PATH1 and add the method instead. Filesystem operations under core.files are not affected the same way.

cards.body:
Integration closeout only. Broad implementation remains on existing focused child cards. This card owns reconciliation of their evidence and removal of duplicate paths.

Original context:
Owner hit this live (2026-07-09): `big :: BigInt(100)` in jet repl fails with E0956 "calling BigInt can't run at compile time yet", while examples/features/text/bigint.jet (D-BIGINT1=A, golden) runs fine AOT. The REPL executes through the comptime interpreter (tier-0), so every builtin the AOT backend supports but comptime doesn't is a user-visible parity break — R12 requires JIT/dev/REPL parity through the same executable TIR.

Scope:
1. Implement BigInt construction + arithmetic + to_string in the comptime interpreter (crates/jet-comptime; CtValue may need a BigInt variant — check how AOT lowers it first).
2. Audit: enumerate every builtin/Core call AOT supports vs the comptime whitelist; produce the parity matrix as a test (ui or dedicated tests/parity.rs) so new builtins can't ship AOT-only. E0956 sites are the search key.
3. Each fixed gap needs a repl transcript test; keep E0956 wording for genuinely impossible-at-comptime effects only.

Repro: printf 'big :: BigInt(100)\n:quit\n' | target/debug/jet repl

questions.text:
How substantial is the win vs the additional surface for option C? Does this make things unsafe or less ergonomic with a worse DX to have option C? If the beneficial cases of option A are notably less frequent than the benefit we would get in frequency/impact of c, then c maybe better even if it allows an additional surface. 

Maybe come up with a better hybrid no compromises way to handle this that gives us the best of both worlds at the expense of additional work up front on our end.
questions.answer: General need is substantial; option C specific win is modest. It preserves unchanged append and count callbacks, but only remains memory-safe through private copies plus rejected aliases and unsupported operations. Hidden copy cost and type-specific merge, ordering, conflict, and failure laws still make DX less predictable. No honest Jet usage frequency data exists; established parallel APIs show aggregation is common, not that implicit capture merging is. Updated ballot adds recommended D: reject ordinary mutable captures, add ordered par_partition for common splits, and replace the serial par_fold prototype with a truly parallel seed, step, and merge reducer. This covers beginner and expert cases without races, silent serialization, or guessed merges. Custom reducers stay explicit; diagnostics can show the equivalent reducer shape. questions.text: This ballot makes absolutely no sense to me. I have no idea what this means or what it is. Please rework in plain language to be more clearly understandable
questions.answer:
Rewritten in plain language, in place — the ballot text you saw is replaced.

What it decides: a profile merges several packages into one file tree (same engine for `jet profile`, JetOS systems, and user environments). Sometimes two packages both install a file at the same path — say two editors both install `bin/editor`. Identical files and folders merge automatically; a file-vs-folder clash always fails. This ballot only decides the remaining case: two different files at the same path.

The recommended option (A): the build fails, names both packages and their content hashes, and you add one line to the profile — `"bin/editor": packages.helix` — picking the winner for that exact path. If a later upgrade changes either contender, the old pick is refused and you review again. Option B has no pick mechanism (you must drop or rebuild a package). Option C lets list order decide silently.

cards.title: Service runtime: topology, supervision, endpoints, and mailboxes
cards.body:
Single-task slice extracted from former #444 umbrella. This card owns only: Service runtime: topology, supervision, endpoints, and mailboxes. Sibling scope lives on separate successor cards.

Context only; it does not add sibling scope:
Build a production service model over the ratified task/group/channel substrate (D-CONC-GROUP1, D-CONC-CHAN1, D-CONC-SCHED1 — "TaskGroup" and its channel-builder-chain vocabulary are superseded), distinct from Jetpack external-process supervision. Scope: typed endpoints/mailboxes, bounded backpressure, supervision/restart escalation, cancellation/drain, delivery/retry/idempotency, identity/discovery, authenticated clusters, partitions, durable state policy, placement, rolling generation handoff, rollback, observability, and chaos proof. No actor syntax or second scheduler. Owner decisions select topology and distributed semantics. docs/proposals/concurrency-work-is-a-value.md places the service plane in Phase C, after the concurrency substrate's Phase A (machinery) and Phase B (surface) land; this card follows that sequencing.
cards.plan:
## Reopen finding

The closure reused two golden examples over an in-memory service catalog; that does not prove the named group/channel runtime, durable state, cluster, migration, or chaos behavior.

## Outcome

Complete **Service runtime: topology, supervision, endpoints, and mailboxes** to the intent of the title, body, and current ratified law. Apply D-SERVICE1=D, D-SERVICE-DELIVERY1=D, D-SERVICE-STATE1=D, D-SERVICE-WORKFLOW1=D, D-SERVICE-IDENTITY1=D, D-SERVICE-UPGRADE1=D on top of the concurrency substrate ratified 2026-08-06: D-CONC-SCHED1 (typed schedule data, one job vocabulary, service plane on the group substrate — "a supervisor is a task that owns a group; a restart rule is data on that group, no new mechanism"), D-CONC-GROUP1 (TaskGroup is renamed Group; a group may be named and passed in any borrow position, never stored), D-CONC-UNIT1 (task lifecycle is a typestate row plus one join obligation, not ad-hoc fields), D-CONC-JOIN1 (a dropped bound task handle is a compile error — join, use its result, or detach), D-CONC-OUTCOME1 (task result and control state are the typed TaskOutcome/TaskStatus enums, not strings), D-CONC-CROSS1 (one crossing-safety plane and error family for every endpoint/mailbox boundary). Do not invent new syntax or policy beyond these; raise a ballot for any new owner choice.

## Ratified vocabulary this card must use

- Named/passed spawn scope is Group, not TaskGroup. crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/TaskGroup.rs and crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/ServicesLite.rs still say TaskGroup; the rename itself belongs to the concurrency slate's Phase B surface migration, not this card, but new code this card writes targets Group and any TaskGroup call sites this card must touch migrate in the same change if the rename has already landed.
- Supervisor restart decisions and endpoint/mailbox diagnostics read TaskOutcome/TaskStatus (D-CONC-OUTCOME1); never trace()/exception() strings.
- Every task handle a supervisor or worker holds is joined, awaited for its result, or explicitly detached (D-CONC-JOIN1); no silent drop.
- Endpoint/mailbox crossing checks report through the one crossing-safety error family (D-CONC-CROSS1); do not add a sixth ad-hoc sendability checker.

## Work

1. Trace the public entry point through the production implementation and map every named behavior (sema-known service tree, typed builders, endpoint types, cancellation/drain, supervisor-owned child groups with typed restart budget and escalation, one-way deployment projection) to source and proof.
2. Implement the named service-runtime slice through real groups, channels, typed endpoints, durable adapters, and lifecycle paths. An in-memory catalog or display-only simulator does not satisfy the card.
3. Backpressure, cancellation, duplicate delivery, crash/restart, corrupt state, partition, authentication failure, migration failure, rollback, and drain preserve safety and bounded recovery for the named slice.
4. Remove or correct any false claim, fallback, duplicate mechanism, stale criterion, or gap parking owned by this slice, including any lingering "taskgroup" or string-outcome wording in this slice's own docs and examples.
5. Update affected docs, examples (examples/features/tooling/service_tree.jet, service_runtime.jet, service_authority.jet), diagnostics, goldens, and audit output.

## Not building

No actor syntax, no second scheduler, no unbounded mailboxes, no ambient authority. No parallel restart-tracking mechanism outside the D-CONC-UNIT1 typestate row. No string-keyed outcome checks. Check whether the concurrency slate's Phase B surface (tracked on card #1505) has landed before writing new group/channel-facing code; do not write new code against the pre-rethink TaskGroup/channel-builder-chain API once that surface ships.

## Proof

Targeted success and failure checks drive the production runtime, including restart or partition where relevant, and prove default `jet run` plus AOT parity; interpreter ambient uses the same Prelude symbol when reached. Use focused checks for this card. Full-suite proof runs once at the epoch closeout.

## Scope

Keep the card bounded to its named slice and direct production seams. A reviewer will verify the completed card through Tower.

## Goal
Finish the COM/VBA slice under D-FFI-COM1=A: Windows-gated `com.*`, typed stubs generated from an installed or file-backed type library, and the audited `#Unsafe` IDispatch escape for components without a type library. The remaining work is proving the real Windows success path, packaging and docs.

## Current state
- The binder is `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/ComBind.rs`. Its unit tests (`:1000-1116`) cover schema parsing, typed stubs, dual interfaces, duplicate-name rejection, winegcc cross-compile and the non-Windows gate.
- `tests/ffi_com.rs:13` `com_example_is_rejected_before_binding_on_non_windows` is non-Windows only. No Windows success test exists yet.
- Example: `Examples/features/lowlevel/polyglot_com/{run.jet, office_fixture.idl}`. Tier map: VBA/COM row at `Docs/spec/reference/migration-tier-map.md:27`.
- Criteria 3, 4 and 6 are verified. Criteria 1, 2 and 5 need a Windows host (e13 cross-platform).
- The old plan's `examples/…` and `docs/…` paths are stale and are now `Examples/` and `Docs/`.
- The binder is not yet ported to Jetpack. That belongs to the Jetpack port (#3590 family), not this card.

## Changes (on a Windows host)
1. `tests/ffi_com.rs`: add `#[cfg(windows)] com_office_fixture_binds_and_runs_on_windows`. Register `office_fixture.idl` as a file-backed type library, run `jet inspect bind com`, commit the generated `com.*` stubs, run `Examples/features/lowlevel/polyglot_com/run.jet`, and compare with its golden.
2. Add a real Office automation case (for example `Excel.Application` workbook open/read) when Office is installed. Otherwise report it as unavailable, never as a pass.
3. Cover the dynamic IDispatch path without a type library, which requires `#Unsafe`. The same test must show that omitting `#Unsafe` gives the registered diagnostic.
4. Fix whatever the Windows run exposes in `ComBind.rs` / the `FFI.rs` seam. Update the VBA/COM tier-map row, the example golden and diagnostics only from that evidence.

## Proof
- On Windows: `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ffi_com` passes, including `com_office_fixture_binds_and_runs_on_windows`.
- `jet run Examples/features/lowlevel/polyglot_com/run.jet` matches its golden against the fixture type library. The Office case is recorded as pass or unavailable.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cffi_native_matrix` stays green.

## Batch
`batch-deferred`: e13 cross-platform work that needs a Windows host.

## Dependencies
A Windows host with the Office/COM fixture (an environment prerequisite, not a card).

cards.body:
Moved from Epoch 3 by owner instruction (2026-08-01): Package-graph depth that depends on Epoch 4 metaprogramming belongs here, not as an E3 umbrella closeout.

Integration closeout for language-shape Package/Config graph depth once E4 build/reflection foundations land. Child cards still own individual laws; this card reconciles evidence and removes duplicate Package authorities.

Do not invent a parallel Package mechanism (I8). Syntax.rs + syntax-decisions.md remain classification authority for user-typeable forms already shipped in E3.
cards.plan:
## Reopen finding

Workspace execution grants root CLI authority to every member and unions member grants, violating the ratified rule that dependencies receive no Tier-2 authority unless explicitly named; the integration closeout is therefore false.

## Outcome

Complete **Language-shape Package-graph depth closeout (from E3 #560)** to the intent of the title, body, and current ratified law. Do not invent new syntax or policy; raise a ballot for any new owner choice.

## Work

1. Trace the public entry point through the production implementation and map every named behavior to source and proof.
2. Enforce unit-local entry selection and explicit package/workspace/dependency grant provenance in the existing driver layer, while keeping the root facade thin.
3. Unlisted dependency authority, grant escalation, cycles, outside-root paths, read/write failure, and stale computed facts reject before effects with the correct registered diagnostic and exact UI snapshot.
4. Remove or correct any false claim, fallback, duplicate mechanism, stale criterion, or gap parking owned by this slice.
5. Update affected docs, examples, diagnostics, goldens, and audit output.

## Proof

Focused multi-member workspace tests prove grant non-inheritance, explicit dependency grants, order, root-layer boundaries, diagnostic snapshots, and rollback of failed builds. Use focused checks for this card. Full-suite proof runs once at the epoch closeout.

## Scope

Keep the card bounded to its named slice and direct production seams. A reviewer will verify the completed card through Tower.

questions.text: Practically speaking what is the difference in performance between these options? I like the sound of universal in option a and run/dev commands already use cranelift, so what is the real benefit list at the end of the day in plain language?
questions.answer:
Measured today on this machine, one shell, warm toolchain, examples/features/basics/fizzbuzz.jet:

- `jet check` (all of Jet's own checking: parse, types, ownership): 0.007s.
- `jet build` (today's path: generate Rust text, rustc compiles it, link): about 12s cold, 11s warm.
- Even hello.jet pays about 11.7s through that path.

So nearly all of the wait for a binary is rustc re-checking code the Jet front end already proved, plus LLVM work a debug artifact does not need. The wait grows with program size roughly the way cargo build waits do.

One measured correction to the premise: the resident Cranelift engine currently serves `jet dev` and `jet serve` hot-swaps. Plain `jet run` still rides the rustc path today. That is why hello.jet takes 11.7 seconds to run once.

What each option means in practice:

Option A (rustc opt-level 0). The debug binary keeps the full current path with optimization turned off. That saves some LLVM time. It still pays Rust text generation, rustc parsing, type-checking, borrow-checking, codegen, and linking. Expect waits like cargo's debug builds, forever.

Option B (Cranelift). The same checked program lowers straight from Jet's internal form (TIR) to object code, then links. No Rust text, no rustc. Cranelift is built for exactly this; it recompiles programs between dev hot-swaps in well under a second. A debug binary lands at roughly check time plus link time. The 12 seconds above collapses to about a second, and the gap widens as programs grow.

Reference point: Rust's own Cranelift backend (rustc_codegen_cranelift) cuts debug build times by about a third while still paying Rust's full front end every build. Jet under B skips that front end entirely, so Jet's saving is much larger than Rust's third.

On "universal": option B keeps it. A target Cranelift cannot emit for automatically uses option A's exact path, and `jet explain build` names which backend ran and why. Behavior is identical either way: same checked TIR, same R12 differential tests, same diagnostics. Only the wait changes.

Bottom line. A means one backend everywhere, and every debug build waits on rustc. B means the dev-loop engine also produces your debug binaries on mainstream targets (x86-64 and aarch64 Linux, macOS, Windows), with A's exact path as the automatic, named fallback everywhere else.

cards.title: TIR spec freeze — the lens contract for self-hosting
cards.body: R12 and D-VERDICT-666-1 require exactly two feature-identical lenses: JIT and optimized AOT, both consuming one executable TIR. Self-hosting changes the front end that produces TIR; it does not add a third consumer or lens. This card records and machine-enforces that internal contract from canonical source before port work begins, without a serialized schema or speculative version framework.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Freeze the semantic-core TIR contract with the self-hosted source as canon. One TIR is consumed exhaustively by every engine (R12, D-ONECORE1=A, D-TIER-ONEIR1, D-TIER-FORM1), so a new node cannot land without every consumer handling it. No serialization, version tag or new lens.

## Current state
- `Docs/spec/tir.md` (86 lines) exists. Lines 5-8 still name `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs` as the current implementation and call `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet` a staged port.
- Canonical Jet types: `TExprKind` (`TIR.jet:468`) and `TStmt`, with walkers such as `tir_stmt_list_children` (`TIR.jet:2279`).
- Consumers in Jet: TIR-to-MIR lowering in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/` (`Statements.jet` TStmt match near :1907, `Expressions.jet`) and the TIR walkers in `Compiler/JetSema`. Correction to the earlier retarget text: `Compiler/JetEval` evaluates MIR (`MirType`/`MirProgram` throughout `Evaluator.jet`), not TIR. The interpreter reference therefore consumes MIR lowered from the one TIR, and TIR exhaustiveness is enforced at the codegen lowering.
- Criterion 1 (owner reopens #217) is satisfied in substance. The owner authorized the port on 2026-09-25, and #217 now gates only production cutover readiness.

## Changes
1. `Docs/spec/tir.md`: name `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet` as canonical and link to it without copying the variant list. State totality, sema ownership, lowering and consumer laws. State that R12 means one semantic-core TIR lowered to one MIR for the interpreter reference, Cranelift run/dev, LLVM-backed AOT via Rust emission and applicable web. Keep the `TFactChannel` (#2301) note. Update the matching `architecture.md` R12 text.
2. `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/{Expressions,Statements}.jet` and the `Compiler/JetSema` TIR walkers: remove every `else ->` arm in a match over `TExprKind`, `TStmt` or `THandleOp`, and list each variant explicitly. The same applies to `Compiler/JetEval` over `MirOperation`.
3. Add `tests/tir_contract.rs` with one test that runs a mutation probe: it appends a dummy `TExprKind` variant to a scratch copy of the assembled unit and asserts that `jet check` reports a non-exhaustive match in each consumer.
4. Main: replace criterion 1 with the authorization note. No serialization, versioning, migration layer or duplicate schema.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test tir_contract -- new_texpr_variant_fails_every_consumer` passes.
- Jet slice check: `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` reports no diagnostic in `Compiler/JetCodegen` or `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR`.
- `Docs/spec/tir.md` links to the canonical file and restates no variants.

None open. #217 is stale as a blocker (see Current state).

cards.plan:
## Goal
Map the six compile-speed bets to the self-hosted compiler (`Compiler/`), and extend the existing checked corpus and timing machinery with self-host size tiers and stage identities. No second architecture document, runner or performance gate. The plan follows triage option B (retarget to `Compiler/`); see the owner note below.

## Current state
- The compiler-speed reference is `Docs/spec/reference/compiler-speed.md`. `docs/plans/compiler-speed.md` and `crates/jet-driver/src/PhaseTiming.rs` are historical.
- The owned paths in the old plan are archived Rust: `crates/jet-sema`, `crates/jet-queries/src/lib.rs`, `crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs`. Their self-host equivalents are `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/{Pipeline.jet,CompilerQueries.jet}`, `Compiler/JetSema` (sema-only verification), `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet` (one TIR, #668) and `Compiler/JetOptimizer`.
- The existing harness is `Source/CmdPerf.rs` plus `Tools/perf/` (`dashboard.sh`, `ci-perf-check.sh`, `corpus.tsv`). The old `tools/perf` path is stale.
- #1023 (checked corpus and phase timing) and #666 are done. #217 now gates only production cutover; the owner authorized the port on 2026-09-25, so #217 is not a gate here. #668 (TIR freeze) is ready. D-INCR-UNIT1 is not ratified.

1. `Docs/spec/reference/compiler-speed.md`: a current-source table mapping each bet (sema-only verification, query invalidation, per-module fan-out, monomorphization control, one TIR with two lenses, performance-role budget) to its `Compiler/` mechanism, owner card, enforcement test and remaining gap.

cards.title: Bootstrap validation harness — differential proof vs the Rust-hosted compiler
cards.body: Self-hosting needs one reusable behavioral comparator for any reference and candidate compiler binary. It runs the same public cases through both and reports the first observable semantic divergence. Card #218 separately owns byte-identical stage1/stage2 compiler artifacts; this card does not conflate behavior with binary identity.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Build one reusable two-binary behavioral comparator. It runs the same existing public corpus through a pinned reference and a candidate compiler and reports the first observable divergence. This is how the self-hosted compiler proves it behaves like the Rust-hosted one. It makes no byte-identity claim; that is #815/#218.

## Owner gate
Criterion 1 requires the owner to reopen #217 before work starts. Triage question: does the 2026-09-28 self-hosted-primary direction supersede that gate? Recommended **A**: yes, start now. This plan is written for A; #217 is then not a prerequisite. The retired #669 never is.

## Current state
- `Compiler/Bootstrap/{Runner.rs,Tests.rs,check.sh,BuildIdentity.rs,assemble.mjs}`. `check.sh:17-43` assembles the Compiler unit and runs `jet check` with a receipt. `Runner.rs:1-30` orchestrates the factory tiers (Aot, CraneliftJit, SourceInterpreterDeopt). None of these compares two binaries.
- `Tools/agent/` has no comparator (`compiler-proof.mjs` is the Lean proof replay). `Tools/agent/verify-full.sh` exists.
- Reusable corpora:
  - `Examples/**` with goldens under `Examples/features/expected/` (`tests/golden`);
  - UI fixtures `tests/ui/*.jet` (diagnostic snapshots);
  - `tests/dev_parts/corpus.rs` (the dev/tier corpus, replacing `tests/jit_gaps.txt`).
- Old plan paths: `scripts/agent/` → `Tools/agent/`.

## Changes
1. `Tools/agent/compiler-diff.mjs`: a non-product runner taking `--reference <jet>`, `--candidate <jet>` and `--corpus golden|ui|dev|all`. It enumerates cases from the existing loaders' manifests (golden list, `tests/ui` directory, `tests/dev_parts/corpus.rs` table) rather than keeping its own list. It fixes deterministic project roots under `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/compiler-diff/<case>`, `LC_ALL=C`, a scrubbed environment, and timeout and memory limits (criterion 2).
2. For each case, run `check`, `run`, `run --interpret` and `build` on both binaries. Compare exit status, diagnostic codes and spans, stdout, stderr, panic/ICE classification, and declared side-effect files. Stop at the first divergence and print case, phase, span, expected, candidate and a bounded repro directory, with secrets and home paths redacted (criteria 3, 6).
3. Missing candidate or unavailable tool → exit 2 `unavailable`, never "match" (criterion 6).
4. `--canary` mode: a checked fixture pair under `tests/compiler-diff/` whose controlled input differs by construction, for example a UI case whose expected snapshot is fed as the candidate output. It proves detection with no manual source edits (criterion 4).
5. `Tools/agent/verify-full.sh`: run it as an opt-in stage only when `JET_CANDIDATE_COMPILER` is set (criterion 5). Stage identity and hashing stay on #815.

## Proof
See the added criterion. Also a real reference-versus-candidate run with the self-hosted build as candidate, whose first-divergence report is attached to the card.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver. A self-host harness.

## Dependencies
Owner answer on criterion 1 (recommended A). #217 is listed as stale under A.

That breaks criterion 6 (never treat an unavailable compiler as a behavioral match): the comparator checks the binaries only at startup. cards.title: Jet-in-Jet front-end milestone 1: lexer port + C-ABI link-in
cards.body: First concrete port milestone after owner-frozen #217 reopens and the architecture/behavioral prerequisites land. Port the current lexer contract to Jet, add one narrow internal integration ABI to the Rust driver, prove exact token/span/diagnostic parity, then replace the Rust path. This ABI is new internal bootstrap machinery, not a ratified user FFI surface or public compatibility promise. Driver orchestration owns query caching and module fan-out; the lexer stays one sequential implementation.
cards.plan:
## Goal
First Jet-in-Jet front-end milestone: port the public lexer contract to Jet, add the smallest internal C ABI for the Rust driver, prove token/span/diagnostic parity, then make the Jet path authoritative.

## Law
- Exact port of current public lexer contract (`lex`, `lex_raw`, TokKind/Token/StrTokPart, byte spans, interpolation, nested comments, terminator insertion, recovery, Jet-owned diagnostics).
- Use existing Syntax constants — no second keyword table (I7).
- ABI is internal only: owned buffers, token/diagnostic serialization, panic containment, alloc/free ownership, version lock; no user-facing export.
- One selectable comparison seam until parity; then Jet path authoritative with no facade.
- Driver owns jet-queries and fan-out; no lexer-local parallelism invention.

## Scope
In: Jet lexer sources; internal ABI; differential corpus + seeded fuzz vs Rust lexer; cutover.
Out: parser/sema ports (#809/#810); umbrella inventory (#218) except consuming its seam list.

## Owned paths
- new Jet lexer tree (location TBD under self-host layout from #218 inventory)
- `crates/jet-lexer` comparison seam / ABI bridge
- `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs` (consume, do not fork)
- fuzz/differential harnesses
- diagnostics remain I4-compliant (no new user codes unless behavior differs — should not)

## Steps
1. Gates: #217 reopened; #669 and #670 complete.
2. Port lexer to Jet against Syntax constants.
3. Specify and implement minimal internal C ABI; contain panics; lock versions.
4. Selectable seam: Rust vs Jet lexer; corpus + seeded fuzz differentials.
5. On parity, switch driver to Jet path; remove facade.
6. File only concrete next-port gaps; independent review.

## Acceptance / proof
Criteria: byte-identical kinds/payloads/spans/terminators/order vs Rust on corpus; fuzz clean; cutover done.

## Blockers
blockedBy: #217, #669, #670. #218 informs seams but is not a cycle dependency.

questions.text:
1) Since we have the "build" method that lets us run code at build time, is there still a reason to keep comptime? What is the boundary & what is the value? 
2) I'm not entirely clear on what this question means. What are the real tradeoffs, where would people get the most value regardless of safety, how can we mitigate issues with safety? It's up to us to do more work on the backend to give the best end result and experience for the user
questions.answer:
Q1 — comptime vs fn build: the boundary and the value.

Keep both. The docs make them different tools. comptime (S26, D-CTEFFECT1) is pure value evaluation. A fuel-limited sema interpreter runs type-checked Core code and lowers the result to constant data. It has no authority and can never create or select a type (S26). Its only external reads are Tier-1 locked operations — `embed_file`, `embed_bytes`, `find`, `fetch(url, sha256:)` — each recorded in `.jet/lock`. Tier-2 ambient reads need `#Impure` plus `--allow-impure`. comptime values feed constants, marker values, and module fields.

`fn build(b: BuildContext)` (D-BUILDENTRY1, D-BUILDACTION1) is a build-time action runner. It registers targets (`b.add_executable`, `b.add_library`), declares cached capability-gated actions (`b.action(name, inputs, outputs, run, caps)`), selects toolchains, and runs processes. It emits artifacts and generated source under `.jet/generated/`, with input and output hashes in the lock. Tier 1 is pure+locked by default; Tier 2 needs `#Impure` plus explicit permission plus provenance.

Why both exist: comptime is a calculator over declared values, available in every expression position with no ceremony. `fn build` is an authorized effect runner, invoked only by `jet build` and gated by granted capabilities. Merging them breaks safe-by-default (I1). Either every constant expression gains filesystem and process authority, or every build action loses its capability gate. A beginner would need a `BuildContext` just to write `label: "ledger " + release`.

Examples:
- comptime: `comptime release = "1.4.0"` then `label: "ledger " + release`. Pure, no lock entry.
- build: `b.action("gen-proto", inputs, outputs, run: protoc, caps: [.exec])`. Runs `protoc`, records provenance, emits generated source.
- comptime moving to build: `banner: embed_file("./banner.txt")` is a Tier-1 locked comptime read. Producing that banner by running `git describe` is a process effect, so it moves to a capability-gated `fn build` action. The ballot's own option-C error says the same for ambient reads: `env_var("TOKEN")` is Tier-2 and must move to an authorized `fn build` action.

Q2 — what the ballot decides and the real tradeoffs.

Plain restatement: this ballot decides whether one module field may reference another field in the same module, and whether a field may directly read a hash-locked external input such as an embedded file or pinned fetch.

Option A, pure dependency graph. A field can name a sibling. Cycles fail before any plan runs and print the full chain. A field cannot spell a Tier-1 read inline.

    module env.dev {
      label: "ledger " + release
      prompt: label + " > "
    }

Option B, independent fields. A field cannot name a sibling. Any shared value lifts to a top-level `comptime` binding. No graph, most ceremony for reuse.

Option C, graph plus locked reads. Everything in A, and a field may spell a Tier-1 read inline. The input is recorded in `.jet/lock` and reproduced offline.

    module env.dev {
      banner: embed_file("./banner.txt")
      prompt: banner + " > "
    }

Where users get the most value. Shared computed values across fields is the common case; A and C both cover it, B does not. Embedding a file or a version string is the next case. C spells it inside a field. A reaches the same value through a top-level comptime binding, which is already law (D-CTIO1):

    comptime banner = embed_file("./banner.txt")
    module env.dev {
      banner: banner
      prompt: banner + " > "
    }

The only delta between A and C is one binding line and where the read is written.

Safety, honestly. C is not unsafe. Tier-1 reads are hash-pinned, recorded in `.jet/lock`, and fail closed under `--locked` and offline. The safety story is fully engineerable, and effort is never a deterrent in this project. C does not lose on safety and must not be rejected for costing more backend work.

The real argument for A over C is I8, one way to mean it. External input already has one home: top-level `comptime` bindings and the `fn build` input surface. C adds a second home — every module field — where a locked read may appear. Provenance review then scans every field instead of one binding list. That is a legibility cost the reviewer pays on every module, not a safety cost.

Which option the analysis supports: A. The one concrete reason: a field under A can already reference a top-level `comptime banner = embed_file(...)` binding, so C buys one line of convenience while scattering external-input provenance across every field, which I8 rules against. If inline field reads later prove real value beyond that one line, C reopens on its own merits, not on a safety argument.

cards.title: Typed project compile-latency budgets
cards.body: The compiler-speed corpus in #666 protects Jet's own latency. Decide whether application teams may also make cold, no-change, and representative-edit compile latency enforceable product facts through #241's existing typed budget system. Any chosen surface must stay opt-in, preserve zero-ceremony defaults, record exact cache and environment identity, and use the shared evaluator/report/baseline path.
cards.plan: Add a compile-latency measurement family to the ratified budget system (D-PERFBUDGET-COMPILE1=C on this card; umbrella law at syntax-decisions.md:4836 — typed module perf.<role> declarations, pinned baselines, one BudgetReport, jet budget check / plan-first update). Extend the closed budget grammar in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/BudgetSpecs.rs:6 with the compile-latency metric; register and execute a CompileLatency provider beside CompilerFacts in Source/BudgetProviders.rs:137, following the command-owned evidence path BenchMeasurement/AllocationProbe use (Source/CmdBudget.rs:314/:543); integrate workload capture, evidence, and unit in Source/CmdBudget.rs:301/:628. The workload is a deterministic in-repo fixture project compiled with the resident toolchain; samples are wall-clock with the pinned statistical baseline the umbrella prescribes. Non-goals: no CI wiring (E10), no new report format.

log.text: BLOCKED on #2074 (c09otnjg), measured 2026-08-19. The proof cannot fit any 900s suite guard: the ratified policy pins 1 warmup + 20 samples per workload and the test runs two measuring commands, so 128 child jet builds at ~34s each is ~72 min. The 2026-08-17 '102s' log was a FAILED run that died at Clean sample 0 after 3 front-end passes (102.7/3 = ~34s per pass), so nothing regressed. Root cause of the 34s tax is #2074: the Core/CoreLib closure (~1.54MB) is emitted outside the CACHED_RUNTIME markers (Codegen/mod.rs:4267 vs :4269), so every child compile re-feeds it to rustc. Timing-artifact root cause from the earlier lane IS fixed (Driver laps PhaseTiming + JET_TIMING_DIR). cards.body:

Close only from existing child-card evidence. Do not absorb child implementation scope.
Amended 2026-07-24 after D-ONECORE1=A and D-LENS-RUN2=A: parity is delivered structurally by the sidequest chain #776 (semantic-core TIR) -> #777 (canonical interpreter) -> #778 (tiered jet run) -> #779 (core shrink), not by hand-writing every Cranelift gap.
1. Keep the #727 differential corpus gate green (criterion 1, verified) — it is the safety net for the whole rework.
2. The E2211 burn-down steps of the old plan are superseded; tier-1 widening continues later as perf work on the new structured TIR.
3. This card closes when #778 lands: every AOT-runnable corpus program runs under default jet run with byte-identical output via tiered execution, and the CI gate (#730) enforces it.
4. Shared SoT rule stands: host shims call jet-foundation / existing runtime; never a third algorithm copy.

log.text: Independent closeout at 1735d0e5b by e3-batch-review (Codex GPT-5, high effort): reviewed e0b2e00ed..1735d0e5b with no findings. Criterion 6 verified: one shared StructuralDebug source supplies AOT and tier-0 record/Map/Union token assembly, and exact cross-tier regression bytes pass. Targeted proof: auto_derive_policy 5/5; Prelude ownership/hash 1/1; foundation traits 1/1; foundation+codegen checks; diff check. No broad suite.

Structural debug parity fix committed as 1735d0e5b. AOT and tier-0 now consume one shared formatter source; runtime adapters only render child values. Exact Map and Union bytes now match across AOT, default run, and forced interpreter, while existing local and imported record output remains unchanged. Criterion 6 is met and ready for independent verification.

Reopened from new #1267 proof: synthesized auto-derived Map/Union debug values are observably different across AOT and default run. AOT uses Prelude JetDebug; tier-0 uses CtValue debug_rust, producing map braces and user_Int wrappers. #1267 proof remains red until both lenses share one canonical formatter seam.
Independent closeout completed. Criteria 3 and 5 verified from completed blocker evidence and a fresh Unicode default-run/AOT/golden smoke. All five criteria are verified; #688 is done.

Fresh #1307 review found a latent parity gap outside its original red set: typed Codable succeeds resident but a surrounding function deopt can bypass generated codec bodies. Tracked as #1310 and required before this closeout.

verify finding (2026-07-28): closeout must not proceed. Full-corpus audit shows 23 examples violating the 'done means' law (AOT-green, default-run red), incl. ui/events E0956 committed as acceptable in tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt deopt_interp class. Evidence: docs/audits/jit-run-tier-vs-aot-parity-audit-2026-07-28.md; burndown owned by #1254 (owner verdict D-VERDICT-1254-1 recorded there).

CORRECTION to my earlier verification of criterion 2, and #688 cannot close yet.

I verified criterion 2 on the tripwire and the named deopt reasons. Both of those hold. I did not test the rest of the criterion text, the clause requiring deopt to produce identical observable behavior. That clause fails.

Measured at c485d5f17 with a fresh build. examples/features/crypto/crypto_suite.jet exits 0 under jet run --release and exits 1 under default jet run. examples/features/types/generic_constructor_inference.jet does the same; AOT prints '7 jet 2 9' and JIT prints an error. Both are byte-different, which is the exact condition this card exists to eliminate.

Mechanism: --trace-tiers confirms the deopt happens as designed ('run tier0 interp (body stmt 6: Let[0] init=OtherExpr)'). The problem is the target. Tier-0 is the comptime evaluator, and its own E0956 text says it evaluates a pure subset of Jet. So the deopt target cannot run what Cranelift could not compile.

This means the compile-gap ratchet drift the JIT worker reported is not manifest bookkeeping. Each entry is a real lens violation. Growing tests/jit_gaps.txt to absorb them would have recorded two parity failures as normal, so the worker was right to stop and ask.

Carded as #1254 and this card now blocks on it. Criteria 2 and 3 must be re-proved after #1254 lands. The JIT worker's tier-1 additions at c485d5f17 are correct and stay: sha512_bytes and blake3_bytes now compile resident and match AOT byte for byte.

STOP AND REPORT on the gap ratchet, as instructed. The gap set cannot return to zero inside this card, and I did not grow tests/jit_gaps.txt. Fresh JET_DUMP_JIT_GAPS=1 jit_coverage_audit at c485d5f17 shows covered 371 against a manifest of 370, and two gaps against a manifest of none. Gap one: 'crypto/crypto_suite: run: jit core call unsupported: jet.crypto.hkdf_sha256'. Behind it sit at least constant_time_equal, constant_time_equal_bytes, x25519_shared and file_seal, plus the Secret.from_bytes, X25519SecretKey.new_random, public_key and text method calls, none of which the JIT host table carries. Gap two: 'types/generic_constructor_inference: run: jit string interp type unsupported: Named("T")'. That one needs the lowerer to resolve a generic field type through monomorphisation before it can print it, which no host shim can supply. Gap two alone puts a zero gap set out of reach whatever I do to crypto. All three movements come from other workers' frontend fixes landing today and admitting three previously rejected examples into the compile attempt: crypto_suite from #1210, plus generic_constructor_inference and generic_modules. Criterion #3 assigns Cranelift completeness to the #778 ratchet and excludes it here. Card #771's example is not landed: its precondition, an empty gap set, is unmet, and it would add a third gap.

JIT hash coverage landed at c485d5f17: jet.crypto.sha512_bytes and jet.crypto.blake3_bytes now compile. A core call needs an entry in two tables, and both were missing: crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs picks the Cranelift host function, and crates/jet-jit/src/jit/safety.rs decides whether the function stays resident. With only the lowering entry the planner still deopted the whole program before lowering ran, and tier-0 then refused the call with E0956. Both host shims reuse the shared jet_crypto_sha512_impl and jet_crypto_blake3_impl that the AOT bridge uses, so there is no second algorithm copy. A program printing both digests now reports 'run tier1 native' and matches jet run --release byte for byte. Three-way differential stays green for crypto/hash and crypto/typed_crypto. The gap ratchet is still red for two reasons that belong to other work; details in the next log.

cards.title: Exclusive range spelling for index loops
cards.body:
Persona audit (Klaus): `..` is inclusive (S22, ratified, stays), so `0..1000` makes 1001 items and the common `0..len()` index loop panics at run time. The examples show no exclusive spelling.

Ballot D-RANGE-EXCL1 on this card decides: add an exclusive spelling, bless Jet-native idioms (sequence two-binding + `indexes`, pipeline `indexed`), or both. S22 inclusive-by-default is not reopened. Rec C would also amend D-ITER1 `enumerate` → `indexed`.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-RANGE-EXCL1=C as one extension of the existing loop-range and collection-iteration paths. Add a registered ..< token and carry an inclusive/exclusive end mode through the loop AST, formatter, sema, TIR, native emitter, web/dev emitter, and semantic tokens; keep .. inclusive and keep the existing semicolon stride contract. Extend list and fixed-list source loops so two bindings receive index then item, while one binding remains item-only. Add the indexes sequence member through the existing builtin-member path and emit valid Int indexes only. In sema, recognize only the provable same-root shape where an inclusive loop ends at xs.len() and its body indexes xs; report a registered teaching diagnostic with the three ratified fixes and avoid heuristic lookalikes. Rename the public D-ITER1 adapter enumerate() to indexed() across sema, TIR, codegen, docs, examples, and tests, preserving the named tuple contract. Update the syntax decision log and examples, regenerate grammars, bless diagnostics, and run focused parser/formatter/UI/golden plus native/web/dev parity checks.

cards.title: MCP SDK: protocol types, negotiation, and lifecycle
cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#768:0] Split from the former #768 umbrella. This card owns only “MCP SDK: protocol types, negotiation, and lifecycle.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #768. The other 8 delivery slices have separate cards.
cards.plan:
## Goal

Ship the first MCP SDK slice: protocol values, revision negotiation, codecs, lifecycle, and audit facts over one canonical core. Typed beginner builders and expert policy use the same mechanism.

## Law and scope

Apply `D-MCP-SURFACE1=A`. Stable `2025-11-25` is the default session profile; preview `2026-07-28` requires explicit policy and its own codec. Keep this slice dependency-free and protocol-only. Client convenience (#1061), server tools/resources/prompts (#1062), stdio (#1063), HTTP (#1064), OAuth (#1065), schema/reflection (#1066), interop (#1067), and hostile proof (#1068) remain sibling work.

## Owned paths

- `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/MCP.rs`: canonical protocol values, codecs, policy, negotiation, lifecycle, limits, and redacted audit facts
- `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/lib.rs` and `crates/jetpack/src/lib.rs`: the existing module and re-export seams
- the focused MCP unit tests in `MCP.rs`, with an integration test only if the public re-export needs coverage
- `docs/spec/reference/core-library.md`, `docs/spec/architecture.md`, `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md`, and `docs/spec/diagnostics.md` only for durable protocol or diagnostic wording

## Work

1. Reconcile the existing `jet_pkg_model::MCP` implementation with the ratified revision registry and keep one source of truth; do not create a parallel `core.mcp` module.
2. Preserve typed message values, per-revision codecs, stable/preview policy, downgrade refusal, lifecycle transitions, and the configured message/depth/capability bounds without transport or authorization code.
3. Emit only the version, lifecycle, limits, and redacted audit facts owned by this slice; do not claim tool, resource, prompt, transport, OAuth, schema, or cancellation behavior.
4. Update the existing exports and durable references only where the current implementation requires it, then exercise incompatible-peer, preview-opt-in, malformed/deep/oversized-message, invalid-limit, and invalid-transition cases.

## Cutover and proof

Run focused protocol/negotiation/lifecycle checks through the real package exports. A transport or sibling feature must not supply the evidence. Full-suite proof belongs to Epoch 11 closeout.

cards.title: Agent executor: authority and resource policy model
cards.body:
Single-task slice extracted from former #770 umbrella. This card owns only: Agent executor: authority and resource policy model. Sibling scope lives on separate successor cards.

Context only; it does not add sibling scope:
Give Jet programs and AI agents one safe way to execute untrusted commands. The beginner default grants only declared workspace reads/writes and no network or secrets. Experts can grant exact capabilities and receive a complete plan and receipt. This is the application-facing consumer of #398's native Linux/macOS/Windows isolation boundary, not a second sandbox engine. It extends the shipped #291 core.process model instead of adding a shell DSL or parallel process API.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship D-AGENT-EXEC1=A: one `Authority` model on `core.process` with safe workspace defaults, exact expert grants, dry-run plans, and redacted receipts. Application-facing consumer of #398/#893 native isolation — not a second sandbox.

cards.plan:
Complete only this slice; do not absorb sibling scope. Preserve these parent constraints where they apply:
D-PROCESS-SESSION1 must choose the public extension to ProcessSpec and ProcessChild. Keep non-interactive argv execution as the safe default. questions.answer:
"Facts" here means the host capability report from `plan.capabilities()` — answers about what this machine can do (terminal present? resize? raw mode?), not settings you choose.

cards.title: Proposal: checked transaction regions (rollback on failure)
cards.body: PARKED design proposal, not active work. Do NOT ballot yet (owner instruction 2026-07-24). Idea mined from Verse's decides effect + Logan Smith video series: an explicit expert-only region where a failure undoes every state change the region made, so code reads as the happy path only. Jet's current disposition is 'watch'; ordinary ? never implies rollback. Full proposal, constraints, invariant check, and open owner questions in the ref doc. Next step IF owner wants it: ballot for scope/syntax/effect-model fit + a spike on the ^T take case.
cards.plan:
## Outcome
A committed, upgraded proposal doc at docs/proposals/transactional-rollback-regions.md records the full checked transaction-region design — rollback semantics, effect interaction, spelling candidates, and explicitly rejected alternatives — and an owner ballot slate is DRAFTED from it on this card (`decision add --draft`, never promoted to decide). No implementation, no parser/sema/runtime work. This satisfies criterion 1 exactly: doc + drafted slate, nothing built.

## Law
- Ratified rule this design must not touch: ordinary `?` propagation never implies rollback (docs/archive/language-lessons-and-regrets.md:399-407 "watch" disposition; restated in the proposal doc:30-34).
- D-CONC-STM1=A keeps `#Transact` (card #1505; Syntax.rs concurrency block) — the STM/transaction word already exists; the slate must reconcile with it, not mint a competing concept blindly.
- D-STRUCT-POLICY1=A (ratified 2026-08-19, card #2052): user-authored `#Policy` settings exist as a mechanism; "rollback as a policy setting" must be weighed as an alternative (adopt or reject with reasons).
- D-CONC-FREEZE1=A, D-MEM1 (`&` exclusive write), I3 (rollback-safety is a sema proof), I8 (one mechanism per concept).
- Owner instruction 2026-07-24 "Do NOT ballot yet" still governs the decide lane: ballots are drafted (`--draft`), not opened for ratification. The 2026-08-19 criterion rewrite asks for a drafted slate, which is compatible.

## Work
1. Read the current draft end-to-end: docs/proposals/transactional-rollback-regions.md (all 140 lines) and docs/research/2026-07-24-verse-video-mining.md (the `decides` sections only). The doc already has: idea, Verse source, constraints, invariant check, open questions 1-5, prior art, recommendation.
2. Upgrade the doc to criterion-1 shape. Add/complete three sections:
   - **Rollback semantics**: what is journaled (memory writes to bindings/containers reachable from the region), failure classes (typed `? E` failure vs panic — panic never rolls back per D-NOPANIC1=D), nesting, task interaction (a region may not cross a `task` boundary; cite D-CONC-FREEZE1), and the `^T` take case (open question 2) worked as a written design sketch — what happens when a region moves a value out and then fails. This is a paper spike, not code.
   - **Effect interaction**: memory-only rollback vs compensation contracts for FS/DB/Net; how a region's effect row is spelled (does the region demand an effect ceiling `=[...]=>`); relation to `#Transact` (D-CONC-STM1) — either the region IS the `#Transact` surface generalized, or the doc says why they stay separate (I8 pressure is the deciding test).
   - **Spelling candidates**: at least three, each with a code sample: (a) marker block `#Transact { … }` reusing the ratified word, (b) a keyword region, (c) a `#Policy(transactional)` setting per D-STRUCT-POLICY1=A. Name a recommended spelling.
   - **Rejected alternatives** (required verbatim by criterion 1): implicit rollback on `?` (breaks the ratified rule), Verse-style `decides` effect on functions (rollback becomes invisible at call sites — violates Jet's one-visible-marker failure law), library-only STM with closures (loses the sema proof, I3), automatic FS/DB compensation (unbounded contract surface). Each with one-line reason.
3. Draft the ballot slate on this card, one ballot per open owner question the doc's own recommendation names (proposal:99-101): scope of automatic rollback (memory-only vs compensations), spelling, and effect-model fit. Suggested IDs: D-TXN-SCOPE1, D-TXN-SPELL1, D-TXN-EFFECT1. Use `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs decision add '#775' --draft --file <payload.json> --by <You>` — draft mode skips full-ballot validation and keeps the owner's "do not ballot yet" standing. Each draft still carries options + rec so it is ballot-ready the day the owner unfreezes.
4. Commit the doc (and the tracked board files: `git add plugins/tower/.tower/*.json docs/proposals/transactional-rollback-regions.md && git commit` — the board is tracked; uncommitted mints die in resets).
5. Meet criterion 1 with evidence: doc path + commit hash + the three draft decision IDs. Log the drafted-not-balloted distinction on the card.

## Not building
- No parser, sema, TIR, or runtime work of any kind (criterion 1 forbids implementation on this card).
- No promotion of drafts to the decide lane; no `decision update --ready`; no ratification.
- No change to `?`/`??` semantics or docs describing them.
- No new Tower cards; implementation cards are minted only after the owner ratifies, on a future pass.

## Proof
- `node plugins/tower/tower.mjs card show '#775' --json | jq '.decisions[].id,.decisions[].draft'` shows the three slate entries with `draft: true`.
- `git show --stat HEAD` shows the proposal doc committed with the new sections; quote the section headers in criterion evidence.
- Criterion 1 marked met via `card criteria '#775' --meet 1 --evidence "…" --by <You>`.
- No runtime behavior changes → no `jet run`/`--release` parity proof required. `tower lint` note: draft ballots trip the stale-draft sweeper after a while; record in the card log that drafts are intentionally parked pending owner unfreeze.

## blockedBy
none — pure documentation + draft-ballot work; the 2026-07-24 "do not ballot" instruction is honored by using `--draft`, and the card is unfrozen (owner log 2026-08-10).

It states the scope question, the spelling question, and the effect-model question as three named ballots — D-TXN-SCOPE1, D-TXN-SPELL1, D-TXN-EFFECT1 — plus a paper spike for the ^T case, and records the prior art it draws on (Verse failure contexts, Haskell STM, database transactions, RAII scope guards). cards.title: One canonical interpreter over the semantic TIR core
cards.body:
Today Jet has three separate answers to "what does this program do": the AOT Rust emitter, the Cranelift JIT lowering, and the comptime tree-walker that also serves jet dev --interpret and the REPL. Each has its own coverage holes and its own bug surface.

This card builds one interpreter that walks the semantic TIR core from #776 and makes it the reference for runtime behavior. Comptime, the REPL, jet dev --interpret, and the deopt tier of jet run (card below) all execute through it. The AST tree-walker in jet-comptime retires for those roles.

Payoff: a new feature is executable the day its TIR lowering lands, because the interpreter's exhaustive match forces coverage at compile time of the compiler itself. The comptime-parity work on cards #392/#721/#722/#723 feeds this directly; their builtin inventory becomes the interpreter's host surface.
cards.plan:
1. Build a TIR evaluator (values, places, calls, control flow) with an exhaustive, wildcard-free match over executable TIR — a new variant fails the compiler build until the interpreter handles it.
2. Port the comptime builtin/host surface (the inventory from card #721) onto it.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Deterministic self-hosting. The stage1 Jet compiler, built by the pinned stage0, produces stage2 compiler artifacts that are byte-identical to stage1's under the same declared inputs. This card owns artifact identity; behavioral differential proof belongs to #218.

## Current state
- Stage identity lives in `Compiler/Bootstrap/BuildIdentity.rs` and `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet`. Assembly is `Compiler/Bootstrap/assemble.mjs` (one ordered unit from `sources.list`). The runner is `Compiler/Bootstrap/Runner.rs`.
- The stage0-to-stage1 slice (#814) is done and folded into #218. Its receipt (pinned stage0 binary, toolchain, target, profile, source and dependency digests) is the input here. No route builds stage1 yet: the Jet compiler does not execute (#218 log 2026-09-28).
- The old plan traced `Source/lib.rs`, `crates/jet-driver` and `crates/jet-codegen` TIR, which are now archived. Retargeted criterion 7 replaces the `Source/lib.rs` bypass check.

## Changes
1. `Compiler/Bootstrap/BuildIdentity.rs` and `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet`: identity covers target, profile, toolchain (rustc and linker), source digests, dependency digests and the stage number. Timestamps, absolute host paths, hash-map iteration order, environment variables and temp names never enter emitted artifacts. Sort every emitted collection by stable key and normalize paths relative to the source root.
2. `Compiler/Bootstrap/Runner.rs`: add a two-build mode. Build stage2 with stage1 in an isolated scratch root under `~/.cache/jet-luna/compiler-bootstrap/`, then compare the compiler image and declared companion artifacts byte for byte.
3. Failure cases: changed source, malformed source, resource-limit hit, ABI mismatch or stage mismatch each fail reproducibly. None falls back to stage0 or publishes a mixed-stage artifact.
4. Add `tests/selfhost_fixpoint.rs` with the success test plus bypass and changed-source failure tests. Update only the self-hosting proof notes in `Docs/spec/architecture.md`.

## Proof
- The added criterion.
- `cargo test --test selfhost_fixpoint -- changed_source_fails_without_stage0_fallback` passes.

cards.title: core.game ECS: storage, queries, and schedule
cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#238:1] Split from the former #238 umbrella. This card owns only “core.game ECS: storage, queries, and schedule.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #238. The other 6 delivery slices have separate cards.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement the core.game ECS in Jet under D-GAME-ECS1=B (struct-marker components): typed component storage, deterministic entity identity, deterministic queries, and an ordered frame schedule that rejects conflicting mutation before any state changes.

## Current state
- There is no ECS. Game.rs pushes component type names into a `Vec<String>` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Game.rs:371-376), and `jet_game_scene_query` returns one synthetic entity row of default-initialized Int fields (:378-400).
- Examples/features/game/core_game_headless.jet:20-24 prints that synthetic row (`query {hits.len()}`, `row {hits[0]}`).
- Core/game/game.jet has no entity, component or query types.
- Ratified spelling (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:3698-3699; D-GAME-ECS1=B): `struct Velocity {...}` plus `scene.component<Velocity>()` and `scene.query<Position, Velocity>()`.
- No decision covers entity creation or removal, or how systems are ordered.

## Changes
1. Ballot first (this is why the phase is deciding): draft D-GAME-ENTITY1 with same-program alternatives. Recommended: `e :: scene.spawn(Position{x: 0}, Velocity{dx: 1})`, `scene.despawn(e)`, `&scene.insert(e, value)`, `Entity{index, generation}` with generation-checked reuse, and systems as `scene.on_frame` callbacks run in registration order.
2. Core/game/game.jet: per-type columnar component storage keyed by the component's struct identity, and an entity table with generations. `query<T...>()` returns rows in ascending entity index. A handle to a despawned entity is a typed error, never a stale row. A query naming an unregistered component, or an unsupported backend, fails before state mutation. A frame that both mutates and iterates the same component is rejected before that frame applies.
3. Delete the synthetic Game.rs component list and query rows. Route `scene.component` and `scene.query` to the Jet source (Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Game.jet), and regenerate with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`.
4. New Examples/features/game/game_ecs.jet with its .out: spawn, query order, despawn and reuse with a stale-handle error, a missing component, a conflicting mutation, and schedule order. Update core_game_headless.jet and its .out to print real rows.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=game/game_ecs cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=game/core_game_headless cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/game/game_ecs.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/game/game_ecs.out` prints nothing.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: Core/game with its game goldens.

## Dependencies
The D-GAME-ENTITY1 ballot. #238 (assets) is not a prerequisite.

cards.title: core.game input actions, fixed-step clock, deterministic replay and rollback
cards.body:
[R-POSTE3-1:#238:3] Split from the former #238 umbrella. This card owns only “core.game deterministic replay and rollback.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #238. The other 6 delivery slices have separate cards.

Absorbed #821 (c0jh3z59, "input actions and fixed-step clock") 2026-08-19: input/clock is only observable through replay determinism; D-GAME-INPUT1=A and D-GAME-REPLAY1=A ratified together; identical owned paths (Game.rs, game_checks.rs, core_game_headless.jet), byte-identical criteria, consecutive chain links.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-GAME-INPUT1=A and D-GAME-REPLAY1=A in Jet: scene input bindings with per-frame snapshots, a fixed-step clock, a `game.Replay` record/play contract that detects divergence, and rollback. Identical input logs must give identical tick sequences on every tier.

## Current state
- Core/game/game.jet:25-27 and :40-42 provide `Replay{path}` and `Replay.record`, and nothing else.
- The tape lives in the host: the Foundation replay tape (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Game.rs:169-171, :274-280, :523-537). It panics on an invalid replay (`panic!("invalid game replay ...")` at :276), and budget and frame validation also panic (:311, :549, :555).
- There is no rollback symbol.
- Ratified spellings (D-GAME-INPUT1=A, D-GAME-REPLAY1=A): `scene.input.bind(.jump, keys: [.space])`, `frame.input.pressed(.jump)`, `game.run(scene, replay: game.Replay.record("run.jreplay"))` and `game.Replay.play("run.jreplay", scene)?`. The artifact holds input actions, seeds, fixed-step timing, backend identity and budget events.
- Examples/features/game/core_game_headless.jet:19 still uses the unratified string form `scene.input.bind("jump", "Space")`.

## Changes
1. Core/game/game.jet: typed action bindings, per-frame input snapshots, a fixed-step clock (tick index, dt from the fixed rate), and the `.jreplay` record and play in Jet over the host's byte IO. Play compares each tick's recorded state hash and returns a typed divergence error, never absorbing it. A corrupt or truncated replay and an input disconnect mid-recording return typed errors. Remove the panics at Game.rs:276/:311/:549/:555 from these paths.
2. Rollback has no ratified name. Draft D-GAME-ROLLBACK1 with same-program alternatives (recommended: `scene.restore(tick)` over retained snapshots). Only this slice waits for it.
3. Migrate core_game_headless.jet to the ratified `bind(.jump, keys: [.space])` form and update its .out.
4. Route through Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Game.jet and Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet:1095-1099. The host keeps file IO only.
5. New Examples/features/game/game_replay.jet with its .out: record, play to a bit-identical final state, injected divergence detected, a corrupt file, a disconnect, and rollback plus re-simulation matching the original run.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=game/game_replay cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=game/core_game_headless cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/game/game_replay.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/game/game_replay.out` prints nothing (I9 across interpreter, default and AOT).

## Batch
batch-core-ui: Core/game and its goldens.

## Dependencies
The D-GAME-ROLLBACK1 ballot, for the rollback slice only.

cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#238:4] Split from the former #238 umbrella. This card owns only “core.game editor hooks and performance budgets.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #238. The other 6 delivery slices have separate cards.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Move the core.game editor hooks (play/simulate/pause/step transitions and paused inspection) and the scene performance budgets (D-GAME-BUDGET1=A as superseded by D-PERFBUDGET-GAMEMIGRATE1's typed `perf` roles) into Jet semantics, with the host keeping only the devtools transport and the probe leaves.

## Current state
- Editor transitions and sessions are Rust: `GameDevRunMode`, `GameDevPhase` and `GameDevTransition` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/GameDevProtocol.rs:55-150), the control decoding (:1339-1470) and the profile ring (:960).
- Budgets are measured in Game.rs through one SceneProbe (:616-624, :720-722, emitting `JETSCENE1` rows for DrawCalls, SceneAssetBytes and MemoryHighWater), with the metric enum at crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/GameOverlay.rs:183-215.
- Budgets are declared as typed perf roles in Examples/features/game/core_game_headless.jet:3-5 (`module perf.game { budgets: [Budget]{...} }`). The superseding note is at Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:3702-3703.
- The replay artifact carries budget events (D-GAME-REPLAY1=A), so this slice builds on #822's replay contract.

## Changes
1. Core/game: the editor phase machine (Editing, Playing, Simulating, Paused), the transition legality rules, and a deterministic step, as Jet code. The host GameDevProtocol.rs keeps only transport: decoding control frames and forwarding the session envelope.
2. Core/game: budget evaluation. Scene probe samples, which stay host leaves, are compared against the declared `perf.game` budgets. An overrun emits a typed budget event into the frame transcript and the replay, and does not panic (Game.rs:549 and :555 currently panic).
3. Sema and codegen route through Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Game.jet and Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet. Regenerate with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`.
4. New Examples/features/game/game_editor_budgets.jet with its .out: a headless play, pause, step and resume sequence with deterministic frame indices; a rejected illegal transition; a budget overrun event; and device loss on the headless backend degrading visibly.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=game/game_editor_budgets cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/game/game_editor_budgets.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/game/game_editor_budgets.out` prints nothing.
- The existing `cargo test --test cli_scene_probe` still passes, because the SceneProbe transport is unchanged.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: Core/game plus the game goldens.

## Dependencies
#822 (the replay and input contract that budget events and the step clock use).
